11.s: kalādhvā vakṣyate śrīmacchāṃbhavājñānusārataḥ // 1
11.d: कलाध्वा वक्ष्यते श्रीमच्छांभवाज्ञानुसारतः ॥ 1
11.m: The path of parts will be explained according to the venerable command of Śambhu. // 1b

11.s:
yathā pūrvoktabhuvanamadhye nijanijaṃ gaṇam /
anuyatparato bhinnaṃ tattvaṃ nāmeti bhaṇyate // 2
11.d:
यथा पूर्वोक्तभुवनमध्ये निजनिजं गणम् ।
अनुयत्परतो भिन्नं तत्त्वं नामेति भण्यते ॥ 2
11.m: Just as that which conforms to its respective group amid the previously stated worlds / and is distinguished from another is declared by the name 'principle', // 2

11.s:
tathā teṣvapi tattveṣu svavarge'nugamātmakam /
vyāvṛttaṃ paravargācca kaleti śivaśāsane // 3
11.d:
तथा तेष्वपि तत्त्वेषु स्ववर्गेऽनुगमात्मकम् ।
व्यावृत्तं परवर्गाच्च कलेति शिवशासने ॥ 3
11.m: so too, among those principles, that which conforms to its own group / and is excluded from another group is a part in the teaching of Śiva. // 3

11.s:
kecidāhuḥ punaryāsau śaktirantaḥ susūkṣmikā /
tattvānāṃ sā kaletyuktā dharaṇyāṃ dhārikā yathā // 4
11.d:
केचिदाहुः पुनर्यासौ शक्तिरन्तः सुसूक्ष्मिका ।
तत्त्वानां सा कलेत्युक्ता धरण्यां धारिका यथा ॥ 4
11.m: Others, however, say: that power which is extremely subtle within / the principles is called a part, as the supporting power in the earth. // 4

11.s:
atra pakṣadvaye vastu na bhinnaṃ bhāsate yataḥ /
anugāmi na sāmānyamiṣṭaṃ naiyāyikādivat // 5
11.d:
अत्र पक्षद्वये वस्तु न भिन्नं भासते यतः ।
अनुगामि न सामान्यमिष्टं नैयायिकादिवत् ॥ 5
11.m: On these two views, reality does not appear as differentiated, because / an enduring universal is not accepted [here], as it is by the Naiyāyikas and others. // 5

11.s:
anye vadanti dīkṣādau sukhasaṃgrahaṇārthataḥ /
śivena kalpito vargaḥ kaleti samayāśrayaḥ // 6
11.d:
अन्ये वदन्ति दीक्षादौ सुखसंग्रहणार्थतः ।
शिवेन कल्पितो वर्गः कलेति समयाश्रयः ॥ 6
11.m: Others say: for the purpose of easy comprehension during initiation and the like, / the group constructed by Śiva is a part, having conventional designation as its basis. // 6

11.s:
kṛtaśca devadevena samayo'paramārthatām /
na gacchatīti nāsatyo na cānyasamayodayaḥ // 7
11.d:
कृतश्च देवदेवेन समयोऽपरमार्थताम् ।
न गच्छतीति नासत्यो न चान्यसमयोदयः ॥ 7
11.m: And a convention established by the God of gods does not reach / unreality, so it is not untrue, nor does another convention arise. // 7

11.s:
nivṛttiḥ pṛthivītattve pratiṣṭhāvyaktagocare /
vidyā niśānte śāntā ca śaktyante'ṇḍamidaṃ catuḥ // 8
11.d:
निवृत्तिः पृथिवीतत्त्वे प्रतिष्ठाव्यक्तगोचरे ।
विद्या निशान्ते शान्ता च शक्त्यन्तेऽण्डमिदं चतुः ॥ 8
11.m: Nivṛtti is in the earth principle, Pratiṣṭhā pertains to the unmanifest, / Vidyā reaches the end of night, and Śāntā reaches the end of Śakti: this is the fourfold egg. // 8

11.s:
śāntātītā śive tattve kalātītaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ /
nahyatra vargīkaraṇaṃ samayaḥ kalanāpi vā // 9
11.d:
शान्तातीता शिवे तत्त्वे कलातीतः परः शिवः ।
नह्यत्र वर्गीकरणं समयः कलनापि वा ॥ 9
11.m: Śāntātītā is in the Śiva principle; supreme Śiva is beyond parts. / For here grouping, convention, or division // 9

11.s:
yujyate sarvatodikkaṃ svātantryollāsadhāmani /
svātantryāttu nijaṃ rūpaṃ boddhṛdharmādavicyutam // 10
11.d:
युज्यते सर्वतोदिक्कं स्वातन्त्र्योल्लासधामनि ।
स्वातन्त्र्यात्तु निजं रूपं बोद्धृधर्मादविच्युतम् ॥ 10
11.m: is not appropriate in the abode where absolute autonomy blazes in every direction. / Yet out of absolute autonomy, without deviating from the nature of the knower, // 10

11.s:
upadeśatadāveśaparamārthatvasiddhaye /
bodhyatāmānayandevaḥ sphuṭameva vibhāvyate // 11
11.d:
उपदेशतदावेशपरमार्थत्वसिद्धये ।
बोध्यतामानयन्देवः स्फुटमेव विभाव्यते ॥ 11
11.m: in order to accomplish the ultimate reality of instruction and absorption therein, / the God brings [His] own form into the state of being known, and is clearly conceived. // 11

11.s:
yato'taḥ śivatattve'pi kalāsaṃgatirucyate /
aṇḍaṃ ca nāma bhuvanavibhāgasthitikāraṇam // 12
11.d:
यतोऽतः शिवतत्त्वेऽपि कलासंगतिरुच्यते ।
अण्डं च नाम भुवनविभागस्थितिकारणम् ॥ 12
11.m: Therefore, association with a part is stated even in the Śiva principle. / And an egg is the cause of the persistence of the division of worlds; // 12

11.s:
prāhurāvaraṇaṃ tacca śaktyantaṃ yāvadasti hi /
yadyapi prāk śivākhye'pi tattve bhuvanapaddhatiḥ // 13
11.d:
प्राहुरावरणं तच्च शक्त्यन्तं यावदस्ति हि ।
यद्यपि प्राक् शिवाख्येऽपि तत्त्वे भुवनपद्धतिः ॥ 13
11.m: they declare it to be an envelope, and it indeed extends up to the end of Śakti. / Although the series of worlds was previously stated // 13

11.s:
uktā tathāpyapratighe nāsminnāvṛtisaṃbhavaḥ /
nanvevaṃ dharaṇīṃ muktvā śaktau prakṛtimāyayoḥ // 14
11.d:
उक्ता तथाप्यप्रतिघे नास्मिन्नावृतिसंभवः ।
नन्वेवं धरणीं मुक्त्वा शक्तौ प्रकृतिमाययोः ॥ 14
11.m: even in the principle named Śiva, nevertheless in this unimpeded [realm] no envelopment is possible. / Now, if it is thus, except for the earth, in Śakti, Prakṛti, and Māyā, // 14

11.s:
api cāpratighatve'pi kathamaṇḍasya saṃbhavaḥ /
atrāsmadguravaḥ prāhuryatpṛthivyādipañcakam // 15
11.d:
अपि चाप्रतिघत्वेऽपि कथमण्डस्य संभवः ।
अत्रास्मद्गुरवः प्राहुर्यत्पृथिव्यादिपञ्चकम् ॥ 15
11.m: since there is unobstructedness, how is the occurrence of an egg possible? / To this our gurus replied: as for the pentad beginning with earth, // 15

11.s:
pratyakṣamidamābhāti tato'nyannāsti kiṃcana /
meyatve sthūlasūkṣmatvānmānatve karaṇatvataḥ // 16
11.d:
प्रत्यक्षमिदमाभाति ततोऽन्यन्नास्ति किंचन ।
मेयत्वे स्थूलसूक्ष्मत्वान्मानत्वे करणत्वतः ॥ 16
11.m: this appears perceptible, and there is nothing whatever other than that. / In its state as object of knowledge, due to grossness and subtlety; in its state as means of knowledge, due to being an instrument; // 16

11.s:
kartṛtollāsataḥ kartṛbhāve sphuṭatayoditam /
triṃśattattvaṃ vibhedātma tadabhedo niśā matā // 17
11.d:
कर्तृतोल्लासतः कर्तृभावे स्फुटतयोदितम् ।
त्रिंशत्तत्त्वं विभेदात्म तदभेदो निशा मता ॥ 17
11.m: and in the state of subject, through the flash of agency: it is clearly proclaimed / as the thirtyfold principle consisting of differentiation; its non-differentiation is considered to be night. // 17

11.s:
kāryatvakaraṇatvādivibhāgagalane sati /
vikāsotkasvatantratve śivāntaṃ pañcakaṃ jaguḥ // 18
11.d:
कार्यत्वकरणत्वादिविभागगलने सति ।
विकासोत्कस्वतन्त्रत्वे शिवान्तं पञ्चकं जगुः ॥ 18
11.m: When the division into effect, instrument, and so forth melts away, / and there is autonomous reality eager for expansion, they proclaimed the pentad ending with Śiva. // 18

11.s:
śrīmatkālottarādau ca kathitaṃ bhūyasā tathā /
pañcaitāni tu tattvāni yairvyāptamakhilaṃ jagat // 19
11.d:
श्रीमत्कालोत्तरादौ च कथितं भूयसा तथा ।
पञ्चैतानि तु तत्त्वानि यैर्व्याप्तमखिलं जगत् ॥ 19
11.m: And in the venerable Kālottara and other texts it is repeatedly stated thus: / 'These are the five principles by which the entire universe is pervaded.' // 19

11.s:
pañcamantratanau tena sadyojātādi bhaṇyate /
īśānāntaṃ tatra tatra dharādigaganāntakam // 20
11.d:
पञ्चमन्त्रतनौ तेन सद्योजातादि भण्यते ।
ईशानान्तं तत्र तत्र धरादिगगनान्तकम् ॥ 20
11.m: Therefore, in the body of the five mantras, Sadyojāta and the rest are recited / ending with Īśāna, right there ending with space from earth onward. // 20

11.s:
śivatattvamataḥ śūnyātiśūnyaṃ syādanāśri[vṛ]tam /
yattu sarvāvibhāgātma svatantraṃ bodhasundaram // 21
11.d:
शिवतत्त्वमतः शून्यातिशून्यं स्यादनाश्रि[वृ]तम् ।
यत्तु सर्वाविभागात्म स्वतन्त्रं बोधसुन्दरम् ॥ 21
11.m: Therefore the Śiva principle would be the void beyond the void, unclad. / But that which is devoid of all division, autonomous, beautiful with consciousness, // 21

11.s:
saptatriṃśaṃ tu tatprāhustattvaṃ paraśivābhidham /
tasyāpyuktanayādvedyabhāve'tra parikalpite // 22
11.d:
सप्तत्रिंशं तु तत्प्राहुस्तत्त्वं परशिवाभिधम् ।
तस्याप्युक्तनयाद्वेद्यभावेऽत्र परिकल्पिते ॥ 22
11.m: they call that the thirty-seventh principle, named Paraśiva. / When, by the stated reasoning, the condition of an object of knowledge is conceptualized even for that, // 22

11.s:
yadāste hyanavacchinnaṃ tadaṣṭātriṃśamucyate /
na cānavasthā hyevaṃ syāddṛśyatāṃ hi mahātmabhiḥ // 23
11.d:
यदास्ते ह्यनवच्छिन्नं तदष्टात्रिंशमुच्यते ।
न चानवस्था ह्येवं स्याद्दृश्यतां हि महात्मभिः ॥ 23
11.m: that which abides uncircumscribed is called the thirty-eighth. / Nor would there be infinite regress in this way; let it indeed be seen by the great-souled! // 23

11.s:
yadvedyaṃ kiṃcidābhāti tatkṣaye yatprakāśate /
tattattvamiti nirṇītaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ hṛdi bhāsate // 24
11.d:
यद्वेद्यं किंचिदाभाति तत्क्षये यत्प्रकाशते ।
तत्तत्त्वमिति निर्णीतं षट्त्रिंशं हृदि भासते ॥ 24
11.m: Whatever object of knowledge appears, that which shines upon its destruction / is ascertained as the principle; it shines in the heart as the thirty-sixth. // 24

11.s:
tatkiṃ na kiṃcidvā kiṃcidityākāṅkṣāvaśe vapuḥ /
cidānandasvatantraikarūpaṃ taditi deśane // 25
11.d:
तत्किं न किंचिद्वा किंचिदित्याकाङ्क्षावशे वपुः ।
चिदानन्दस्वतन्त्रैकरूपं तदिति देशने ॥ 25
11.m: 'Is that nothing, or something?': due to this inquiry, when it is taught / that its form consists solely of consciousness, bliss, and autonomy, // 25

11.s:
saptatriṃśaṃ samābhāti tatrākāṅkṣā ca nāparā /
taccāpi klṛptavedyatvaṃ yatra bhāti sa cinmayaḥ // 26
11.d:
सप्तत्रिंशं समाभाति तत्राकाङ्क्षा च नापरा ।
तच्चापि क्लृप्तवेद्यत्वं यत्र भाति स चिन्मयः ॥ 26
11.m: the thirty-seventh shines forth, and regarding that there is no further inquiry. / And when even that appears having an assumed objectivity, that which consists of consciousness // 26

11.s:
aṣṭātriṃśattamaḥ so'pi bhāvanāyopadiśyate /
yadi nāma tataḥ saptatriṃśa eva punarbhavet // 27
11.d:
अष्टात्रिंशत्तमः सोऽपि भावनायोपदिश्यते ।
यदि नाम ततः सप्तत्रिंश एव पुनर्भवेत् ॥ 27
11.m: is the thirty-eighth; even that is taught for contemplative absorption. / If indeed it were to arise from that, it would simply be the thirty-seventh again, // 27

11.s:
avibhāgasvatantratvacinmayatvādidharmatā /
samaiva vedyīkaraṇaṃ kevalaṃ tvadhikaṃ yataḥ // 28
11.d:
अविभागस्वतन्त्रत्वचिन्मयत्वादिधर्मता ।
समैव वेद्यीकरणं केवलं त्वधिकं यतः ॥ 28
11.m: because the properties such as indivisibility, autonomy, and consisting of consciousness / are completely identical; only the making [it] an object of knowledge is additional. // 28

11.s:
dharāyāṃ guṇatattvānte māyānte kramaśaḥ sthitāḥ /
gandho raso rūpamantaḥ sūkṣmabhāvakrameṇa tu // 29
11.d:
धरायां गुणतत्त्वान्ते मायान्ते क्रमशः स्थिताः ।
गन्धो रसो रूपमन्तः सूक्ष्मभावक्रमेण तु ॥ 29
11.m: In earth, up to the end of the principle of the qualities, and up to the end of Māyā, there abide successively / smell, taste, and form, in the order of inner subtlety. // 29

11.s:
iti sthite naye śaktitattvānte'pyasti saukṣmyabhāk /
sparśaḥ ko'pi sadā yasmai yoginaḥ spṛhayālavaḥ // 30
11.d:
इति स्थिते नये शक्तितत्त्वान्तेऽप्यस्ति सौक्ष्म्यभाक् ।
स्पर्शः कोऽपि सदा यस्मै योगिनः स्पृहयालवः ॥ 30
11.m: This doctrine being established, even up to the end of the Śakti principle there is a subtle / touch of some kind, for which yogins are always longing. // 30

11.s:
tatsparśānte tu saṃvittiḥ śuddhacidvyomarūpiṇī /
yasyāṃ rūḍhaḥ samabhyeti svaprakāśātmikāṃ parām // 31
11.d:
तत्स्पर्शान्ते तु संवित्तिः शुद्धचिद्व्योमरूपिणी ।
यस्यां रूढः समभ्येति स्वप्रकाशात्मिकां पराम् ॥ 31
11.m: At the end of that touch, however, is consciousness in the form of the pure ether of consciousness, / established in which one attains the supreme, self-luminous state. // 31

11.s:
ato vindurato nādo rūpamasmādato rasaḥ /
ityuktaṃ kṣobhakatvena spande sparśastu no tathā // 32
11.d:
अतो विन्दुरतो नादो रूपमस्मादतो रसः ।
इत्युक्तं क्षोभकत्वेन स्पन्दे स्पर्शस्तु नो तथा ॥ 32
11.m: Therefore, 'from the drop, sound; from this, form; from this, taste'— / this was stated in terms of agitation in the Spanda [system], but touch is not so. // 32

11.s:
mataṃ caitanmaheśasya śrīpūrve yadabhāṣata /
dhārikāpyāyinī boddhrī pavitrī cāvakāśadā // 33
11.d:
मतं चैतन्महेशस्य श्रीपूर्वे यदभाषत ।
धारिकाप्यायिनी बोद्ध्री पवित्री चावकाशदा ॥ 33
11.m: And this doctrine of the Great Lord was spoken in the revered Pūrva (Mālinīvijayottara): / Supporting, nourishing, knowing, purifying, and space-giving, // 33

11.s:
ebhiḥ śabdairvyavaharan nivṛttyādernijaṃ vapuḥ /
pañcatattvavidhiḥ proktastritattvamadhunocyate // 34
11.d:
एभिः शब्दैर्व्यवहरन् निवृत्त्यादेर्निजं वपुः ।
पञ्चतत्त्वविधिः प्रोक्तस्त्रितत्त्वमधुनोच्यते ॥ 34
11.m: expressing with these words the essential forms of Nivṛtti and the rest, / the rule of five principles was taught. Now the threefold principle is spoken of: // 34

11.s:
vijñānākalaparyantamātmā vidyeśvarāntakam /
śeṣe śivastritattve syādekatattve śivaḥ param // 35
11.d:
विज्ञानाकलपर्यन्तमात्मा विद्येश्वरान्तकम् ।
शेषे शिवस्त्रितत्त्वे स्यादेकतत्त्वे शिवः परम् ॥ 35
11.m: The soul [extends] up to the knower free of instruments; up to the lord of knowledge, [the principle of power]; / and in the remainder Śiva exists in the threefold principle; but in the single principle, only Śiva. // 35

11.s:
imau bhedāvubhau tattvabhedamātrakṛtāviti /
tattvādhvaivāyamitthaṃ ca na ṣaḍadhvasthiteḥ kṣatiḥ // 36
11.d:
इमौ भेदावुभौ तत्त्वभेदमात्रकृताविति ।
तत्त्वाध्वैवायमित्थं च न षडध्वस्थितेः क्षतिः ॥ 36
11.m: These two divisions are produced merely by the division of principles; / therefore this is just the path of principles, and thus there is no damage to the reality of the sixfold path. // 36

11.s:
prakṛt pumānyatiḥ kālo māyā vidyeśasauśivau /
śivaśca navatattve'pi vidhau tattvādhvarūpatā // 37
11.d:
प्रकृत् पुमान्यतिः कालो माया विद्येशसौशिवौ ।
शिवश्च नवतत्त्वेऽपि विधौ तत्त्वाध्वरूपता ॥ 37
11.m: Prakṛti, Puruṣa, Niyati, Kāla, Māyā, the lord of knowledge along with Śiva, / and Śiva: even in the ninefold principle rule, it has the nature of the path of principles. // 37

11.s:
evamaṣṭādaśākhye'pi vidhau nyāyaṃ vadetsudhīḥ /
yatra yatra hi bhogecchā tatprādhānyopayogataḥ // 38
11.d:
एवमष्टादशाख्येऽपि विधौ न्यायं वदेत्सुधीः ।
यत्र यत्र हि भोगेच्छा तत्प्राधान्योपयोगतः ॥ 38
11.m: Likewise, the wise person should state the reasoning in the rule called the eighteenfold. / For wherever there is a desire for enjoyment, through the utility of its primacy // 38

11.s:
anyāntarbhāvanātaśca dīkṣānantavibhedabhāk /
tena ṣaṭtriṃśato yāvadekatattvavidhirbhavet // 39
11.d:
अन्यान्तर्भावनातश्च दीक्षानन्तविभेदभाक् ।
तेन षट्त्रिंशतो यावदेकतत्त्वविधिर्भवेत् ॥ 39
11.m: and through the inclusion of others, initiation partakes of endless divisions; / by this, up from thirty-six down to the rule of a single principle may exist. // 39

11.s:
tattvādhvaiva sa devena prokto vyāsasamāsataḥ /
ekatattvavidhiścaiṣa suprabuddhaṃ guruṃ prati // 40
11.d:
तत्त्वाध्वैव स देवेन प्रोक्तो व्याससमासतः ।
एकतत्त्वविधिश्चैष सुप्रबुद्धं गुरुं प्रति ॥ 40
11.m: That very path of principles has been spoken by the God in expansion and contraction; / and this rule of a single principle is taught with respect to a well-awakened guru // 40

11.s:
śiṣyaṃ ca gatabhogāśamuditaḥ śaṃbhunā yataḥ /
bhedaṃ visphārya visphārya śaktyā svacchandarūpayā // 41
11.d:
शिष्यं च गतभोगाशमुदितः शंभुना यतः ।
भेदं विस्फार्य विस्फार्य शक्त्या स्वच्छन्दरूपया ॥ 41
11.m: and a disciple whose longing for enjoyment is gone by Śambhu, because, / expanding and expanding diversity through His freely willing power, // 41

11.s:
svātmanyabhinne bhagavānnityaṃ viśramayan sthitaḥ /
itthaṃ tryātmādhvano bhedaḥ sthūlasūkṣmaparatvataḥ // 42
11.d:
स्वात्मन्यभिन्ने भगवान्नित्यं विश्रमयन् स्थितः ।
इत्थं त्र्यात्माध्वनो भेदः स्थूलसूक्ष्मपरत्वतः ॥ 42
11.m: the Lord remains perpetually resting within His undivided Self. / Thus the division of the threefold path according to gross, subtle, and supreme states, // 42

11.s:
meyabhāgagataḥ proktaḥ puratattvakalātmakaḥ /
adhunā mātṛbhāgasthaṃ rūpaṃ tredhā nirūpyate // 43
11.d:
मेयभागगतः प्रोक्तः पुरतत्त्वकलात्मकः ।
अधुना मातृभागस्थं रूपं त्रेधा निरूप्यते ॥ 43
11.m: residing in the portion of the object of knowledge and consisting of worlds, principles, and kalās, has been stated. / Now the form residing in the portion of the subject is explained in three ways. // 43

11.s:
yatpramāṇātmakaṃ rūpamadhvano mātṛbhāgagam /
padaṃ hyavagamātmatvasamāveśāttaducyate // 44
11.d:
यत्प्रमाणात्मकं रूपमध्वनो मातृभागगम् ।
पदं ह्यवगमात्मत्वसमावेशात्तदुच्यते ॥ 44
11.m: That form of the path consisting of the means of knowledge, which resides in the subject's portion, / is indeed called a word (pada), because of immersion into the nature of understanding. // 44

11.s:
tadeva ca padaṃ mantraḥ prakṣobhātpracyutaṃ yadā /
guptabhāṣī yato mātā tūṣṇīṃbhūto vyavasthitaḥ // 45
11.d:
तदेव च पदं मन्त्रः प्रक्षोभात्प्रच्युतं यदा ।
गुप्तभाषी यतो माता तूष्णींभूतो व्यवस्थितः ॥ 45
11.m: And that very word is a mantra when it has fallen away from agitation; / for the knowing subject remains silent, whispering secretly; // 45

11.s:
tathāpi na vimarśātma rūpaṃ tyajati tena saḥ /
pramāṇātmavimarśātmā mānavatkṣobhabhāṅnatu // 46
11.d:
तथापि न विमर्शात्म रूपं त्यजति तेन सः ।
प्रमाणात्मविमर्शात्मा मानवत्क्षोभभाङ्नतु ॥ 46
11.m: nonetheless, he does not abandon his reflective nature; therefore, / being of the reflective nature of the means of knowledge, he is not subject to agitation like an ordinary measurement. // 46

11.s:
mantrāṇāṃ ca padānāṃ ca tenoktaṃ trikaśāsane /
abhinnameva svaṃ rūpaṃ niḥspandakṣobhite param // 47
11.d:
मन्त्राणां च पदानां च तेनोक्तं त्रिकशासने ।
अभिन्नमेव स्वं रूपं निःस्पन्दक्षोभिते परम् ॥ 47
11.m: Therefore it is said in the Trika teaching that the essential nature / of mantras and of words is identical; the difference is only in the unmoving and the agitated. // 47

11.s:
audāsīnyaparityāge prakṣobhānavarohaṇe /
varṇādhvā mātṛbhāge syāt pūrvaṃ yā kathitā pramā // 48
11.d:
औदासीन्यपरित्यागे प्रक्षोभानवरोहणे ।
वर्णाध्वा मातृभागे स्यात् पूर्वं या कथिता प्रमा ॥ 48
11.m: When abandonment of indifference occurs, without descending into agitation, / the path of phonemes comes to be in the subject's portion. The valid cognition previously spoken of, // 48

11.s:
sā tu pūrṇasvarūpatvādavibhāgamayī yataḥ /
tata ekaikavarṇatvaṃ tattve tattve kṣamāditaḥ // 49
11.d:
सा तु पूर्णस्वरूपत्वादविभागमयी यतः ।
तत एकैकवर्णत्वं तत्त्वे तत्त्वे क्षमादितः ॥ 49
11.m: being undivided because of its full nature, / and having on that account assigned one phoneme to each principle, beginning with earth, // 49

11.s:
kṛtvā śaive pare proktāḥ ṣoḍaśārṇā visargataḥ /
tatra śaktiparispandastāvān prāk ca nirūpitaḥ // 50
11.d:
कृत्वा शैवे परे प्रोक्ताः षोडशार्णा विसर्गतः ।
तत्र शक्तिपरिस्पन्दस्तावान् प्राक् च निरूपितः ॥ 50
11.m: sixteen phonemes are stated up to the supreme Śiva, by way of creative emission. / The vibration of power therein is of such extent, and has been explained earlier. // 50

11.s:
saṃkalayyocyate sarvamadhunā sukhasaṃvide /
padamantravarṇamekaṃ puraṣoḍaśakaṃ dhareti ca nivṛttiḥ /
tattvārṇamagninayanaṃ rasaśarapuramastramantrapadamanyā // 51
11.d:
संकलय्योच्यते सर्वमधुना सुखसंविदे ।
पदमन्त्रवर्णमेकं पुरषोडशकं धरेति च निवृत्तिः ।
तत्त्वार्णमग्निनयनं रसशरपुरमस्त्रमन्त्रपदमन्या ॥ 51
11.m: Summarising it, all is now stated for ease of understanding: / Nivṛtti has one word, mantra, and phoneme, sixteen worlds, and earth; / the next has twenty-three principles and phonemes, fifty-six worlds, and the astra mantra and word; // 51

11.s:
munitattvārṇaṃ dvikapadamantraṃ vasvakṣibhuvanamaparakalā /
agnyarṇatattvamekakapadamantraṃ sainyabhuvanamiti turyā // 52
11.d:
मुनितत्त्वार्णं द्विकपदमन्त्रं वस्वक्षिभुवनमपरकला ।
अग्न्यर्णतत्त्वमेककपदमन्त्रं सैन्यभुवनमिति तुर्या ॥ 52
11.m: the other kalā has seven principles and phonemes, two words and mantras, and twenty-eight worlds; / the fourth has three phonemes and principles, one word and mantra, and eighteen worlds; // 52

11.s:
ṣoḍaśa varṇāḥ padamantratattvamekaṃ ca śāntyatīteyam /
abhinavaguptenāryātrayamuktaṃ saṃgrahāya śiṣyebhyaḥ // 53
11.d:
षोडश वर्णाः पदमन्त्रतत्त्वमेकं च शान्त्यतीतेयम् ।
अभिनवगुप्तेनार्यात्रयमुक्तं संग्रहाय शिष्येभ्यः ॥ 53
11.m: Śāntyatītā has sixteen phonemes, and one word, mantra, and principle. / This triad of āryā verses has been spoken by Abhinavagupta as a summary for disciples. // 53

11.s:
so'yaṃ samasta evādhvā bhairavābhedavṛttimān /
tatsvātantryātsvatantratvamaśnuvāno'vabhāsate // 54
11.d:
सोऽयं समस्त एवाध्वा भैरवाभेदवृत्तिमान् ।
तत्स्वातन्त्र्यात्स्वतन्त्रत्वमश्नुवानोऽवभासते ॥ 54
11.m: This entire path, functioning non-differently from Bhairava, / shines forth attaining autonomy by virtue of His absolute autonomy. // 54

11.s:
tathāhi mātṛrūpastho mantrādhveti nirūpitaḥ /
tathāhi cidvimarśena grastā vācyadaśā yadā // 55
11.d:
तथाहि मातृरूपस्थो मन्त्राध्वेति निरूपितः ।
तथाहि चिद्विमर्शेन ग्रस्ता वाच्यदशा यदा ॥ 55
11.m: Thus the path of mantras is explained as residing in the form of the knowing subject. / For when the state of the denoted object is swallowed up by consciousness's reflection, // 55

11.s:
śivajñānakriyāyattamananatrāṇatatparā /
aśeṣaśaktipaṭalīlīlālāmpaṭyapāṭavāt // 56
11.d:
शिवज्ञानक्रियायत्तमननत्राणतत्परा ।
अशेषशक्तिपटलीलीलालाम्पट्यपाटवात् ॥ 56
11.m: intent on contemplating and protecting, dependent on the knowledge and action of Śiva, / through the expert passion for the play of the multitude of all powers, // 56

11.s:
cyutā mānamayādrūpāt saṃvinmantrādhvatāṃ gatā /
pramāṇarūpatāmetya prayātyadhvā padātmatām // 57
11.d:
च्युता मानमयाद्रूपात् संविन्मन्त्राध्वतां गता ।
प्रमाणरूपतामेत्य प्रयात्यध्वा पदात्मताम् ॥ 57
11.m: fallen from the form consisting of measurement, consciousness becomes the path of mantras; / attaining the nature of the means of knowledge, the path reaches the state of words. // 57

11.s:
tathā hi māturviśrāntirvarṇānsaṃghaṭya tānbahūn /
saṃghaṭṭanaṃ ca kramikaṃ saṃjalpātmakameva tat // 58
11.d:
तथा हि मातुर्विश्रान्तिर्वर्णान्संघट्य तान्बहून् ।
संघट्टनं च क्रमिकं संजल्पात्मकमेव तत् ॥ 58
11.m: For the rest of the subject consists of assembling those many phonemes, / and that combination is successive, consisting precisely of inner speech; // 58

11.s:
vikalpasya svakaṃ rūpaṃ bhogāveśamayaṃ sphuṭam /
ataḥ pramāṇatārūpaṃ padamasmadgururjagau // 59
11.d:
विकल्पस्य स्वकं रूपं भोगावेशमयं स्फुटम् ।
अतः प्रमाणतारूपं पदमस्मद्गुरुर्जगौ ॥ 59
11.m: it is clearly the intrinsic form of conceptual construction, consisting of immersion in enjoyment. / Hence our guru declared the word to be the form of the means of knowledge. // 59

11.s: pramāṇarūpatāveśamaparityajya meyatām // 60
11.d: प्रमाणरूपतावेशमपरित्यज्य मेयताम् ॥ 60
11.m: Without abandoning immersion in the nature of the means of knowledge, moving into objecthood, // 60

11.s:
gacchankalanayā yogādadhvā proktaḥ kalātmakaḥ /
śuddhe prameyatāyoge sūkṣmasthūlatvabhāgini // 61
11.d:
गच्छन्कलनया योगादध्वा प्रोक्तः कलात्मकः ।
शुद्धे प्रमेयतायोगे सूक्ष्मस्थूलत्वभागिनि ॥ 61
11.m: the path, through its connection with impulsion (kalanā), is declared to consist of kalās. / When connected with pure objecthood, partaking of subtlety and grossness, // 61

11.s:
tattvādhvabhuvanādhvatve krameṇānusaredguruḥ /
prameyamānamātṝṇāṃ yadrūpamupari sthitam // 62
11.d:
तत्त्वाध्वभुवनाध्वत्वे क्रमेणानुसरेद्गुरुः ।
प्रमेयमानमातॄणां यद्रूपमुपरि स्थितम् ॥ 62
11.m: the guru should pursue respectively the paths of principles and worlds. / That form which stands above the object, the means, and the subjects of knowledge // 62

11.s:
pramātmātra sthito'dhvāyaṃ varṇātmā dṛśyatāṃ kila /
ucchalatsaṃvidāmātraviśrāntyāsvādayoginaḥ // 63
11.d:
प्रमात्मात्र स्थितोऽध्वायं वर्णात्मा दृश्यतां किल ।
उच्छलत्संविदामात्रविश्रान्त्यास्वादयोगिनः ॥ 63
11.m: is the subject of valid cognition here: let this path consisting of phonemes indeed be seen! / Possessing the experience of resting in consciousness as the pure knowing subject, brimming forth, // 63

11.s:
sarvābhidhānasāmarthyādaniyantritaśaktayaḥ /
sṛṣṭāḥ svātmasahotthe'rthe dharāparyantabhāgini // 64
11.d:
सर्वाभिधानसामर्थ्यादनियन्त्रितशक्तयः ।
सृष्टाः स्वात्मसहोत्थेऽर्थे धरापर्यन्तभागिनि ॥ 64
11.m: their powers unrestricted because of their capacity to name everything, / projected into objects co-emerging with oneself, extending as far as earth, // 64

11.s:
āmṛśantaḥ svacidbhūmau tāvato'rthānabhedataḥ /
varṇaughāste pramārūpāṃ satyāṃ bibhrati saṃvidam // 65
11.d:
आमृशन्तः स्वचिद्भूमौ तावतोऽर्थानभेदतः ।
वर्णौघास्ते प्रमारूपां सत्यां बिभ्रति संविदम् ॥ 65
11.m: reflecting upon so many objects non-differently within the ground of their own consciousness, / those multitudes of phonemes bear true consciousness, consisting of valid cognition. // 65

11.s:
bālāstiryakpramātāro ye'pyasaṃketabhāginaḥ /
te'pyakṛtrimasaṃskārasārāmenāṃ svasaṃvidam // 66
11.d:
बालास्तिर्यक्प्रमातारो येऽप्यसंकेतभागिनः ।
तेऽप्यकृत्रिमसंस्कारसारामेनां स्वसंविदम् ॥ 66
11.m: Even children and animal knowers who do not partake of conventions, / relying on this consciousness of their own, whose essence is uncontrived latent impressions, // 66

11.s:
bhinnabhinnāmupāśritya yānti citrāṃ pramātṛtām /
asyā cākṛtrimānantavarṇasaṃvidi rūḍhatām // 67
11.d:
भिन्नभिन्नामुपाश्रित्य यान्ति चित्रां प्रमातृताम् ।
अस्या चाकृत्रिमानन्तवर्णसंविदि रूढताम् ॥ 67
11.m: differentiated, attain manifold states of knower; / and when conventions attain rootedness in this uncontrived consciousness of endless phonemes, // 67

11.s:
saṃketā yānti cette'pi yāntyasaṃketavṛttitām /
anayā tu vinā sarve saṃketā bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ // 68
11.d:
संकेता यान्ति चेत्तेऽपि यान्त्यसंकेतवृत्तिताम् ।
अनया तु विना सर्वे संकेता बहुशः कृताः ॥ 68
11.m: they too arrive at the function of unconventionality. / But without this, all conventions, although made many times, // 68

11.s:
aviśrāntatayā kuryuranavasthāṃ duruttarām /
bālo vyutpādyate yena tatra saṃketamārgaṇāt // 69
11.d:
अविश्रान्ततया कुर्युरनवस्थां दुरुत्तराम् ।
बालो व्युत्पाद्यते येन तत्र संकेतमार्गणात् ॥ 69
11.m: due to a lack of resting, would produce a vicious regress hard to overcome. / For in the way a child is taught, by seeking convention there, // 69

11.s:
aṅgulyādeśane'pyasya nāvikalpā tathā matiḥ /
vikalpaḥ śabdamūlaśca śabdaḥ saṃketajīvitaḥ // 70
11.d:
अङ्गुल्यादेशनेऽप्यस्य नाविकल्पा तथा मतिः ।
विकल्पः शब्दमूलश्च शब्दः संकेतजीवितः ॥ 70
11.m: even when pointing with a finger, his mind is not non-conceptual; / and conceptual construction is rooted in speech, while speech has convention as its life. // 70

11.s:
tenānanto hyamāyīyo yo varṇagrāma īdṛśaḥ /
saṃvidvimarśasacivaḥ sadaiva sa hi jṛmbhate // 71
11.d:
तेनानन्तो ह्यमायीयो यो वर्णग्राम ईदृशः ।
संविद्विमर्शसचिवः सदैव स हि जृम्भते ॥ 71
11.m: Therefore, the endless, non-illusory collection of phonemes of this kind, / assisted by consciousness's reflection, is ever blossoming forth; // 71

11.s:
yata eva ca māyīyā varṇāḥ sūtiṃ vitenire /
ye ca māyīyavarṇeṣu vīryatvena nirūpitāḥ // 72
11.d:
यत एव च मायीया वर्णाः सूतिं वितेनिरे ।
ये च मायीयवर्णेषु वीर्यत्वेन निरूपिताः ॥ 72
11.m: and precisely from which the phonemes belonging to Māyā have extended their generation; / and those which are described as the virility within the phonemes of Māyā, // 72

11.s:
saṃketanirapekṣāste prameti parigṛhyatām /
tathā hi paravākyeṣu śruteṣvāvriyate nijā // 73
11.d:
संकेतनिरपेक्षास्ते प्रमेति परिगृह्यताम् ।
तथा हि परवाक्येषु श्रुतेष्वाव्रियते निजा ॥ 73
11.m: independent of conventions: let these be recognized as valid cognition. / For when the words of another are heard, if one's own valid cognition is obscured, // 73

11.s:
pramā yasya jaḍo'sau no tatrārthe'bhyeti mātṛtām /
śukavatsa paṭhatyeva paraṃ tatkramitaikabhāk // 74
11.d:
प्रमा यस्य जडोऽसौ नो तत्रार्थेऽभ्येति मातृताम् ।
शुकवत्स पठत्येव परं तत्क्रमितैकभाक् ॥ 74
11.m: he is inert and does not attain the state of knower with respect to that object; / like a parrot, he merely recites, partaking only of its succession. // 74

11.s:
svātantryalābhataḥ svākyapramālābhe tu boddhṛtā /
yasya hi svapramābodho vipakṣodbhedanigrahāt // 75
11.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यलाभतः स्वाक्यप्रमालाभे तु बोद्धृता ।
यस्य हि स्वप्रमाबोधो विपक्षोद्भेदनिग्रहात् ॥ 75
11.m: However, in the attainment of one's own valid cognition from the attainment of autonomy, the state of knower arises. / For he whose awareness of his own valid cognition [shines] due to the suppression of the emergence of opponents, // 75

11.s:
vākyādivarṇapuñje sve sa pramātā vaśībhavet /
yathā yathā cākṛtakaṃ tadrūpamatiricyate // 76
11.d:
वाक्यादिवर्णपुञ्जे स्वे स प्रमाता वशीभवेत् ।
यथा यथा चाकृतकं तद्रूपमतिरिच्यते ॥ 76
11.m: that knowing subject becomes a master over his collection of phonemes, such as sentences. / And in whatever degree that uncontrived form excels, // 76

11.s:
tathā tathā camatkāratāratamyaṃ vibhāvyate /
ādyāmāyīyavarṇāntarnimagne cottarottare // 77
11.d:
तथा तथा चमत्कारतारतम्यं विभाव्यते ।
आद्यामायीयवर्णान्तर्निमग्ने चोत्तरोत्तरे ॥ 77
11.m: in that degree the graduation of aesthetic wonder is realized. / When successive conventions are submerged within the primary, non-illusory phonemes, // 77

11.s:
sakete pūrvapūrvāṃśamajjane pratibhābhidaḥ /
ādyodrekamahattve'pi pratibhātmani niṣṭhitāḥ // 78
11.d:
सकेते पूर्वपूर्वांशमज्जने प्रतिभाभिदः ।
आद्योद्रेकमहत्त्वेऽपि प्रतिभात्मनि निष्ठिताः ॥ 78
11.m: due to the immersion of previous parts, distinctions of intuitive flash [arise], / established in the self of intuitive flash, even while the initial surge is immense. // 78

11.s:
dhruvaṃ kavitvavaktṛtvaśālitāṃ yānti sarvataḥ /
yāvaddhāmani saṃketanikārakalanojjhite // 79
11.d:
ध्रुवं कवित्ववक्तृत्वशालितां यान्ति सर्वतः ।
यावद्धामनि संकेतनिकारकलनोज्झिते ॥ 79
11.m: They unfailingly attain poetic power and eloquence everywhere, / as long as in that abode freed from the affliction of conventions // 79

11.s:
viśrāntaścinmaye kiṃ kiṃ na vetti kurute na vā /
ata eva hi vāksiddhau varṇānāṃ samupāsyatā // 80
11.d:
विश्रान्तश्चिन्मये किं किं न वेत्ति कुरुते न वा ।
अत एव हि वाक्सिद्धौ वर्णानां समुपास्यता ॥ 80
11.m: resting in the nature of consciousness, what does one not know or what does one not accomplish? / Precisely for this reason, the phonemes are to be worshipped for the attainment of speech, // 80

11.s:
sarvajñatvādisiddhau vā kā siddhiryā na tanmayī /
taduktaṃ varadena śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmate // 81
11.d:
सर्वज्ञत्वादिसिद्धौ वा का सिद्धिर्या न तन्मयी ।
तदुक्तं वरदेन श्रीसिद्धयोगीश्वरीमते ॥ 81
11.m: or for the attainment of omniscience and the like; for what spiritual accomplishment is not composed of that? / That was stated by the boon-giver in the venerable Siddhayogīśvarīmata: // 81

11.s:
tena guptena guptāste śeṣā varṇāstviti sphuṭam /
evaṃ māmātṛmānatvameyatvairyo'vabhāsate // 82
11.d:
तेन गुप्तेन गुप्तास्ते शेषा वर्णास्त्विति स्फुटम् ।
एवं मामातृमानत्वमेयत्वैर्योऽवभासते ॥ 82
11.m: "Hidden by that hidden [phoneme], the remaining phonemes indeed [exist]"—this is clear. / Thus, that path which manifests as the measure, the measurer, the measuring, and the measured, // 82

11.s:
ṣaḍvidhaḥ svavapuḥśuddhau śuddhiṃ so'dhvādhigacchati /
ekena vapuṣā śuddhau tatraivānyaprakāratām // 83
11.d:
षड्विधः स्ववपुःशुद्धौ शुद्धिं सोऽध्वाधिगच्छति ।
एकेन वपुषा शुद्धौ तत्रैवान्यप्रकारताम् ॥ 83
11.m: sixfold, attains purification through the purification of its own form. / In purifying through one form, within that very [form] the nature of the others // 83

11.s:
antarbhāvyācarecchuddhimanusaṃdhānavān guruḥ /
anantarbhāvaśaktau tu sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tu śodhayet // 84
11.d:
अन्तर्भाव्याचरेच्छुद्धिमनुसंधानवान् गुरुः ।
अनन्तर्भावशक्तौ तु सूक्ष्मं सूक्ष्मं तु शोधयेत् ॥ 84
11.m: having subsumed, the attentive guru should perform the purification. / But if unable to subsume, one should purify subtly, level by level. // 84

11.s:
tadviśuddhaṃ bījabhāvāt sūte nottarasaṃtatim /
śodhanaṃ bahudhā tattadbhogaprāptyekatānatā // 85
11.d:
तद्विशुद्धं बीजभावात् सूते नोत्तरसंततिम् ।
शोधनं बहुधा तत्तद्भोगप्राप्त्येकतानता ॥ 85
11.m: That, once purified, does not generate a subsequent series owing to its seed-like nature. / Purification is manifold: one-pointed absorption in obtaining those respective enjoyments, // 85

11.s:
tadādhipatyaṃ tattyāgastacchivātmatvavedanam /
tallīnatā tannirāsaḥ sarvaṃ caitatkramākramāt // 86
11.d:
तदाधिपत्यं तत्त्यागस्तच्छिवात्मत्ववेदनम् ।
तल्लीनता तन्निरासः सर्वं चैतत्क्रमाक्रमात् ॥ 86
11.m: lordship over them, abandonment of them, the cognition of their identity with Śiva, / absorption in them, and their eradication—all this through succession and non-succession. // 86

11.s:
ata eva ca te mantrāḥ śodhakāścitrarūpiṇaḥ /
siddhāntavāmadakṣādau citrāṃ śuddhiṃ vitanvate // 87
11.d:
अत एव च ते मन्त्राः शोधकाश्चित्ररूपिणः ।
सिद्धान्तवामदक्षादौ चित्रां शुद्धिं वितन्वते ॥ 87
11.m: For this very reason, those purifying mantras, having diverse forms, / bring about diverse purifications in Siddhānta, Vāma, Dakṣiṇa, and so forth. // 87

11.s:
anuttaratrikānāmakramamantrāstu ye kila /
te sarve sarvadāḥ kintu kasyācit kvāpi mukhyatā // 88
11.d:
अनुत्तरत्रिकानामक्रममन्त्रास्तु ये किल ।
ते सर्वे सर्वदाः किन्तु कस्याचित् क्वापि मुख्यता ॥ 88
11.m: However, the mantras of non-succession of the unexcelled Trika / are indeed all-bestowing, but a particular one has prominence somewhere. // 88

11.s:
ataḥ śodhakabhāvena śāstre śrīpūrvasaṃjñite /
parāparādimantrāṇāmadhvanyuktā vyavasthitiḥ // 89
11.d:
अतः शोधकभावेन शास्त्रे श्रीपूर्वसंज्ञिते ।
परापरादिमन्त्राणामध्वन्युक्ता व्यवस्थितिः ॥ 89
11.m: Therefore, in the scripture named the venerable Pūrva, / the arrangement of the Parā, Aparā, and other mantras in the path is declared as purifying. // 89

11.s:
śodhakatvaṃ ca mālinyā devīnāṃ tritayasya ca /
devatrayasya vaktrāṇāmaṅgānāmaṣṭakasya ca // 90
11.d:
शोधकत्वं च मालिन्या देवीनां त्रितयस्य च ।
देवत्रयस्य वक्त्राणामङ्गानामष्टकस्य च ॥ 90
11.m: And the role of purifier belongs to the Mālinī, to the triad of goddesses, / to the triad of gods, to the faces, and to the octad of limbs. // 90

11.s:
kiṃ vātibahunā dvāravāstvādhāragurukrame /
lokapāstravidhau mantrān muktvā sarvaṃ viśodhakam // 91
11.d:
किं वातिबहुना द्वारवास्त्वाधारगुरुक्रमे ।
लोकपास्त्रविधौ मन्त्रान् मुक्त्वा सर्वं विशोधकम् ॥ 91
11.m: Or why say too much? In the sequence of the door, the site, the support, and the guru, / and in the rite of the world-protectors and weapons, except for the mantras, everything is a purifier. // 91

11.s:
yaccaitadadhvanaḥ proktaṃ śodhyatvaṃ śoddhṛtā ca yā /
sā svātantryācchivābhede yuktetyuktaṃ ca śāsane // 92
11.d:
यच्चैतदध्वनः प्रोक्तं शोध्यत्वं शोद्धृता च या ।
सा स्वातन्त्र्याच्छिवाभेदे युक्तेत्युक्तं च शासने ॥ 92
11.m: And as for this purifiability and purifier-nature spoken of regarding the path, / that is appropriate due to absolute autonomy within non-difference from Śiva, as stated in the teaching; // 92

11.s:
sarvametadvibhātyeva parameśitari dhruve /
pratibimbasvarūpeṇa na tu bāhyatayā yataḥ // 93
11.d:
सर्वमेतद्विभात्येव परमेशितरि ध्रुवे ।
प्रतिबिम्बस्वरूपेण न तु बाह्यतया यतः ॥ 93
11.m: since all this shines forth within the unchanging Supreme Lord alone / in the form of a reflection, and not as something external. // 93

11.s:
cidvyomnyeva śive tattaddehādimatirīdṛśī /
bhinnā saṃsāriṇāṃ rajjau sarpasragvīcibuddhivat // 94
11.d:
चिद्व्योम्न्येव शिवे तत्तद्देहादिमतिरीदृशी ।
भिन्ना संसारिणां रज्जौ सर्पस्रग्वीचिबुद्धिवत् ॥ 94
11.m: In the ether of consciousness alone, in Śiva, such a notion of diverse bodies and so forth, / fragmented, occurs to transmigrating beings, like the cognition of a snake, a garland, or a ripple in a rope. // 94

11.s:
yataḥ prāgdehamaraṇasiddhāntaḥ svapnagocaraḥ /
dehāntarādirmaraṇe kīdṛgvā dehasaṃbhavaḥ // 95
11.d:
यतः प्राग्देहमरणसिद्धान्तः स्वप्नगोचरः ।
देहान्तरादिर्मरणे कीदृग्वा देहसंभवः ॥ 95
11.m: For the settled view of the death of a previous body is a domain of dream; / at death, another body and so forth—what sort of emergence of a body could there be? // 95

11.s:
svapne'pi pratibhāmātrasāmānyaprathanābalāt /
viśeṣāḥ pratibhāsante na bhāvyante'pi te yathā // 96
11.d:
स्वप्नेऽपि प्रतिभामात्रसामान्यप्रथनाबलात् ।
विशेषाः प्रतिभासन्ते न भाव्यन्तेऽपि ते यथा ॥ 96
11.m: Even in a dream, by the force of the manifestation of a mere general intuitive flash, / particulars appear, although they are not even contemplated as such. // 96

11.s:
śālagrāmopalāḥ keciccitrākṛtibhṛto yathā /
tathā māyādibhūmyantalekhācitrahṛdaścitaḥ // 97
11.d:
शालग्रामोपलाः केचिच्चित्राकृतिभृतो यथा ।
तथा मायादिभूम्यन्तलेखाचित्रहृदश्चितः ॥ 97
11.m: Just as certain Śālagrāma stones bear variegated forms, / so the heart of consciousness is variegated by delineations from Māyā down to the earth. // 97

11.s:
nagarārṇavaśailādyāstadicchānuvidhāyinaḥ /
na svayaṃ sadasanto no kāraṇākāraṇātmakāḥ // 98
11.d:
नगरार्णवशैलाद्यास्तदिच्छानुविधायिनः ।
न स्वयं सदसन्तो नो कारणाकारणात्मकाः ॥ 98
11.m: Cities, oceans, mountains, and the like conform to His will; / they are not intrinsically existent or non-existent, nor of the nature of cause or non-cause. // 98

11.s:
niyateścirarūḍhāyāḥ samucchedātpravartanāt /
arūḍhāyāḥ svatantro'yaṃ sthitaścidvyomabhairavaḥ // 99
11.d:
नियतेश्चिररूढायाः समुच्छेदात्प्रवर्तनात् ।
अरूढायाः स्वतन्त्रोऽयं स्थितश्चिद्व्योमभैरवः ॥ 99
11.m: By uprooting long-established restriction and instituting / what is unestablished, this Bhairava, the ether of consciousness, stands independent. // 99

11.s:
ekacinmātrasaṃpūrṇabhairavābhedabhāgini /
evamasmītyanāmarśo bhedako bhāvamaṇḍale // 100
11.d:
एकचिन्मात्रसंपूर्णभैरवाभेदभागिनि ।
एवमस्मीत्यनामर्शो भेदको भावमण्डले ॥ 100
11.m: In that which shares non-difference with Bhairava, full of the single, pure consciousness, / the non-awareness "thus I am" is the differentiator in the circle of entities. // 100

11.s:
sarvapramāṇairno siddhaṃ svapne kartrantaraṃ yathā /
svasaṃvidaḥ svasiddhāyāstathā sarvatra buddhyatām // 101
11.d:
सर्वप्रमाणैर्नो सिद्धं स्वप्ने कर्त्रन्तरं यथा ।
स्वसंविदः स्वसिद्धायास्तथा सर्वत्र बुद्ध्यताम् ॥ 101
11.m: Just as by all means of knowledge no other agent is established in a dream / apart from one's own self-established consciousness, so should it be understood everywhere. // 101

11.s:
cittacitrapurodyāne krīḍedevaṃ hi vetti yaḥ /
ahameva sthito bhūtabhāvatattvapurairiti // 102
11.d:
चित्तचित्रपुरोद्याने क्रीडेदेवं हि वेत्ति यः ।
अहमेव स्थितो भूतभावतत्त्वपुरैरिति ॥ 102
11.m: Indeed, one who knows thus may play in the garden of the variegated city of the mind: / "I alone abide in the form of the cities of the elements, entities, and principles." // 102

11.s:
evaṃ jāto mṛto'smīti janmamṛtyuvicitratāḥ /
ajanmanyamṛtau bhānti cittabhittau svanirmitāḥ // 103
11.d:
एवं जातो मृतोऽस्मीति जन्ममृत्युविचित्रताः ।
अजन्मन्यमृतौ भान्ति चित्तभित्तौ स्वनिर्मिताः ॥ 103
11.m: "Thus was I born, I am dead"—these variegations of birth and death / appear on the canvas of the mind, self-fashioned, within the birthless and deathless. // 103

11.s:
parehasaṃvidāmātraṃ paralokehalokate /
vastutaḥ saṃvido deśaḥ kālo vā naiva kiṃcana // 104
11.d:
परेहसंविदामात्रं परलोकेहलोकते ।
वस्तुतः संविदो देशः कालो वा नैव किंचन ॥ 104
11.m: The states of other-world and this-world are mere consciousness of 'there' and 'here'; / in reality, there is no space or time whatsoever for consciousness. // 104

11.s:
abhaviṣyadayaṃ sargo mūrtaścenna tu cinmayaḥ /
tadavekṣyata tanmadhyāt kenaiko'pi dharādharaḥ // 105
11.d:
अभविष्यदयं सर्गो मूर्तश्चेन्न तु चिन्मयः ।
तदवेक्ष्यत तन्मध्यात् केनैकोऽपि धराधरः ॥ 105
11.m: If this creation were material and not composed of consciousness, / then by whom could even a single mountain have been seen within it? // 105

11.s:
bhūtatanmātravargāderādhārādheyatākrame /
ante saṃvinmayī śaktiḥ śivarūpaiva dhāriṇī // 106
11.d:
भूततन्मात्रवर्गादेराधाराधेयताक्रमे ।
अन्ते संविन्मयी शक्तिः शिवरूपैव धारिणी ॥ 106
11.m: In the sequence of container and contained among the groups of elements, subtle elements, and so forth, / ultimately the power consisting of consciousness, being of the very nature of Śiva, is the support. // 106

11.s:
tasmātpratītirevetthaṃ kartrī dhartrī ca sā śivaḥ /
tato bhāvāstatra bhāvāḥ śaktirādhārikā tataḥ // 107
11.d:
तस्मात्प्रतीतिरेवेत्थं कर्त्री धर्त्री च सा शिवः ।
ततो भावास्तत्र भावाः शक्तिराधारिका ततः ॥ 107
11.m: Therefore, manifestation alone is thus the agent and the support, and that is Śiva. / From that arise entities; in that are entities; and thence power is the foundational support. // 107

11.s:
sāṃkalpikaṃ nirādhāramapi naiva patatyadhaḥ /
svādhāraśaktau viśrāntaṃ viśvamitthaṃ vimṛśyatām // 108
11.d:
सांकल्पिकं निराधारमपि नैव पतत्यधः ।
स्वाधारशक्तौ विश्रान्तं विश्वमित्थं विमृश्यताम् ॥ 108
11.m: Even a conceptualized object, though baseless, does not fall down; / resting in the power that is its own support, let the universe thus be contemplated. // 108

11.s:
asyā ghanāhamityādirūḍhireva dharāditā /
yāvadante cidasmīti nirvṛttā bhairavātmatā // 109
11.d:
अस्या घनाहमित्यादिरूढिरेव धरादिता ।
यावदन्ते चिदस्मीति निर्वृत्ता भैरवात्मता ॥ 109
11.m: The very crystallization of this [consciousness] such as "I am solid" is the state of earth and the rest, / until finally, as "I am consciousness," the nature of Bhairava is realized. // 109

11.s:
maṇāvindrāyudhe bhāsa iva nīlādayaḥ śive /
paramārthata eṣāṃ tu nodayo na vyayaḥ kvacit // 110
11.d:
मणाविन्द्रायुधे भास इव नीलादयः शिवे ।
परमार्थत एषां तु नोदयो न व्ययः क्वचित् ॥ 110
11.m: Like colors such as blue in a jewel or a rainbow, [these] appearances are in Śiva; / in the ultimate sense, however, there is never any arising or passing away of them. // 110

11.s:
deśe kāle'tra vā sṛṣṭirityetadasamañjasam /
cidātmanā hi devena sṛṣṭirdikkālayorapi // 111
11.d:
देशे कालेऽत्र वा सृष्टिरित्येतदसमञ्जसम् ।
चिदात्मना हि देवेन सृष्टिर्दिक्कालयोरपि ॥ 111
11.m: "Creation occurs here in space or in time"—this is incongruous; / for space and time are also creations by the Lord whose nature is consciousness. // 111

11.s:
jāgarābhimate sārdhahastatritayagocare /
prahare ca pṛthak svapnāścitradikkālamāninaḥ // 112
11.d:
जागराभिमते सार्धहस्तत्रितयगोचरे ।
प्रहरे च पृथक् स्वप्नाश्चित्रदिक्कालमानिनः ॥ 112
11.m: Within the three and a half cubits deemed the waking state / and within a single three-hour watch, diverse dreams imagine varied space and time. // 112

11.s:
ata eva kṣaṇaṃ nāma na kiṃcidapi manmahe /
kriyākṣaṇe vāpyekasmin bahvyaḥ saṃsyurdrutāḥ kriyāḥ // 113
11.d:
अत एव क्षणं नाम न किंचिदपि मन्महे ।
क्रियाक्षणे वाप्येकस्मिन् बह्व्यः संस्युर्द्रुताः क्रियाः ॥ 113
11.m: Precisely for this reason, we do not consider a "moment" to be anything [objective]; / or even in a single moment of action, there can be many rapid actions. // 113

11.s:
tena ye bhāvasaṃkocaṃ kṣaṇāntaṃ pratipedire /
te nūnamenayā nāḍyā śūnyadṛṣṭyavalambinaḥ // 114
11.d:
तेन ये भावसंकोचं क्षणान्तं प्रतिपेदिरे ।
ते नूनमेनया नाड्या शून्यदृष्ट्यवलम्बिनः ॥ 114
11.m: Therefore, those who accepted the contraction of entities down to a moment, / surely, through this channel, resorted to the view of the void. // 114

11.s:
tadya eṣa sato bhāvāñ śūnyīkartuṃ tathāsataḥ /
sphuṭīkartuṃ svatantratvādīśaḥ so'smatprabhuḥ śivaḥ // 115
11.d:
तद्य एष सतो भावाञ् शून्यीकर्तुं तथासतः ।
स्फुटीकर्तुं स्वतन्त्रत्वादीशः सोऽस्मत्प्रभुः शिवः ॥ 115
11.m: Therefore, he who is able through absolute autonomy to void existent entities / and likewise to make clear the non-existent, he is our Lord, Śiva. // 115

11.s:
taditthaṃ parameśāno viśvarūpaḥ pragīyate /
na tu bhinnasya kasyāpi dharāderupapannatā // 116
11.d:
तदित्थं परमेशानो विश्वरूपः प्रगीयते ।
न तु भिन्नस्य कस्यापि धरादेरुपपन्नता ॥ 116
11.m: Thus the Supreme Lord is celebrated as having the form of the universe; / no reality of any distinct earth or the like can be established. // 116

11.s:
uktaṃ caitatpuraiveti na bhūyaḥ pravivicyate /
bhūyobhiścāpi bāhyārthadūṣaṇaiḥ pravyaramyata // 117
11.d:
उक्तं चैतत्पुरैवेति न भूयः प्रविविच्यते ।
भूयोभिश्चापि बाह्यार्थदूषणैः प्रव्यरम्यत ॥ 117
11.m: And this has already been stated earlier, so it is not analyzed further; / and an end has been made to extensive refutations of external objects. // 117

11.s: taditthameṣa nirṇītaḥ kalādervistaro'dhvanaḥ // 118
11.d: तदित्थमेष निर्णीतः कलादेर्विस्तरोऽध्वनः ॥ 118
11.m: Thus has this extent of the path consisting of kalā and the rest been ascertained. // 118

12.s: athādhvano'sya prakṛta upayogaḥ prakāśyate // 1
12.d: अथाध्वनोऽस्य प्रकृत उपयोगः प्रकाश्यते ॥ 1
12.m: Now, the present practical application of this path is elucidated. // 1b

12.s:
itthamadhvā samasto'yaṃ yathā saṃvidi saṃsthitaḥ /
taddvārā śūnyadhīprāṇanāḍīcakratanuṣvatho // 2
12.d:
इत्थमध्वा समस्तोऽयं यथा संविदि संस्थितः ।
तद्द्वारा शून्यधीप्राणनाडीचक्रतनुष्वथो ॥ 2
12.m: Thus, this entire path, as it resides in consciousness, / and through that in the void, intellect, vital breath, the network of channels, and the body, // 2

12.s:
bahiśca liṅgamūrtyagnisthaṇḍilādiṣu sarvataḥ /
tathā sthitaḥ samastaśca vyastaścaiṣa kramākramāt // 3
12.d:
बहिश्च लिङ्गमूर्त्यग्निस्थण्डिलादिषु सर्वतः ।
तथा स्थितः समस्तश्च व्यस्तश्चैष क्रमाक्रमात् ॥ 3
12.m: and externally, everywhere in the liṅga, the image, the fire, the altar, and so forth— / thus it abides as both collective and individual, through succession and non-succession. // 3

12.s:
āsaṃvittattvamābāhyaṃ yo'yamadhvā vyavasthitaḥ /
tatra tatrocitaṃ rūpaṃ svaṃ svātantryeṇa bhāsayet // 4
12.d:
आसंवित्तत्त्वमाबाह्यं योऽयमध्वा व्यवस्थितः ।
तत्र तत्रोचितं रूपं स्वं स्वातन्त्र्येण भासयेत् ॥ 4
12.m: This path, which is established from the principle of consciousness down to the external realm, / should manifest through absolute autonomy its appropriate form in each corresponding place. // 4

12.s:
sarvaṃ sarvatra rūpaṃ ca tasyāpi na na bhāsate /
nahyavaccheditāṃ kvāpi svapne'pi viṣahāmahe // 5
12.d:
सर्वं सर्वत्र रूपं च तस्यापि न न भासते ।
नह्यवच्छेदितां क्वापि स्वप्नेऽपि विषहामहे ॥ 5
12.m: And its universal form everywhere does not fail to shine forth; / for we do not tolerate limitation anywhere, even in a dream. // 5

12.s:
evaṃ viśvādhvasaṃpūrṇaṃ kālavyāpāracitritam /
deśakālamayaspandasadma dehaṃ vilokayet // 6
12.d:
एवं विश्वाध्वसंपूर्णं कालव्यापारचित्रितम् ।
देशकालमयस्पन्दसद्म देहं विलोकयेत् ॥ 6
12.m: Thus one should view the body filled with the entire path, variegated by the operation of time, / the abode of the vibration consisting of space and time. // 6

12.s:
tathā vilokyamāno'sau viśvāntardevatāmayaḥ /
dhyeyaḥ pūjyaśca tarpyaśca tadāviṣṭo vimucyate // 7
12.d:
तथा विलोक्यमानोऽसौ विश्वान्तर्देवतामयः ।
ध्येयः पूज्यश्च तर्प्यश्च तदाविष्टो विमुच्यते ॥ 7
12.m: Viewed in this way, it is composed of the deities within the universe, / to be meditated upon, worshipped, and propitiated; possessed of that, one is liberated. // 7

12.s:
itthaṃ ghaṭaṃ paṭaṃ liṅgaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ pustakaṃ jalam /
yadvā kiṃcitkvacitpaśyettatra tanmayatāṃ vrajet // 8
12.d:
इत्थं घटं पटं लिङ्गं स्थण्डिलं पुस्तकं जलम् ।
यद्वा किंचित्क्वचित्पश्येत्तत्र तन्मयतां व्रजेत् ॥ 8
12.m: In this way, whether one sees a pot, a cloth, a liṅga, an altar, a book, water, / or whatever thing anywhere, one should enter into identity with it. // 8

12.s:
tatrārpaṇaṃ hi vastūnāmabhedenārcanaṃ matam /
tathā saṃpūrṇarūpatvānusaṃdhirdhyānamucyate // 9
12.d:
तत्रार्पणं हि वस्तूनामभेदेनार्चनं मतम् ।
तथा संपूर्णरूपत्वानुसंधिर्ध्यानमुच्यते ॥ 9
12.m: For offering objects into it non-differently is held to be worship; / likewise, the continuous contemplation of its replete nature is spoken of as meditation. // 9

12.s:
saṃpūrṇatvānusaṃdhānamakampaṃ dārḍhyamānayan /
tathāntarjalpayogena vimṛśañjapabhājanam // 10
12.d:
संपूर्णत्वानुसंधानमकम्पं दार्ढ्यमानयन् ।
तथान्तर्जल्पयोगेन विमृशञ्जपभाजनम् ॥ 10
12.m: Bringing that contemplation of completeness to unshakeable firmness, / and likewise contemplating through internal dialogue, one becomes an adept in recitation. // 10

12.s:
tatrārpitānāṃ bhāvānāṃ svakabhedavilāpanam /
kurvaṃstadraśmisadbhāvaṃ dadyāddhomakriyāparaḥ // 11
12.d:
तत्रार्पितानां भावानां स्वकभेदविलापनम् ।
कुर्वंस्तद्रश्मिसद्भावं दद्याद्धोमक्रियापरः ॥ 11
12.m: Dissolving the separate existence of the entities offered therein, / making them into the reality of its rays, devoted to the rite of oblation, he would offer [them]. // 11

12.s:
tathaivaṃkurvataḥ sarvaṃ samabhāvena paśyataḥ /
niṣkampatā vrataṃ śuddhaṃ sāmyaṃ nandiśikhoditam // 12
12.d:
तथैवंकुर्वतः सर्वं समभावेन पश्यतः ।
निष्कम्पता व्रतं शुद्धं साम्यं नन्दिशिखोदितम् ॥ 12
12.m: And likewise for one acting thus, seeing everything with an even vision, / that unshakeable state is the pure observance, the equanimity taught in the Nandiśikhā. // 12

12.s:
tathārcanajapadhyānahomavratavidhikramāt /
paripūrṇāṃ sthitiṃ prāhuḥ samādhiṃ guravaḥ purā // 13
12.d:
तथार्चनजपध्यानहोमव्रतविधिक्रमात् ।
परिपूर्णां स्थितिं प्राहुः समाधिं गुरवः पुरा ॥ 13
12.m: Thus, through the procedure of worship, recitation, meditation, oblation, and observance, / the masters of old declared that replete condition to be absorption. // 13

12.s:
atra pūjājapādyeṣu bahirantardvayasthitau /
dravyaughe na vidhiḥ ko'pi na kāpi pratiṣiddhatā // 14
12.d:
अत्र पूजाजपाद्येषु बहिरन्तर्द्वयस्थितौ ।
द्रव्यौघे न विधिः कोऽपि न कापि प्रतिषिद्धता ॥ 14
12.m: Here, in worship, recitation, and so on, whether resting externally or internally, / among the multitude of substances there is no positive injunction, nor is anything prohibited. // 14

12.s:
kalpanāśuddhisaṃdhyādernopayogo'tra kaścana /
uktaṃ śrītrikasūtre ca jāyate yajanaṃ prati // 15
12.d:
कल्पनाशुद्धिसंध्यादेर्नोपयोगोऽत्र कश्चन ।
उक्तं श्रीत्रिकसूत्रे च जायते यजनं प्रति ॥ 15
12.m: Here, constructed purifications, twilight worship, and the like have no utility whatsoever; / and it is said in the Śrītrikasūtra regarding sacrifice: // 15

12.s:
avidhijño vidhijñaścetyevamādi suvistaram /
yadā yathā yena yatra svā samvittiḥ prasīdati // 16
12.d:
अविधिज्ञो विधिज्ञश्चेत्येवमादि सुविस्तरम् ।
यदा यथा येन यत्र स्वा सम्वित्तिः प्रसीदति ॥ 16
12.m: ‘One who knows the rules and one who does not know the rules,’ and so on in full detail. / When, how, by whatever means, and wherever one’s own consciousness is satisfied, // 16

12.s:
tadā tathā tena tatra tattadbhogyaṃ vidhiśca saḥ /
laukikālaukikaṃ sarvaṃ tenātra viniyojayet // 17
12.d:
तदा तथा तेन तत्र तत्तद्भोग्यं विधिश्च सः ।
लौकिकालौकिकं सर्वं तेनात्र विनियोजयेत् ॥ 17
12.m: then, thus, by that means, and there, that is the object of enjoyment, and that is the rule; / therefore, one should employ everything worldly and unworldly herein. // 17

12.s:
niṣkampatve sakampastu kampaṃ nirhrāsayedbalāt /
yathā yenābhyupāyena kramādakramato'pi vā // 18
12.d:
निष्कम्पत्वे सकम्पस्तु कम्पं निर्ह्रासयेद्बलात् ।
यथा येनाभ्युपायेन क्रमादक्रमतोऽपि वा ॥ 18
12.m: One who wavers in unshakeability, however, should forcefully diminish that wavering / by whatever means, gradually or all at once. // 18

12.s:
vicikitsā galatyantastathāsau yatnavānbhavet /
dhīkarmākṣagatā devīrniṣiddhaireva tarpayet // 19
12.d:
विचिकित्सा गलत्यन्तस्तथासौ यत्नवान्भवेत् ।
धीकर्माक्षगता देवीर्निषिद्धैरेव तर्पयेत् ॥ 19
12.m: He should make effort in such a way that doubt melts away internally; / he should gratify the goddesses residing in the senses of intellect and action with precisely what is prohibited, // 19

12.s:
vīravrataṃ cābhinandediti bhargaśikhāvacaḥ /
tathāhi śaṅkā mālinyaṃ glāniḥ saṃkoca ityadaḥ // 20
12.d:
वीरव्रतं चाभिनन्देदिति भर्गशिखावचः ।
तथाहि शङ्का मालिन्यं ग्लानिः संकोच इत्यदः ॥ 20
12.m: and should welcome the observance of heroes: such is the teaching of the Bhargaśikhā. / For suspicion, taint, dejection, and contraction—these // 20

12.s:
saṃsārakārāgārāntaḥ sthūlasthūṇāghaṭāyate /
mantrā varṇasvabhāvā ye dravyaṃ yatpāñcabhautikam // 21
12.d:
संसारकारागारान्तः स्थूलस्थूणाघटायते ।
मन्त्रा वर्णस्वभावा ये द्रव्यं यत्पाञ्चभौतिकम् ॥ 21
12.m: form thick pillars within the prison-house of cyclic existence. / As for mantras, they are of the nature of phonemes; as for substance, it is made of the five elements; // 21

12.s:
yaccidātma prāṇijātaṃ tatra kaḥ saṃkaraḥ katham /
saṃkarābhāvataḥ keyaṃ śaṅkā tasyāmapi sphuṭam // 22
12.d:
यच्चिदात्म प्राणिजातं तत्र कः संकरः कथम् ।
संकराभावतः केयं शङ्का तस्यामपि स्फुटम् ॥ 22
12.m: and as for the multitude of living beings, its essence is consciousness—what pollution could be there, and how? / Because of the absence of pollution, what is this doubt? Even with regard to it, clearly, // 22

12.s:
na śaṅketa tathā śaṅkā vilīyetāvahelayā /
śrīsarvācāravīrālīniśācarakramādiṣu // 23
12.d:
न शङ्केत तथा शङ्का विलीयेतावहेलया ।
श्रीसर्वाचारवीरालीनिशाचरक्रमादिषु ॥ 23
12.m: one should not doubt, so that doubt dissolves effortlessly. / In the scriptures such as the venerable Sarvācāra, Vīrāvalī, Niśācarakrama, and others, // 23

12.s:
śāstreṣu vitataṃ caitattatra tatrocyate yataḥ /
śaṅkayā jāyate glāniḥ śaṅkayā vighnabhājanam // 24
12.d:
शास्त्रेषु विततं चैतत्तत्र तत्रोच्यते यतः ।
शङ्कया जायते ग्लानिः शङ्कया विघ्नभाजनम् ॥ 24
12.m: this is set forth extensively, because it is stated in various places: / ‘Through doubt dejection arises; through doubt one becomes a vessel for obstacles.’ // 24

12.s:
uvācotpaladevaśca śrīmānasmadgurorguruḥ /
sarvāśaṅkāśaniṃ mārgaṃ numo māheśvaraṃ tviti // 25
anuttarapadāptaye tadidamāṇavaṃ darśitābhyupāyamativistarānnanu vidāṃkurudhvaṃ budhāḥ /
12.d:
उवाचोत्पलदेवश्च श्रीमानस्मद्गुरोर्गुरुः ।
सर्वाशङ्काशनिं मार्गं नुमो माहेश्वरं त्विति ॥ 25
अनुत्तरपदाप्तये तदिदमाणवं दर्शिताभ्युपायमतिविस्तरान्ननु विदांकुरुध्वं बुधाः ।
12.m:
And the venerable Utpaladeva, the guru of our guru, said: / ‘We praise the path of Maheśvara, the thunderbolt against all doubt.’ // 25
Therefore, O wise ones, understand this individual means displayed in great detail for the attainment of the unexcelled state!

13.s: athādhikṛtibhāhanaṃ ka iha vā kathaṃ vetyalaṃ vivecayitumucyate vividhaśaktipātakramaḥ // 1
13.d: अथाधिकृतिभाहनं क इह वा कथं वेत्यलं विवेचयितुमुच्यते विविधशक्तिपातक्रमः ॥ 1
13.m: Now, the succession of diverse descents of power is expounded in order to thoroughly discern who in this world is qualified for this [knowledge], or how. // 1b

13.s:
tatra kecidiha prāhuḥ śaktipāta imaṃ vidhim /
taṃ pradarśya nirākṛtya svamataṃ darśayiṣyate // 2
13.d:
तत्र केचिदिह प्राहुः शक्तिपात इमं विधिम् ।
तं प्रदर्श्य निराकृत्य स्वमतं दर्शयिष्यते ॥ 2
13.m: Here, some state this rule regarding the descent of power; / setting it forth and refuting it, [our] own doctrine will be shown. // 2

13.s:
tatredaṃ dṛśyamānaṃ satsukhaduḥkhavimohabhāk /
viṣamaṃ sattathābhūtaṃ samaṃ hetuṃ prakalpayet // 3
13.d:
तत्रेदं दृश्यमानं सत्सुखदुःखविमोहभाक् ।
विषमं सत्तथाभूतं समं हेतुं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 3
13.m: Here, this [world] being experienced, partaking of pleasure, pain, and delusion, / being varied, one should postulate an unvaried cause of such a nature. // 3

13.s:
so'vyaktaṃ tacca sattvādinānārūpamacetanam /
ghaṭādivatkāryamiti hetureko'sya sā niśā // 4
13.d:
सोऽव्यक्तं तच्च सत्त्वादिनानारूपमचेतनम् ।
घटादिवत्कार्यमिति हेतुरेकोऽस्य सा निशा ॥ 4
13.m: That is the unmanifest, and that is insentient, having manifold forms like sattva and the rest; / being an effect like a pot or the like, it has a single cause, which is that night [māyā]. // 4

13.s:
sā jaḍā kāryatādrūpyātkāryaṃ cāsyāṃ sadeva hi /
kalādidharaṇīprāntaṃ jāḍyātsā sūtaye'kṣamā // 5
13.d:
सा जडा कार्यताद्रूप्यात्कार्यं चास्यां सदेव हि ।
कलादिधरणीप्रान्तं जाड्यात्सा सूतयेऽक्षमा ॥ 5
13.m: It is insentient because it has the nature of an effect, and the effect in it is indeed existent, / ending from the parts up to the earth; on account of insentience, it is incapable of giving birth. // 5

13.s:
teneśaḥ kṣobhayedenāṃ kṣobho'syāḥ sūtiyogyatā /
puṃsaḥ prati ca sā bhogyaṃ sūte'nādīn pṛthagvidhān // 6
13.d:
तेनेशः क्षोभयेदेनां क्षोभोऽस्याः सूतियोग्यता ।
पुंसः प्रति च सा भोग्यं सूतेऽनादीन् पृथग्विधान् ॥ 6
13.m: Therefore the Lord agitates it; its agitation is its capacity to give birth, / and for the soul it gives birth to beginningless, distinct kinds of objects of enjoyment. // 6

13.s:
puṃsaśca nirviśeṣatve muktāṇūn prati kiṃ na tat /
nimittaṃ karmasaṃskāraḥ sa ca teṣu na vidyate // 7
13.d:
पुंसश्च निर्विशेषत्वे मुक्ताणून् प्रति किं न तत् ।
निमित्तं कर्मसंस्कारः स च तेषु न विद्यते ॥ 7
13.m: And the soul being without distinction, why does that not [occur] for liberated souls? / The cause is the impression of karma, and that does not exist in them. // 7

13.s:
iti cetkarmasaṃskārābhāvasteṣāṃ kutaḥ kila /
na bhogādanyakarmāṃśaprasaṅgo hi duratyayaḥ // 8
13.d:
इति चेत्कर्मसंस्काराभावस्तेषां कुतः किल ।
न भोगादन्यकर्मांशप्रसङ्गो हि दुरत्ययः ॥ 8
13.m: If it is argued thus, whence indeed is the absence of the impression of karma in them? / Not from experiencing [it], for the consequence of other portions of karma is unavoidable. // 8

13.s:
yugapatkarmaṇāṃ bhogo naca yuktaḥ krameṇa hi /
phaledyatkarma tatkasmātsvaṃ rūpaṃ saṃtyajetkvacit // 9
13.d:
युगपत्कर्मणां भोगो नच युक्तः क्रमेण हि ।
फलेद्यत्कर्म तत्कस्मात्स्वं रूपं संत्यजेत्क्वचित् ॥ 9
13.m: Nor is the simultaneous experience of karmas appropriate, for karma which / bears fruit in succession—why would it ever abandon its own nature? // 9

13.s:
jñānātkarmakṣayaścettatkuta īśvaracoditāt /
dharmādyadi kutaḥ so'pi karmataścettaducyatām // 10
13.d:
ज्ञानात्कर्मक्षयश्चेत्तत्कुत ईश्वरचोदितात् ।
धर्माद्यदि कुतः सोऽपि कर्मतश्चेत्तदुच्यताम् ॥ 10
13.m: If the destruction of karma is from knowledge, whence is that? If from righteousness prompted by the Lord, / whence is that? If from karma, then let that be explained. // 10

13.s:
nahi karmāsti tādṛkṣaṃ yena jñānaṃ pravartate /
karmajatve ca tajjñānaṃ phalarāśau pateddhruvam // 11
13.d:
नहि कर्मास्ति तादृक्षं येन ज्ञानं प्रवर्तते ।
कर्मजत्वे च तज्ज्ञानं फलराशौ पतेद्ध्रुवम् ॥ 11
13.m: For there is no such karma by which knowledge is set in motion; / and if born of karma, that knowledge would certainly fall into the pile of fruits. // 11

13.s:
anyakarmaphalaṃ prācyaṃ karmarāśiṃ ca kiṃ dahet /
īśasya dveṣarāgādiśūnyasyāpi kathaṃ kvacit // 12
13.d:
अन्यकर्मफलं प्राच्यं कर्मराशिं च किं दहेत् ।
ईशस्य द्वेषरागादिशून्यस्यापि कथं क्वचित् ॥ 12
13.m: And why would the fruit of another karma burn away the previous mass of karma? / Even for the Lord, who is devoid of aversion, attachment, and the like, how in any case // 12

13.s:
tathābhisaṃdhirnānyatra bhedahetorabhāvataḥ /
nanvitthaṃ pradahejjñānaṃ karmajālāni karma hi // 13
13.d:
तथाभिसंधिर्नान्यत्र भेदहेतोरभावतः ।
नन्वित्थं प्रदहेज्ज्ञानं कर्मजालानि कर्म हि ॥ 13
13.m: could there be such an intention elsewhere, given the absence of a cause for differentiation? / ‘Well, knowledge burns the webs of karma in this way: for karma, // 13

13.s:
ajñānasahakārīdaṃ sūte svargādikaṃ phalam /
ajñānaṃ jñānato naśyedanyakarmaphalādapi // 14
13.d:
अज्ञानसहकारीदं सूते स्वर्गादिकं फलम् ।
अज्ञानं ज्ञानतो नश्येदन्यकर्मफलादपि ॥ 14
13.m: with ignorance as its auxiliary, gives birth to fruit such as heaven; / ignorance is destroyed by knowledge, and even by the fruit of another karma, // 14

13.s:
upavāsādikaṃ cānyadduṣṭakarmaphalaṃ bhavet /
niṣphalīkurute duṣṭaṃ karmetyaṅgīkṛtaṃ kila // 15
13.d:
उपवासादिकं चान्यद्दुष्टकर्मफलं भवेत् ।
निष्फलीकुरुते दुष्टं कर्मेत्यङ्गीकृतं किल ॥ 15
13.m: such as fasting and the like, which is the fruit of bad karma; / it is accepted, surely, that it makes bad karma fruitless.’ // 15

13.s:
ajñānamiti yatproktaṃ jñānābhāvaḥ sa cetsa kim /
prāgabhāvo'thavā dhvaṃsa ādye kiṃ sarvasaṃvidām // 16
13.d:
अज्ञानमिति यत्प्रोक्तं ज्ञानाभावः स चेत्स किम् ।
प्रागभावोऽथवा ध्वंस आद्ये किं सर्वसंविदाम् ॥ 16
13.m: If that which is called ignorance is the absence of knowledge, what is it? / Is it prior non-existence or destruction? In the first case, is it [the absence] of all cognitions, // 16

13.s:
kasyāpi vātha jñānasya prācyaḥ pakṣastvasaṃbhavī /
na kiṃcidyasya vijñānamudapādi tathāvidhaḥ // 17
13.d:
कस्यापि वाथ ज्ञानस्य प्राच्यः पक्षस्त्वसंभवी ।
न किंचिद्यस्य विज्ञानमुदपादि तथाविधः ॥ 17
13.m: or of some particular knowledge? The first view is impossible: / there is no soul in this beginningless existence for whom no knowledge of any kind // 17

13.s:
nāṇurasti bhave hyasminnanādau ko'nvayaṃ kramaḥ /
bhāvinaḥ prāgabhāvaśca jñānasyeti sthite sati // 18
13.d:
नाणुरस्ति भवे ह्यस्मिन्ननादौ कोऽन्वयं क्रमः ।
भाविनः प्रागभावश्च ज्ञानस्येति स्थिते सति ॥ 18
13.m: has arisen—what sequence would this be? / If it is established that [ignorance] is the prior non-existence of future knowledge, // 18

13.s:
muktāṇorapi so'styeva janmataḥ prāgasau naca /
jñānaṃ bhāvi vimukte'sminniti ceccarcyatāmidam // 19
13.d:
मुक्ताणोरपि सोऽस्त्येव जन्मतः प्रागसौ नच ।
ज्ञानं भावि विमुक्तेऽस्मिन्निति चेच्चर्च्यतामिदम् ॥ 19
13.m: that certainly exists even for a liberated soul prior to birth; / if it is said that future knowledge does not exist in this liberated one, let this be examined: // 19

13.s:
kasmājjñānaṃ na bhāvyatra nanu dehādyajanmataḥ /
tatkasmātkarmaṇaḥ kṣaiṇyāttatkuto'jñānahānitaḥ // 20
13.d:
कस्माज्ज्ञानं न भाव्यत्र ननु देहाद्यजन्मतः ।
तत्कस्मात्कर्मणः क्षैण्यात्तत्कुतोऽज्ञानहानितः ॥ 20
13.m: Why would knowledge not be future here? ‘Surely because of the non-birth of the body and the rest.’ / From what is that? ‘From the exhaustion of karma.’ From what is that? ‘From the cessation of ignorance.’ // 20

13.s:
ajñānasya kathaṃ hāniḥ prāgabhāve hi saṃvidaḥ /
ajñānaṃ prāgabhāvo'sau na bhāvyutpattyasaṃbhavāt // 21
13.d:
अज्ञानस्य कथं हानिः प्रागभावे हि संविदः ।
अज्ञानं प्रागभावोऽसौ न भाव्युत्पत्त्यसंभवात् ॥ 21
13.m: How is there cessation of ignorance? For when there is prior non-existence of consciousness, / that prior non-existence is ignorance, and it cannot occur because of the impossibility of arising. // 21

13.s:
kasmānna bhāvi tajjñānaṃ nanu dehādyajanmataḥ /
ityeṣa sarvapakṣaghno niśitaścakrakabhramaḥ // 22
13.d:
कस्मान्न भावि तज्ज्ञानं ननु देहाद्यजन्मतः ।
इत्येष सर्वपक्षघ्नो निशितश्चक्रकभ्रमः ॥ 22
13.m: Why is that knowledge not future? ‘Surely because of the non-birth of the body and the rest.’ / This is a sharp circular argument that destroys all positions. // 22

13.s:
atha pradhvaṃsa evedamajñānaṃ tatsadā sthitam /
muktāṇuṣviti teṣvastu māyākāryavijṛmbhitam // 23
13.d:
अथ प्रध्वंस एवेदमज्ञानं तत्सदा स्थितम् ।
मुक्ताणुष्विति तेष्वस्तु मायाकार्यविजृम्भितम् ॥ 23
13.m: Now, if this ignorance is simply destruction, that remains constantly / in liberated souls; so let them have the expansion of the effects of māyā. // 23

13.s:
athājñānaṃ nahyabhāvo mithyājñānaṃ tu tanmatam /
tadeva karmaṇāṃ svasminkartavye sahakāraṇam // 24
13.d:
अथाज्ञानं नह्यभावो मिथ्याज्ञानं तु तन्मतम् ।
तदेव कर्मणां स्वस्मिन्कर्तव्ये सहकारणम् ॥ 24
13.m: Now, if ignorance is not non-existence, but rather is held to be false knowledge, / and that alone is the auxiliary cause of karmas in their own operation, // 24

13.s:
vaktavyaṃ tarhi kiṃ karma yadā sūte svakaṃ phalam /
tadaiva mithyājñānena satā hetutvamāpyate // 25
13.d:
वक्तव्यं तर्हि किं कर्म यदा सूते स्वकं फलम् ।
तदैव मिथ्याज्ञानेन सता हेतुत्वमाप्यते ॥ 25
13.m: then it must be stated: when karma gives birth to its fruit, / is causality obtained only then by existing false knowledge? // 25

13.s:
atha yasminkṣaṇe karma kṛtaṃ tatra svarūpasat /
mithyājñānaṃ yadi tatastādṛśātkamarṇaḥ phalam // 26
13.d:
अथ यस्मिन्क्षणे कर्म कृतं तत्र स्वरूपसत् ।
मिथ्याज्ञानं यदि ततस्तादृशात्कमर्णः फलम् ॥ 26
13.m: Or if false knowledge is real in its own nature at the moment karma is performed, / and then from such karma fruit arises: // 26

13.s:
prākpakṣe pralaye vṛtte prācyasṛṣṭipravartane /
dehādyabhāvānno mithyājñānasya kvāpi saṃbhavaḥ // 27
13.d:
प्राक्पक्षे प्रलये वृत्ते प्राच्यसृष्टिप्रवर्तने ।
देहाद्यभावान्नो मिथ्याज्ञानस्य क्वापि संभवः ॥ 27
13.m: On the former view, when dissolution has occurred, upon the initiation of a subsequent creation, / because of the absence of the body and the rest, false knowledge cannot occur anywhere. // 27

13.s:
uttarasminpunaḥ pakṣe yadā yadyena yatra vā /
kriyate karma tatsarvamajñānasacivaṃ tadā // 28
13.d:
उत्तरस्मिन्पुनः पक्षे यदा यद्येन यत्र वा ।
क्रियते कर्म तत्सर्वमज्ञानसचिवं तदा ॥ 28
13.m: On the latter view, on the other hand, whenever, whatever, by whomsoever, or wherever / action is performed, all of it is then assisted by ignorance. // 28

13.s:
avaśyamiti kasyāpi na karmaprakṣayo bhavet /
yadyapi jñānavānbhūtvā vidhatte karma kiṃcana // 29
13.d:
अवश्यमिति कस्यापि न कर्मप्रक्षयो भवेत् ।
यद्यपि ज्ञानवान्भूत्वा विधत्ते कर्म किंचन ॥ 29
13.m: Inevitably, then, no one's karma would ever be eradicated; / even if, having acquired knowledge, one performs some action, // 29

13.s:
viphalaṃ syāttu tatpūrvakarmarāśau tu kā gatiḥ /
atha pralayakāle 'pi citsvabhāvatvayogataḥ // 30
13.d:
विफलं स्यात्तु तत्पूर्वकर्मराशौ तु का गतिः ।
अथ प्रलयकाले ऽपि चित्स्वभावत्वयोगतः ॥ 30
13.m: and that [action] were fruitless, what would become of the accumulation of prior karma? / If [it is argued that] even at the time of dissolution, by virtue of having the nature of consciousness, // 30

13.s:
aṇūnā saṃbhavatyeva jñānaṃ mithyeti tatkutaḥ /
svabhāvāditi cenmukte śive vā kiṃ tathā nahi // 31
13.d:
अणूना संभवत्येव ज्ञानं मिथ्येति तत्कुतः ।
स्वभावादिति चेन्मुक्ते शिवे वा किं तथा नहि ॥ 31
13.m: false knowledge indeed occurs in bound souls, then from what [does it arise]? / If [it is answered], "from their inherent nature," why then does this not apply to the liberated soul or Śiva? // 31

13.s:
yaccādarśanamākhyātaṃ nimittaṃ pariṇāmini /
pradhāne taddhi saṃkīrṇavaivittayobhayayogataḥ // 32
13.d:
यच्चादर्शनमाख्यातं निमित्तं परिणामिनि ।
प्रधाने तद्धि संकीर्णवैवित्तयोभययोगतः ॥ 32
13.m: And as for the non-discrimination spoken of as the cause in transforming / primal nature, that is indeed because of the conjunction of both indiscriminate and discriminate knowledge: // 32

13.s:
darśanāya pumarthaikayogyatāsacivaṃ dhiyaḥ /
ārabhya sate dharaṇīparyantaṃ tatra yaccitaḥ // 33
13.d:
दर्शनाय पुमर्थैकयोग्यतासचिवं धियः ।
आरभ्य सते धरणीपर्यन्तं तत्र यच्चितः ॥ 33
13.m: assisted by its sole fitness for the human purpose [that leads] to discriminative knowledge, / from intellect down to the earth; and in that regard, consciousness's // 33

13.s:
buddhivṛttyaviśiṣṭatvaṃ puṃsprayāśarprasādataḥ /
prakāśanāddhiyo'rthena saha bhogaḥ sa bhaṇyate // 34
13.d:
बुद्धिवृत्त्यविशिष्टत्वं पुंस्प्रयाशर्प्रसादतः ।
प्रकाशनाद्धियोऽर्थेन सह भोगः स भण्यते ॥ 34
13.m: indistinctness from the modifications of the intellect—because of the illumination of the intellect together with its object / by grace of the exertion of the self—that is termed enjoyment. // 34

13.s:
buddhirevāsmi vikṛtidharmikānyastu ko'pyasau /
madvilakṣaṇa ekātmetyevaṃ vaivi yasaṃvidi // 35
13.d:
बुद्धिरेवास्मि विकृतिधर्मिकान्यस्तु कोऽप्यसौ ।
मद्विलक्षण एकात्मेत्येवं वैवि यसंविदि ॥ 35
13.m: When there is distinctive consciousness such that: "I am the intellect itself, which possesses the quality of transformation, / but that other is someone distinct from me, a singular self," // 35

13.s:
pumarthasya kṛtatvena sahakāriviyogataḥ /
taṃ pumāṃsaṃ prati naiva sūte kiṃtvanyameva hi // 36
13.d:
पुमर्थस्य कृतत्वेन सहकारिवियोगतः ।
तं पुमांसं प्रति नैव सूते किंत्वन्यमेव हि ॥ 36
13.m: since the human purpose is accomplished, through the cessation of the auxiliary factor, / [primal nature] no longer generates [experience] for that self, but only for another. // 36

13.s:
atra puṃso'tha mūlasya dharmo'darśanatā dvayoḥ /
athaveti vikalpo'yamāstāmetattu bhaṇyatām // 37
13.d:
अत्र पुंसोऽथ मूलस्य धर्मोऽदर्शनता द्वयोः ।
अथवेति विकल्पोऽयमास्तामेतत्तु भण्यताम् ॥ 37
13.m: Here, whether non-discrimination is a quality of the self, or of the root [nature], or of both— / let this alternative rest; let this [rather] be stated: // 37

13.s:
bhogo vivekaparyanta iti yattatra ko'vadhiḥ /
vivekalābhe nikhilasūtidṛgyadi sāpi kim // 38
13.d:
भोगो विवेकपर्यन्त इति यत्तत्र कोऽवधिः ।
विवेकलाभे निखिलसूतिदृग्यदि सापि किम् ॥ 38
13.m: As for the statement that "enjoyment lasts until discrimination," what is the limit there? / If, when discrimination is obtained, all manifest production is perceived, then is it even so // 38

13.s:
sāmānyena viśeṣairvā prācye syādekajanmataḥ /
uttare na kadācitsyādbhāvikālasya yogataḥ // 39
13.d:
सामान्येन विशेषैर्वा प्राच्ये स्यादेकजन्मतः ।
उत्तरे न कदाचित्स्याद्भाविकालस्य योगतः ॥ 39
13.m: in a general way, or through particular aspects? In the former case, it would occur in a single birth; / in the latter, it would never occur, on account of future time. // 39

13.s:
kaiścideva viśeṣaiścetsarveṣāṃ yugapadbhavet /
viveko'nādisaṃyogātkā hyanyonyaṃ vicitratā // 40
13.d:
कैश्चिदेव विशेषैश्चेत्सर्वेषां युगपद्भवेत् ।
विवेकोऽनादिसंयोगात्का ह्यन्योन्यं विचित्रता ॥ 40
13.m: If [it were to occur] through just some particular aspects, discrimination would arise / for all [souls] simultaneously from their beginningless conjunction; for what distinct diversity would there be between them? // 40

13.s:
tasmātsāṃkhyadṛśāpīdamajñānaṃ naiva yujyate /
ajñānena vinā bandhamokṣau naiva vyavasthayā // 41
13.d:
तस्मात्सांख्यदृशापीदमज्ञानं नैव युज्यते ।
अज्ञानेन विना बन्धमोक्षौ नैव व्यवस्थया ॥ 41
13.m: Therefore, even according to the Sāṅkhya view, this ignorance is not tenable. / Without ignorance, bondage and liberation are by no means properly established // 41

13.s:
yujyete tacca kathitayuktibhirnopapadyate /
bhāyākarmāṇudevecchāsadbhāve'pi sthite tataḥ // 42
13.d:
युज्येते तच्च कथितयुक्तिभिर्नोपपद्यते ।
भायाकर्माणुदेवेच्छासद्भावेऽपि स्थिते ततः ॥ 42
13.m: as systematic, nor does that [ignorance] hold according to the stated arguments. / Even if the existence of illusion, karma, the soul, and the divine will remains established, therefore, // 42

13.s:
na bandhamokṣayoryogo bhedahetorasaṃbhavāt /
tasmādajñānaśabdena jñatvakartṛtvadharmaṇām // 43
13.d:
न बन्धमोक्षयोर्योगो भेदहेतोरसंभवात् ।
तस्मादज्ञानशब्देन ज्ञत्वकर्तृत्वधर्मणाम् ॥ 43
13.m: the conjunction of bondage and liberation is impossible, because a cause of difference does not exist. / Therefore, by the word "ignorance," a wise person must state that // 43

13.s:
cidaṇūnāmāvaraṇaṃ kiṃcidvācyaṃ vipaścitā /
āvāraṇātmanā siddhaṃ tatsvarūpādabhedavat // 44
13.d:
चिदणूनामावरणं किंचिद्वाच्यं विपश्चिता ।
आवारणात्मना सिद्धं तत्स्वरूपादभेदवत् ॥ 44
13.m: it is a certain covering of the conscious souls that possess the qualities of knowing and acting. / It is established as an obstruction, as it were non-different from its own nature; // 44

13.s:
bhede pramāṇābhāvācca tadekaṃ nikhilātmasu /
tacca kasmātprasūtaṃ syānmāyātaścetkathaṃ nu sā // 45
13.d:
भेदे प्रमाणाभावाच्च तदेकं निखिलात्मसु ।
तच्च कस्मात्प्रसूतं स्यान्मायातश्चेत्कथं नु सा ॥ 45
13.m: and because there is no proof of difference, it is one in all souls. / And from what could it arise? If from māyā, how indeed could she // 45

13.s:
kvacideva suvītaitanna tu muktātmanītyayam /
prācyaḥ paryanuyogaḥ syānnimittaṃ cenna labhyate // 46
13.d:
क्वचिदेव सुवीतैतन्न तु मुक्तात्मनीत्ययम् ।
प्राच्यः पर्यनुयोगः स्यान्निमित्तं चेन्न लभ्यते ॥ 46
13.m: generate it only in some, and not in the liberated soul? / This would be the same prior objection, if no cause is found. // 46

13.s:
utpattyabhāvatastena nityaṃ naca vinaśyati /
tata evaikatāyāṃ cānyātmasādhāraṇatvataḥ // 47
13.d:
उत्पत्त्यभावतस्तेन नित्यं नच विनश्यति ।
तत एवैकतायां चान्यात्मसाधारणत्वतः ॥ 47
13.m: Therefore, from the absence of origination, it is eternal and does not perish; / for that very reason, in its oneness, it is common to other souls. // 47

13.s:
na vāvastvarthakāritvānna cittatsaṃvṛtitvataḥ /
na caitenātmanāṃ yogo hetumāṃstadasaṃbhavāt // 48
13.d:
न वावस्त्वर्थकारित्वान्न चित्तत्संवृतित्वतः ।
न चैतेनात्मनां योगो हेतुमांस्तदसंभवात् ॥ 48
13.m: Nor is it unreal, because it exercises causal efficacy; nor is it conscious, because it obscures that; / nor does the conjunction of souls with it have a cause, because that is impossible. // 48

13.s:
tenaikaṃ vastu sannityaṃ nityasaṃbaddhamātmabhiḥ /
jaḍaṃ malaṃ tadajñānaṃ saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam // 49
13.d:
तेनैकं वस्तु सन्नित्यं नित्यसंबद्धमात्मभिः ।
जडं मलं तदज्ञानं संसाराङ्कुरकारणम् ॥ 49
13.m: Therefore, impurity is a single, real, eternal entity, eternally bound to souls, / insentient, [called] ignorance, the cause of the sprout of saṃsāra. // 49

13.s:
tasya roddhrī yadā śaktirudāste śivaraśmibhiḥ /
tadāṇuḥ spṛśyate spṛṣṭaḥ svake jñānakriye sphuṭe // 50
13.d:
तस्य रोद्ध्री यदा शक्तिरुदास्ते शिवरश्मिभिः ।
तदाणुः स्पृश्यते स्पृष्टः स्वके ज्ञानक्रिये स्फुटे ॥ 50
13.m: When its obstructing power becomes indifferent through the rays of Śiva, / then the soul is touched; once touched, he enters into his own distinct knowing and acting, // 50

13.s:
samāviśedayaṃ sūryakānto'rkeṇeva coditaḥ /
roddhryāśca śaktermādhyasthyatāratamyavaśakramāat // 51
13.d:
समाविशेदयं सूर्यकान्तोऽर्केणेव चोदितः ।
रोद्ध्र्याश्च शक्तेर्माध्यस्थ्यतारतम्यवशक्रमाअत् ॥ 51
13.m: like a sun-gem stimulated by the sun. / And through the succession determined by the degrees of indifference of the obstructing power, // 51

13.s:
vicitratvamataḥ prāhurabhivyaktau svasaṃvidaḥ /
sa eṣa śaktipātākhyaḥ śāstreṣu paribhāṣyate // 52
13.d:
विचित्रत्वमतः प्राहुरभिव्यक्तौ स्वसंविदः ।
स एष शक्तिपाताख्यः शास्त्रेषु परिभाष्यते ॥ 52
13.m: they speak of diversity in the manifestation of one's own consciousness. / This very [process] is designated in the scriptures as the descent of power. // 52

13.s:
atrocyate malastāvaditthameṣa na yujyate /
iti pūrvāhṇike proktaṃ punaruktau tu kiṃ phalam // 53
13.d:
अत्रोच्यते मलस्तावदित्थमेष न युज्यते ।
इति पूर्वाह्णिके प्रोक्तं पुनरुक्तौ तु किं फलम् ॥ 53
13.m: To this, it is replied: First of all, impurity conceived in this way is untenable; / this has been explained in a prior lesson, so what is the point of repetition? // 53

13.s:
malasya pākaḥ ko 'yaṃ syānnāśaśceditarātmanām /
sa eko mala ityukternairmalyamanuṣajyate // 54
13.d:
मलस्य पाकः को ऽयं स्यान्नाशश्चेदितरात्मनाम् ।
स एको मल इत्युक्तेर्नैर्मल्यमनुषज्यते ॥ 54
13.m: What would this "ripening" of impurity be? If it is destruction, / then because it was stated that impurity is one, purity would inevitably follow for all other souls. // 54

13.s:
atha pratyātmaniyato'nādiśca prāgabhāvavat /
malo naśyettathāpyeṣa nāśo yadi sahetukaḥ // 55
13.d:
अथ प्रत्यात्मनियतोऽनादिश्च प्रागभाववत् ।
मलो नश्येत्तथाप्येष नाशो यदि सहेतुकः ॥ 55
13.m: If [you say that] impurity is restricted to each soul and beginningless, like prior non-existence, / and yet perishes, even so, if this destruction has a cause, // 55

13.s:
hetuḥ karmeśvarecchā vā karma tāvanna tādṛśam /
īśvarecchā svatantrā ca kvacideva tathaiva kim // 56
13.d:
हेतुः कर्मेश्वरेच्छा वा कर्म तावन्न तादृशम् ।
ईश्वरेच्छा स्वतन्त्रा च क्वचिदेव तथैव किम् ॥ 56
13.m: the cause would be either karma or the will of the Lord. Karma, first of all, is not of such a kind; / and the will of the Lord is autonomous, so why would it be thus only in some cases? // 56

13.s:
ahetuko'sya nāśaścetprāgevaiṣa vinaśyatu /
kṣaṇāntaraṃ sadṛk sūte iti cetsthirataiva sā // 57
13.d:
अहेतुकोऽस्य नाशश्चेत्प्रागेवैष विनश्यतु ।
क्षणान्तरं सदृक् सूते इति चेत्स्थिरतैव सा ॥ 57
13.m: If its destruction is uncaused, let it perish right from the start! / If [it is argued that] it generates a similar subsequent moment, that is simply permanence. // 57

13.s:
na ca nityasya bhāvasya hetvanāyattajanmanaḥ /
nāśo dṛṣṭaḥ prāgabhāvastvavastviti tathāstu saḥ // 58
13.d:
न च नित्यस्य भावस्य हेत्वनायत्तजन्मनः ।
नाशो दृष्टः प्रागभावस्त्ववस्त्विति तथास्तु सः ॥ 58
13.m: Nor has destruction ever been seen of an eternal real entity whose birth is independent of causes; / but prior non-existence is a non-entity, so let that be so. // 58

13.s:
athāsya pāko nāmaiṣa svaśaktipratibaddhatā /
sarvānprati tathaiṣa syādruddhaśaktirviṣāgnivat // 59
13.d:
अथास्य पाको नामैष स्वशक्तिप्रतिबद्धता ।
सर्वान्प्रति तथैष स्याद्रुद्धशक्तिर्विषाग्निवत् ॥ 59
13.m: Now, if this so-called "ripening" of it is the obstruction of its own power, / it would be likewise obstructed in its power toward everyone, like poison or fire; // 59

13.s:
punarudbhūtaśaktau ca svakāryaṃ syādviṣāgnivat /
muktā api na muktāḥ syuḥ śaktiṃ cāsya na manmahe // 60
13.d:
पुनरुद्भूतशक्तौ च स्वकार्यं स्याद्विषाग्निवत् ।
मुक्ता अपि न मुक्ताः स्युः शक्तिं चास्य न मन्महे ॥ 60
13.m: and when its power arises again, its effect would occur, as with poison or fire; / even the liberated would not be liberated, and we do not accept that it has power. // 60

13.s:
roddhrīti cetkasya nṛṇāṃ jñatvakartṛtvayoryadi /
sadbhāvamātrādroddhṛtve śivamuktāṇvasaṃbhavaḥ // 61
13.d:
रोद्ध्रीति चेत्कस्य नृणां ज्ञत्वकर्तृत्वयोर्यदि ।
सद्भावमात्राद्रोद्धृत्वे शिवमुक्ताण्वसंभवः ॥ 61
13.m: If [it is called] "obstructing," of what? If of men's knowing and acting, / then if it were an obstructor by its mere existence, Śiva, the liberated soul, and the bound soul would be impossible. // 61

13.s:
saṃnidhānātiriktaṃ ca na kiṃcitkurute malaḥ /
ātmanā pariṇāmitvādanityatvaprasaṅgataḥ // 62
13.d:
संनिधानातिरिक्तं च न किंचित्कुरुते मलः ।
आत्मना परिणामित्वादनित्यत्वप्रसङ्गतः ॥ 62
13.m: And impurity produces nothing apart from [its] proximity, / because of the undesirable consequence of its changing and being non-eternal by itself. // 62

13.s:
jñatvakartṛtvamātraṃ ca pudgalā na tadāśrayāḥ /
taccedāvāritaṃ hanta rūpanāśaḥ prasajyate // 63
13.d:
ज्ञत्वकर्तृत्वमात्रं च पुद्गला न तदाश्रयाः ।
तच्चेदावारितं हन्त रूपनाशः प्रसज्यते ॥ 63
13.m: Moreover, souls are simply knowing and acting; they are not the substrata of them. / If that is covered, alas, the destruction of their very nature would follow! // 63

13.s:
āvāraṇaṃ cādṛśyatvaṃ na ca tadvastuno'nyatām /
karoti ghaṭavajjñānaṃ nāvarītuṃ ca śakyate // 64
13.d:
आवारणं चादृश्यत्वं न च तद्वस्तुनोऽन्यताम् ।
करोति घटवज्ज्ञानं नावरीतुं च शक्यते ॥ 64
13.m: And covering is being invisible, and that does not make an entity something else, / like a pot; nor can knowledge be covered. // 64

13.s:
jñānenāvaraṇīyena tadevāvaraṇaṃ katham /
na jñāyate tathā ca syādāvṛtirnāmamātrataḥ // 65
13.d:
ज्ञानेनावरणीयेन तदेवावरणं कथम् ।
न ज्ञायते तथा च स्यादावृतिर्नाममात्रतः ॥ 65
13.m: How could that very covering not be known by the knowledge that is to be covered? / And so covering would exist in name only. // 65

13.s:
roddhryāśca śakteḥ kastasya pratibandhaka īśvaraḥ /
yadyapekṣāvirahitastatra prāgdattamuttaram // 66
13.d:
रोद्ध्र्याश्च शक्तेः कस्तस्य प्रतिबन्धक ईश्वरः ।
यद्यपेक्षाविरहितस्तत्र प्राग्दत्तमुत्तरम् ॥ 66
13.m: And as for the obstructing power: who is its preventer? If it is the Lord / without dependence [on anything], the answer has already been given previously to that. // 66

13.s:
karmasāmyamapekṣyātha tasyecchā saṃpravartate /
tasyāpi rūpaṃ vaktavyaṃ samatā karmaṇāṃ hi kā // 67
13.d:
कर्मसाम्यमपेक्ष्याथ तस्येच्छा संप्रवर्तते ।
तस्यापि रूपं वक्तव्यं समता कर्मणां हि का ॥ 67
13.m: If His will operates in dependence on the equalization of karma, / the nature of that too must be explained; for what is the equality of karmas? // 67

13.s:
bhogaparyāyamāhātmyātkāle kvāpi phalaṃ prati /
virodhātkarmaṇī ruddhe tiṣṭhataḥ sāmyamīdṛśam // 68
13.d:
भोगपर्यायमाहात्म्यात्काले क्वापि फलं प्रति ।
विरोधात्कर्मणी रुद्धे तिष्ठतः साम्यमीदृशम् ॥ 68
13.m: If, by the power of the cycle of enjoyment, two karmas stand mutually blocked at some time / regarding their fruit due to conflict, such is equality. // 68

13.s:
taṃ ca kālāṃśakaṃ devaḥ sarvajño vīkṣya taṃ malam /
runddhe lakṣyaḥ sa kālaśca sukhaduḥkhādivarjanaiḥ // 69
13.d:
तं च कालांशकं देवः सर्वज्ञो वीक्ष्य तं मलम् ।
रुन्द्धे लक्ष्यः स कालश्च सुखदुःखादिवर्जनैः ॥ 69
13.m: And the omniscient God, perceiving that portion of time, blocks that impurity; / and that time is indicated by the cessation of pleasure, pain, and the rest. // 69

13.s:
naitatkramikasaṃśuddhavyāmiśrākārakarmabhiḥ /
tathaiva deye svaphale keyamanyonyaroddhṛtā // 70
13.d:
नैतत्क्रमिकसंशुद्धव्यामिश्राकारकर्मभिः ।
तथैव देये स्वफले केयमन्योन्यरोद्धृता ॥ 70
13.m: This is not so. When karmas that are successive, purely good, or mixed / must yield their own fruit just as they are, what is this mutual obstruction? // 70

13.s:
rodhe tayośca jātyāyurapi na syādataḥ patet /
deho bhogadayoreva nirodha iti cennanu // 71
13.d:
रोधे तयोश्च जात्यायुरपि न स्यादतः पतेत् ।
देहो भोगदयोरेव निरोध इति चेन्ननु ॥ 71
13.m: And if the two are obstructed, there would not even be birth and lifespan; hence the body / would fall. If it is objected that there is obstruction only of the two [karmas] giving enjoyment, surely: // 71

13.s:
jātyāyuṣpradakarmāṃśasaṃnidhau yadi śaṃkaraḥ /
malaṃ runddhe bhogadātuḥ karmaṇaḥ kiṃ bibheti saḥ // 72
13.d:
जात्यायुष्प्रदकर्मांशसंनिधौ यदि शंकरः ।
मलं रुन्द्धे भोगदातुः कर्मणः किं बिभेति सः ॥ 72
