13.m: If Śaṃkara blocks impurity in the presence of the portion of karma that bestows birth and lifespan, / does He fear the karma that bestows enjoyment? // 72

13.s:
śataśo'pi hlādatāpaśūnyāṃ saṃcinvate daśām /
na ca bhaktirasāveśamiti bhūmnā vilokitam // 73
13.d:
शतशोऽपि ह्लादतापशून्यां संचिन्वते दशाम् ।
न च भक्तिरसावेशमिति भूम्ना विलोकितम् ॥ 73
13.m: Even hundreds of times, people experience a state devoid of both joy and torment, / and yet no immersion in the rasa of devotion is seen to occur frequently.

13.s:
athāpi kālamāhātmyamapekṣya parameśvaraḥ /
tathā karoti vaktavyaṃ kālo'sau kīdṛśastviti // 74
13.d:
अथापि कालमाहात्म्यमपेक्ष्य परमेश्वरः ।
तथा करोति वक्तव्यं कालोऽसौ कीदृशस्त्विति ॥ 74
13.m: Moreover, if the Supreme Lord acts thus in dependence upon the power of time, / it must be explained: what kind of time is this?

13.s:
kiṃ cānādirayaṃ bhogaḥ karmānādi sapudgalam /
tataśca bhogaparyāyakālaḥ sarvasya niḥsamaḥ // 75
13.d:
किं चानादिरयं भोगः कर्मानादि सपुद्गलम् ।
ततश्च भोगपर्यायकालः सर्वस्य निःसमः ॥ 75
13.m: Furthermore, this enjoyment is beginningless; karma together with the individual soul is beginningless; / and therefore, the time of the cycle of enjoyment is unequal for everyone.

13.s:
ādimattve hi kasyāpi vargādasmādbhavediyam /
vaicitrī bhuktametena kalpametena tu dvayam // 76
13.d:
आदिमत्त्वे हि कस्यापि वर्गादस्माद्भवेदियम् ।
वैचित्री भुक्तमेतेन कल्पमेतेन तु द्वयम् ॥ 76
13.m: For if it had a beginning, this diversity might arise from this group: / 'A kalpa was experienced by this one, but two [kalpas] by that one;

13.s:
iyato bhogaparyāyātsyātsāmyaṃ karmaṇāmiti /
anena nayabījena manye vaicitryakāraṇam // 77
13.d:
इयतो भोगपर्यायात्स्यात्साम्यं कर्मणामिति ।
अनेन नयबीजेन मन्ये वैचित्र्यकारणम् ॥ 77
13.m: from such a cycle of enjoyment, an equality of karmas would arise.' / Because of this principle, I think that the cause of diversity

13.s:
jagataḥ karma yatklaptaṃ tattathā nāvakalpate /
anādimalasaṃcchannā aṇavo dṛkkriyātmanā // 78
13.d:
जगतः कर्म यत्क्लप्तं तत्तथा नावकल्पते ।
अनादिमलसंच्छन्ना अणवो दृक्क्रियात्मना ॥ 78
13.m: of the universe, which is assumed to be karma, is not logically tenable in that way. / Covered by beginningless impurity, souls, in their nature of vision and action,

13.s:
sarve tulyāḥ kathaṃ citrāṃ śritāḥ karmaparamparām /
bhogalolikayā cetsā vicitreti kuto nanu // 79
13.d:
सर्वे तुल्याः कथं चित्रां श्रिताः कर्मपरम्पराम् ।
भोगलोलिकया चेत्सा विचित्रेति कुतो ननु ॥ 79
13.m: are all equal; how did they resort to a variegated succession of karmas? / If it is said: 'through the craving for enjoyment', why, indeed, is that [craving] variegated?

13.s:
anādi karmasaṃskāravaicitryāditi cetpunaḥ /
vācyaṃ tadeva vaicitryaṃ kuto niyatirāgayoḥ // 80
13.d:
अनादि कर्मसंस्कारवैचित्र्यादिति चेत्पुनः ।
वाच्यं तदेव वैचित्र्यं कुतो नियतिरागयोः ॥ 80
13.m: If it is claimed that it is due to the diversity of beginningless karmic impressions, then again / it must be stated whence arises that very diversity of niyati and rāga.

13.s:
mahimā cedayaṃ tau kiṃ nāsamañjasyabhāginau /
īśvarecchānapekṣā tu bhedaheturna kalpate // 81
13.d:
महिमा चेदयं तौ किं नासमञ्जस्यभागिनौ ।
ईश्वरेच्छानपेक्षा तु भेदहेतुर्न कल्पते ॥ 81
13.m: If this is their intrinsic power, would they not both be subject to inconsistency? / But an explanation without reference to the will of the Lord cannot account for differentiation.

13.s:
athānāditvamātreṇa yuktihīnena sādhyate /
vyavastheyamalaṃ tarhi malenāstu vṛthāmunā // 82
13.d:
अथानादित्वमात्रेण युक्तिहीनेन साध्यते ।
व्यवस्थेयमलं तर्हि मलेनास्तु वृथामुना ॥ 82
13.m: Now, if this orderly arrangement is established merely by beginninglessness devoid of reasoning, / then enough of this useless impurity!

13.s:
tathāhi karma tāvanno yāvanmāyā na pudgale /
vyāpriyeta na cāhetustadvṛttistanmito malaḥ // 83
13.d:
तथाहि कर्म तावन्नो यावन्माया न पुद्गले ।
व्याप्रियेत न चाहेतुस्तद्वृत्तिस्तन्मितो मलः ॥ 83
13.m: To explain: karma does not exist until māyā / operates in the individual soul; and its operation is not uncaused, so impurity is assumed on that account.

13.s:
itthaṃ ca kalpite māyākārye karmaṇi hetutām /
anādi karma cedgacchetkiṃ malasyopakalpanam // 84
13.d:
इत्थं च कल्पिते मायाकार्ये कर्मणि हेतुताम् ।
अनादि कर्म चेद्गच्छेत्किं मलस्योपकल्पनम् ॥ 84
13.m: And in this way, if beginningless karma should become the cause / in karma assumed to be an effect of māyā, why imagine impurity?

13.s:
nanu mābhūnmalastarhi citrākāreṣu karmasu /
santatyāvartamāneṣu vyavasthā na prakalpate // 85
13.d:
ननु माभून्मलस्तर्हि चित्राकारेषु कर्मसु ।
सन्तत्यावर्तमानेषु व्यवस्था न प्रकल्पते ॥ 85
13.m: Objection: let there be no impurity; but then among karmas of diverse forms / revolving continuously, an orderly arrangement cannot be established.

13.s:
ādau madhye ca citratvātkarmaṇāṃ na yathā samaḥ /
ātmākāro'pi ko'pyeṣa bhāvikāle tathā bhavet // 86
13.d:
आदौ मध्ये च चित्रत्वात्कर्मणां न यथा समः ।
आत्माकारोऽपि कोऽप्येष भाविकाले तथा भवेत् ॥ 86
13.m: Because karmas are diverse in the beginning and in the middle, just as there is no uniform / state of the self, so too would it be in future time.

13.s:
itthamucchinna evāyaṃ bandhamokṣādikaḥ kramaḥ /
ajñānādbandhanaṃ mokṣo jñānāditi parīkṣitam // 87
13.d:
इत्थमुच्छिन्न एवायं बन्धमोक्षादिकः क्रमः ।
अज्ञानाद्बन्धनं मोक्षो ज्ञानादिति परीक्षितम् ॥ 87
13.m: In this way, this order of bondage, liberation, and so forth is completely severed. / [Answer:] It has been examined that bondage is from ignorance, and liberation is from knowledge.

13.s:
virodhe svaphale caite karmaṇī samaye kvacit /
udāsāte yadi tataḥ karmaitatpratibudhyatām // 88
13.d:
विरोधे स्वफले चैते कर्मणी समये क्वचित् ।
उदासाते यदि ततः कर्मैतत्प्रतिबुध्यताम् ॥ 88
13.m: If at some time, in opposition regarding their own fruits, these two karmas / become neutral, then let this karma be understood [as neutral].

13.s:
śivaśaktinipātasya ko'vakāśastu tāvatā /
kvāpi kāle tayoretadaudāsīnyaṃ yadā tataḥ // 89
13.d:
शिवशक्तिनिपातस्य कोऽवकाशस्तु तावता ।
क्वापि काले तयोरेतदौदासीन्यं यदा ततः ॥ 89
13.m: What room, however, is there on that account for the descent of the power of Śiva? / When at some time this neutrality occurs between the two, from that point,

13.s:
kālāntare tayostadvadvirodhasyānivṛttitaḥ /
ataśca na phaletānte tābhyāṃ karmāntaraṇi ca // 90
13.d:
कालान्तरे तयोस्तद्वद्विरोधस्यानिवृत्तितः ।
अतश्च न फलेतान्ते ताभ्यां कर्मान्तरणि च ॥ 90
13.m: at another time, their opposition does not cease in the same way; / and therefore at the end they would not bear fruit, and other karmas,

13.s:
ruddhāni prāptakālatvādgatābhyāmupabhogyatām /
evaṃ sadaiva vārtāyāṃ dehapāte tathaiva ca // 91
13.d:
रुद्धानि प्राप्तकालत्वाद्गताभ्यामुपभोग्यताम् ।
एवं सदैव वार्तायां देहपाते तथैव च ॥ 91
13.m: obstructed because their time had arrived, having become objects of experience— / this being the case continually, at the fall of the body, just in that way,

13.s:
jāte vimokṣa ityāstāṃ śaktipātādikalpanā /
athodāsīnatatkarmadvayayogakṣaṇāntare // 92
13.d:
जाते विमोक्ष इत्यास्तां शक्तिपातादिकल्पना ।
अथोदासीनतत्कर्मद्वययोगक्षणान्तरे ॥ 92
13.m: once liberation had arisen, let the assumption of the descent of power and so forth be abandoned! / Now, in the subsequent moment after the conjunction of those two neutral karmas,

13.s:
karmāntaraṃ phalaṃ sūte tatkṣaṇe'pi tathā na kim /
kṣaṇāntare'tha te eva pratibandhavivarjite // 93
13.d:
कर्मान्तरं फलं सूते तत्क्षणेऽपि तथा न किम् ।
क्षणान्तरेऽथ ते एव प्रतिबन्धविवर्जिते ॥ 93
13.m: another karma produces fruit; why not in that very moment as well? / Or if in another moment those two very [karmas], devoid of obstruction,

13.s:
phalataḥ pratibandhasya varjanaṃ kiṃkṛtaṃ tayoḥ /
karmasāmyaṃ svarūpeṇa na ca tattāratamyabhāk // 94
13.d:
फलतः प्रतिबन्धस्य वर्जनं किंकृतं तयोः ।
कर्मसाम्यं स्वरूपेण न च तत्तारतम्यभाक् ॥ 94
13.m: bear fruit, what caused their freedom from obstruction? / Karmic equality is intrinsic, and it does not possess gradations.

13.s:
na śiveccheti tatkārye śaktipāte na tadbhavet /
tirobhāvaśca nāmāyaṃ sa kasmādudbhavetpunaḥ // 95
13.d:
न शिवेच्छेति तत्कार्ये शक्तिपाते न तद्भवेत् ।
तिरोभावश्च नामायं स कस्मादुद्भवेत्पुनः ॥ 95
13.m: It is not the will of Śiva; therefore, that [will] cannot exist in its effect, the descent of power. / And this so-called concealment—from what would it arise again?

13.s:
karmasāmyena yatkṛtyaṃ prāgevaitatkṛtaṃ kila /
hetutve ceśvarecchāyā vācyaṃ pūrvavadeva tu // 96
13.d:
कर्मसाम्येन यत्कृत्यं प्रागेवैतत्कृतं किल ।
हेतुत्वे चेश्वरेच्छाया वाच्यं पूर्ववदेव तु ॥ 96
13.m: What was to be done through karmic equality had indeed already been done before. / And if the will of the Lord is the cause, it must be stated just as before.

13.s:
etenānye'pi ye'pekṣyā īśecchāyāṃ prakalpitāḥ /
dhvastāste'pi hi nityānyahetvahetvādidūṣaṇāt // 97
13.d:
एतेनान्येऽपि येऽपेक्ष्या ईशेच्छायां प्रकल्पिताः ।
ध्वस्तास्तेऽपि हि नित्यान्यहेत्वहेत्वादिदूषणात् ॥ 97
13.m: By this, other factors that have been postulated as requisites for the Lord's will / are also destroyed, due to defects such as eternal or non-eternal causes and non-causes.

13.s:
vairāgyaṃ bhogavairasyaṃ dharmaḥ ko'pi vivekitā /
satsaṅgaḥ parameśānapūjādyabhyāsanityatā // 98
13.d:
वैराग्यं भोगवैरस्यं धर्मः कोऽपि विवेकिता ।
सत्सङ्गः परमेशानपूजाद्यभ्यासनित्यता ॥ 98
13.m: Detachment, distaste for enjoyment, some religious merit, discriminative discernment, / association with the good, constancy in the practice of worship of the Supreme Lord and so forth,

13.s:
āpatprāptistannirīkṣā dehe kiṃcicca lakṣaṇam /
śāstrasevā bhogasaṃghapūrṇatā jñānamaiśvaram // 99
13.d:
आपत्प्राप्तिस्तन्निरीक्षा देहे किंचिच्च लक्षणम् ।
शास्त्रसेवा भोगसंघपूर्णता ज्ञानमैश्वरम् ॥ 99
13.m: falling into calamity, inspecting it, some bodily sign, / study of scriptures, fullness of the host of enjoyments, divine knowledge—

13.s:
ityapekṣyaṃ yadīśasya dūṣyametacca pūrvavat /
vyabhicāraśca sāmastyavyastatvābhyāṃ svarūpataḥ // 100
13.d:
इत्यपेक्ष्यं यदीशस्य दूष्यमेतच्च पूर्ववत् ।
व्यभिचारश्च सामस्त्यव्यस्तत्वाभ्यां स्वरूपतः ॥ 100
13.m: if these are what is required by the Lord, this is refutable just as before, / and because of their inconsistency, whether taken collectively or individually in their essential nature,

13.s:
anyonyānupraveśaścānupapattiśca bhūyasī /
tasmānna manmahe ko'yaṃ śaktipātavidheḥ kramaḥ // 101
13.d:
अन्योन्यानुप्रवेशश्चानुपपत्तिश्च भूयसी ।
तस्मान्न मन्महे कोऽयं शक्तिपातविधेः क्रमः ॥ 101
13.m: their mutual interpenetration, and abundant logical untenability. / Therefore, we do not accept this: what is this sequential rule for the descent of power?

13.s:
itthaṃ bhrāntiviṣāveśamūrcchānirmokadāyinīm /
śrīśaṃbhuvadanodgīrṇāṃ vacmyāgamamahauṣadhīm // 102
13.d:
इत्थं भ्रान्तिविषावेशमूर्च्छानिर्मोकदायिनीम् ।
श्रीशंभुवदनोद्गीर्णां वच्म्यागममहौषधीम् ॥ 102
13.m: Thus I declare the great medicine of the scriptures, uttered from the mouth of venerable Śambhu, / which grants release from the swoon caused by the entry of the poison of delusion.

13.s:
devaḥ svatantraścidrūpaḥ prakāśātmā svabhāvataḥ /
rūpapracchādanakrīḍāyogādaṇuranekakaḥ // 103
13.d:
देवः स्वतन्त्रश्चिद्रूपः प्रकाशात्मा स्वभावतः ।
रूपप्रच्छादनक्रीडायोगादणुरनेककः ॥ 103
13.m: The Lord is autonomous, of the nature of consciousness, luminous by His own nature; / through connection with the play of concealing His nature, He becomes many an individual soul.

13.s:
sa svayaṃ kalpitākāravikalpātmakakarmabhiḥ /
badhnātyātmānameveha svātantryāditi varṇitam // 104
13.d:
स स्वयं कल्पिताकारविकल्पात्मककर्मभिः ।
बध्नात्यात्मानमेवेह स्वातन्त्र्यादिति वर्णितम् ॥ 104
13.m: Through karmas consisting of conceptual constructs whose forms are imagined by Himself, / He binds Himself alone here out of His absolute autonomy; so it has been described.

13.s:
svātantryamahimaivāyaṃ devasya yadasau punaḥ /
svaṃ rūpaṃ pariśuddhaṃ satspṛśatyapyaṇutāmayaḥ // 105
13.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यमहिमैवायं देवस्य यदसौ पुनः ।
स्वं रूपं परिशुद्धं सत्स्पृशत्यप्यणुतामयः ॥ 105
13.m: This is the very majesty of the Lord's absolute autonomy: that He, / though full of individuality, again touches His own nature which is utterly pure.

13.s:
na vācyaṃ tu kathaṃ nāma kasmiṃścitpuṃsyasau tathā /
nahi nāma pumānkaścidyasminparyanuyujyate // 106
13.d:
न वाच्यं तु कथं नाम कस्मिंश्चित्पुंस्यसौ तथा ।
नहि नाम पुमान्कश्चिद्यस्मिन्पर्यनुयुज्यते ॥ 106
13.m: It should not be asked, however: 'Why indeed [does He act] thus in a certain person?' / For there is indeed no person concerning whom a question could be raised.

13.s:
deva eva tathāsau cet svarūpaṃ cāsya tādṛśam /
tādṛkprathāsvabhāvasya svabhāve kānuyojyatā // 107
13.d:
देव एव तथासौ चेत् स्वरूपं चास्य तादृशम् ।
तादृक्प्रथास्वभावस्य स्वभावे कानुयोज्यता ॥ 107
13.m: If that [person] is the Lord Himself thus, and His nature is such, / what questioning can there be regarding the nature of one whose nature is such manifestation?

13.s:
āhāsmatparameṣṭhī ca śivadṛṣṭau gurūttamaḥ /
pañcaprakārakṛtyoktiśivatvānnijakarmaṇe // 108
13.d:
आहास्मत्परमेष्ठी च शिवदृष्टौ गुरूत्तमः ।
पञ्चप्रकारकृत्योक्तिशिवत्वान्निजकर्मणे ॥ 108
13.m: And our supreme guru, the most excellent master, said in the Śivadṛṣṭi: / 'Because of His Śiva-nature, expressed as fivefold activity, for His own action

13.s:
pravṛttasya nimittānāmapareṣāṃ kva mārgaṇam /
channasvarūpatābhāse puṃsi yadyādṛśaṃ phalam // 109
13.d:
प्रवृत्तस्य निमित्तानामपरेषां क्व मार्गणम् ।
छन्नस्वरूपताभासे पुंसि यद्यादृशं फलम् ॥ 109
13.m: where is the search for other causes when He has engaged in it?' / In a person whose nature appears concealed, whatever kind of fruit [arises],

13.s:
tatrāṇoḥ sata evāsti svātantryaṃ karmatohi tat /
īśvarasya ca yā svātmatirodhitsā nimittatām // 110
13.d:
तत्राणोः सत एवास्ति स्वातन्त्र्यं कर्मतोहि तत् ।
ईश्वरस्य च या स्वात्मतिरोधित्सा निमित्तताम् ॥ 110
13.m: there exists the absolute autonomy of the soul alone, because it arises from karma; / and the Lord's desire to conceal Himself, which assumes causality,

13.s:
sābhyeti karmamalayorato'nādivyavasthitiḥ /
tirodhiḥ pūrṇarūpasyāpūrṇatvaṃ tacca pūraṇam // 111
13.d:
साभ्येति कर्ममलयोरतोऽनादिव्यवस्थितिः ।
तिरोधिः पूर्णरूपस्यापूर्णत्वं तच्च पूरणम् ॥ 111
13.m: attains the status of karma and impurity; hence the beginningless orderly arrangement. / Concealment is the incompleteness of that which has a complete nature, and that fullness [becomes limited]

13.s:
prati bhinnena bhāvena spṛhāto lolikā malaḥ /
viśuddhasvaprakāśātmaśivarūpatayā vinā // 112
13.d:
प्रति भिन्नेन भावेन स्पृहातो लोलिका मलः ।
विशुद्धस्वप्रकाशात्मशिवरूपतया विना ॥ 112
13.m: towards differentiated entities through desire; therefore, craving is impurity. / Without the form of Śiva, whose nature is pure self-luminosity,

13.s:
na kiṃcidyujyate tena heturatra maheśvaraḥ /
itthaṃ sṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsatraye māyāmapekṣate // 113
13.d:
न किंचिद्युज्यते तेन हेतुरत्र महेश्वरः ।
इत्थं सृष्टिस्थितिध्वंसत्रये मायामपेक्षते ॥ 113
13.m: nothing is possible; therefore, the Great Lord is the cause in this case. / In this way, with regard to the triad of emission, maintenance, and destruction, He relies on māyā,

13.s:
kṛtyai malaṃ tathā karma śivecchaiveti susthitam /
yattu kasmiṃścana śivaḥ svena rūpeṇa bhāsate // 114
13.d:
कृत्यै मलं तथा कर्म शिवेच्छैवेति सुस्थितम् ।
यत्तु कस्मिंश्चन शिवः स्वेन रूपेण भासते ॥ 114
13.m: and for His activities, upon impurity and karma—thus it is well established that it is solely Śiva's will. / But that Śiva shines in His own nature in a certain person—

13.s:
tatrāsya nāṇuge tāvadapekṣye malakarmaṇī /
aṇusvarūpatāhānau tadgataṃ hetutāṃ katham // 115
13.d:
तत्रास्य नाणुगे तावदपेक्ष्ये मलकर्मणी ।
अणुस्वरूपताहानौ तद्गतं हेतुतां कथम् ॥ 115
13.m: in that case, His impurity and karma belonging to the individual soul are not to be depended upon at all; / when the individual soul's nature is destroyed, how could that which belongs to it become a cause?

13.s:
vrajenmāyānapekṣatvamata evopapādayet /
tena śuddhaḥ svaprakāśaḥ śiva evātra kāraṇam // 116
13.d:
व्रजेन्मायानपेक्षत्वमत एवोपपादयेत् ।
तेन शुद्धः स्वप्रकाशः शिव एवात्र कारणम् ॥ 116
13.m: Hence, He would demonstrate independence from māyā. / Therefore, pure, self-luminous Śiva alone is the cause in this matter.

13.s:
sa ca svācchandyamātreṇa tāratamyaprakāśakaḥ /
kulajātivapuṣkarmavayonuṣṭhānasaṃpadaḥ // 117
13.d:
स च स्वाच्छन्द्यमात्रेण तारतम्यप्रकाशकः ।
कुलजातिवपुष्कर्मवयोनुष्ठानसंपदः ॥ 117
13.m: And He, merely through His absolute freedom, manifests gradations [of that descent]. / Without dependence upon clan, caste, body, karma, age, or wealth of ritual performance,

13.s:
anapekṣya śive bhaktiḥ śaktipāto'phalārthinām /
yā phalārthitayā bhaktiḥ sā karmādyamapekṣate // 118
13.d:
अनपेक्ष्य शिवे भक्तिः शक्तिपातोऽफलार्थिनाम् ।
या फलार्थितया भक्तिः सा कर्माद्यमपेक्षते ॥ 118
13.m: devotion to Śiva is the descent of power for those who do not desire fruit. / That devotion which has desire for fruit depends upon karma and the like;

13.s:
tato'tra syātphale bhedo nāpavarge tvasau tathā /
bhogāpavargadvitayābhisaṃdhāturapi sphuṭam // 119
13.d:
ततोऽत्र स्यात्फले भेदो नापवर्गे त्वसौ तथा ।
भोगापवर्गद्वितयाभिसंधातुरपि स्फुटम् ॥ 119
13.m: therefore, there may be difference in fruit in that case, but not so in liberation, / clearly even for one who aims at both enjoyment and liberation.

13.s:
prāgbhāge'pekṣate karma citratvānnottare punaḥ /
anābhāsitarūpo'pi tadābhāsitayeva yat // 120
13.d:
प्राग्भागेऽपेक्षते कर्म चित्रत्वान्नोत्तरे पुनः ।
अनाभासितरूपोऽपि तदाभासितयेव यत् ॥ 120
13.m: Karma depends on it in the prior stage, but due to variety not in the subsequent stage; / because even one whose nature is not manifested appears as though manifested by it. // 120

13.s:
sthitvā mantrādi saṃgṛhya tyajetso'sya tirobhavaḥ /
śrīsāraśāstre bhagavānvastvetatsamabhāṣata // 121
13.d:
स्थित्वा मन्त्रादि संगृह्य त्यजेत्सोऽस्य तिरोभवः ।
श्रीसारशास्त्रे भगवान्वस्त्वेतत्समभाषत ॥ 121
13.m: Remaining [in worldly existence], grasping mantra and the rest, he may abandon it: this is his concealment. / In the venerable Sāraśāstra, the Lord explained this reality:

13.s:
dharmādharmātmakairbhāvairanekairveṣṭayetsvayam /
asandehaṃ svamātmānamavīcyādiśivāntake // 122
13.d:
धर्माधर्मात्मकैर्भावैरनेकैर्वेष्टयेत्स्वयम् ।
असन्देहं स्वमात्मानमवीच्यादिशिवान्तके ॥ 122
13.m: "He envelops Himself, undoubtedly, with manifold states / consisting of merit and demerit, extending from Avīci up to Śiva.

13.s:
tadvacchaktisamūhena sa eva tu viveṣṭayet /
svayaṃ badhnāti deveśaḥ svayaṃ caiva vimuñcati // 123
13.d:
तद्वच्छक्तिसमूहेन स एव तु विवेष्टयेत् ।
स्वयं बध्नाति देवेशः स्वयं चैव विमुञ्चति ॥ 123
13.m: In the same way, He alone indeed envelops Himself with the host of powers; / the Lord of gods binds Himself, and He alone liberates Himself.

13.s:
svayaṃ bhoktā svayaṃ jñātā svayaṃ caivopalakṣayet /
svayaṃ bhuktiśca muktiśca svayaṃ devī svayaṃ prabhuḥ // 124
13.d:
स्वयं भोक्ता स्वयं ज्ञाता स्वयं चैवोपलक्षयेत् ।
स्वयं भुक्तिश्च मुक्तिश्च स्वयं देवी स्वयं प्रभुः ॥ 124
13.m: He alone is the enjoyer, He alone the knower, and He alone observes; / He alone is enjoyment and liberation, He alone the Goddess, He alone the Lord.

13.s:
svayamekākṣarā caiva yathoṣmā kṛṣṇavartmanaḥ /
vastūktamatra svātantryātsvātmarūpaprakāśanam // 125
13.d:
स्वयमेकाक्षरा चैव यथोष्मा कृष्णवर्त्मनः ।
वस्तूक्तमत्र स्वातन्त्र्यात्स्वात्मरूपप्रकाशनम् ॥ 125
13.m: And She is inherently monosyllabic, just like the heat of fire." / What is stated here as reality is the illumination of one's own nature through absolute autonomy.

13.s:
śrīmanniśākule'pyuktaṃ mithyābhāvitacetasaḥ /
malamāyāvicāreṇa kliśyante svalpabuddhayaḥ // 126
13.d:
श्रीमन्निशाकुलेऽप्युक्तं मिथ्याभावितचेतसः ।
मलमायाविचारेण क्लिश्यन्ते स्वल्पबुद्धयः ॥ 126
13.m: In the venerable Niśākula it is also stated: "Those whose minds are falsely conditioned, / being of little intelligence, suffer through the consideration of impurity and māyā.

13.s:
sphaṭikopalago reṇuḥ kiṃ tasya kurutāṃ priye /
vyomnīva nīlaṃ hi malaṃ malaśaṃkāṃ tatastyajet // 127
13.d:
स्फटिकोपलगो रेणुः किं तस्य कुरुतां प्रिये ।
व्योम्नीव नीलं हि मलं मलशंकां ततस्त्यजेत् ॥ 127
13.m: O dear one, what does the dust on a crystal stone do to it? / For impurity is like blueness in the sky; therefore one should abandon the fear of impurity."

13.s:
śrīmānvidyāguruścāha pramāṇastutidarśane /
dharmādharmavyāptivināśāntarakāle śakteḥ pāto gāhanikairyaḥ pratipannaḥ // 128
13.d:
श्रीमान्विद्यागुरुश्चाह प्रमाणस्तुतिदर्शने ।
धर्माधर्मव्याप्तिविनाशान्तरकाले शक्तेः पातो गाहनिकैर्यः प्रतिपन्नः ॥ 128
13.m: And the venerable Vidyāguru said in the Pramāṇastutidarśana: / "The descent of power that is accepted by the profound thinkers at the time following the destruction of the pervasion of merit and demerit—

13.s:
taṃ svecchātaḥ saṃgiramāṇāḥ stavakādyāḥ svātantryaṃ tattvayyanapekṣaṃ kathayeyuḥ /
tāratamyaprakāśo yastīvramadhyamamandatāḥ // 129
13.d:
तं स्वेच्छातः संगिरमाणाः स्तवकाद्याः स्वातन्त्र्यं तत्त्वय्यनपेक्षं कथयेयुः ।
तारतम्यप्रकाशो यस्तीव्रमध्यममन्दताः ॥ 129
13.m: those such as praise-singers, proclaiming it according to their own wish, / would describe that as an absolute autonomy in You that is independent [of conditions]." / As for the degrees of manifestation—intense, middling, and mild—

13.s:
tā eva śaktipātasya pratyekaṃ traidhamāsthitāḥ /
tīvratīvraḥ śaktipāto dehapātavaśātsvayam // 130
13.d:
ता एव शक्तिपातस्य प्रत्येकं त्रैधमास्थिताः ।
तीव्रतीव्रः शक्तिपातो देहपातवशात्स्वयम् ॥ 130
13.m: these threefold states belong individually to the descent of power. / An intensely intense descent of power, through the fall of the body, spontaneously

13.s:
mokṣapradastadaivānyakāle vā tāratamyataḥ /
madhyatīvrātpunaḥ sarvamajñānaṃ vinivartate // 131
13.d:
मोक्षप्रदस्तदैवान्यकाले वा तारतम्यतः ।
मध्यतीव्रात्पुनः सर्वमज्ञानं विनिवर्तते ॥ 131
13.m: bestows liberation at that very moment, or at another time according to degrees. / From the middling-intense, moreover, all ignorance turns away,

13.s:
svayameva yato vetti bandhamokṣatayātmatām /
tatprātibhaṃ mahājñānaṃ śāstrācāryānapekṣi yat. // 132
13.d:
स्वयमेव यतो वेत्ति बन्धमोक्षतयात्मताम् ।
तत्प्रातिभं महाज्ञानं शास्त्राचार्यानपेक्षि यत्। ॥ 132
13.m: since by oneself alone one knows the selfhood consisting of bondage and liberation. / That is the great intuitive knowledge that does not depend on scripture or master.

13.s:
pratibhācandrikāśāntadhvāntaścācāryacandramāḥ /
tamastāpau hanti dṛśaṃ visphāryānandanirbharām // 133
13.d:
प्रतिभाचन्द्रिकाशान्तध्वान्तश्चाचार्यचन्द्रमाः ।
तमस्तापौ हन्ति दृशं विस्फार्यानन्दनिर्भराम् ॥ 133
13.m: And the moon-like master, whose darkness has been stilled by the moonlight of intuitive flash, / dispels darkness and torment, opening wide a vision overflowing with bliss.

13.s:
sa śiṣṭaḥ karmakartṛtvācchiṣyo'nyaḥ karmabhāvataḥ /
śiṣṭaḥ sarvatra ca smārtapadakālakulādiṣu // 134
13.d:
स शिष्टः कर्मकर्तृत्वाच्छिष्योऽन्यः कर्मभावतः ।
शिष्टः सर्वत्र च स्मार्तपदकालकुलादिषु ॥ 134
13.m: He is the instructed master (śiṣṭa) through his role as agent of action; the other is the disciple (śiṣya) through his role as object of action. / And the instructed master is [recognised] everywhere in traditional law, prosody, astrology, Kula, and so forth.

13.s:
uktaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ śāstrārthapratibhāpariniṣṭhitaḥ /
yanmūlaṃ śāsanaṃ tena na riktaḥ ko'pi jantukaḥ // 135
13.d:
उक्तः स्वयंभूः शास्त्रार्थप्रतिभापरिनिष्ठितः ।
यन्मूलं शासनं तेन न रिक्तः कोऽपि जन्तुकः ॥ 135
13.m: He is called self-born (svayaṃbhū), established in the intuitive flash of scriptural meaning. / Because teaching has that as its root, no living being is destitute [of it].

13.s:
tatrāpi tāratamyotthamānantyaṃ dārḍhyakamprate /
yuktiḥ śāstraṃ gururvādo'bhyāsa ityādyapekṣate // 136
13.d:
तत्रापि तारतम्योत्थमानन्त्यं दार्ढ्यकम्प्रते ।
युक्तिः शास्त्रं गुरुर्वादोऽभ्यास इत्याद्यपेक्षते ॥ 136
13.m: There too, an infinity arises from degrees of difference, regarding firmness and wavering; / [one] requires reasoning, scripture, a guru, debate, practice, and the like.

13.s:
kampamānaṃ hi vijñānaṃ svayameva punarvrajet /
kasyāpi dārḍhyamanyasya yuktyādyaiḥ kevaletaraiḥ // 137
13.d:
कम्पमानं हि विज्ञानं स्वयमेव पुनर्व्रजेत् ।
कस्यापि दार्ढ्यमन्यस्य युक्त्याद्यैः केवलेतरैः ॥ 137
13.m: For wavering knowledge may indeed spontaneously regain / firmness for someone; for another, only through reasoning and the rest.

13.s:
yathā yathā parāpekṣātānavaṃ prātibhe bhavet /
tathā tathā gururasau śreṣṭho vijñānapāragaḥ // 138
13.d:
यथा यथा परापेक्षातानवं प्रातिभे भवेत् ।
तथा तथा गुरुरसौ श्रेष्ठो विज्ञानपारगः ॥ 138
13.m: To the extent that there is diminution of dependence on others in what is intuitive, / to that extent is this guru supreme, having crossed to the further shore of knowledge.

13.s:
anyataḥ śikṣitānantajñāno'pi pratibhābalāt /
yadvetti tatra tatrāsya śivatā jyāyasī ca sā // 139
13.d:
अन्यतः शिक्षितानन्तज्ञानोऽपि प्रतिभाबलात् ।
यद्वेत्ति तत्र तत्रास्य शिवता ज्यायसी च सा ॥ 139
13.m: Even if infinite knowledge is learned from another, that which he knows / by the power of intuitive flash—in that and that respect, his Śivahood is superior.

13.s:
na cāsya samayitvādikramo nāpyabhiṣecanam /
na santānādi no vidyāvrataṃ prātibhavartmanaḥ // 140
13.d:
न चास्य समयित्वादिक्रमो नाप्यभिषेचनम् ।
न सन्तानादि नो विद्याव्रतं प्रातिभवर्त्मनः ॥ 140
13.m: And for him there is no progression of being an initiate into the rule and so forth, nor consecration; / there is no lineage and the like, nor vow of knowledge, for one on the intuitive path.

13.s:
ādividvānmahādevastenaiṣo'dhiṣṭhito yataḥ /
saṃskārāstadadhiṣṭhānasiddhyai tattasya tu svataḥ // 141
13.d:
आदिविद्वान्महादेवस्तेनैषोऽधिष्ठितो यतः ।
संस्कारास्तदधिष्ठानसिद्ध्यै तत्तस्य तु स्वतः ॥ 141
13.m: Because he is presided over by the primordial knower, the Great God Himself; / the purificatory rites are for the attainment of that presiding [grace], but that belongs to him naturally.

13.s:
devībhirdīkṣitastena sabhaktiḥ śivaśāsane /
dṛḍhatākampratābhedaiḥ so'pi svayamatha vratāt // 142
13.d:
देवीभिर्दीक्षितस्तेन सभक्तिः शिवशासने ।
दृढताकम्प्रताभेदैः सोऽपि स्वयमथ व्रतात् ॥ 142
13.m: Therefore, initiated by the Goddesses, he is devoted to the teaching of Śiva. / Even he, according to the distinctions of firmness and wavering, spontaneously or from a vow,

13.s:
tapojapādergurutaḥ svasaṃskāraṃ prakalpayet /
yato vājasineyākhya uktaṃ siñcetsvayaṃ tanum // 143
13.d:
तपोजपादेर्गुरुतः स्वसंस्कारं प्रकल्पयेत् ।
यतो वाजसिनेयाख्य उक्तं सिञ्चेत्स्वयं तनुम् ॥ 143
13.m: from ascetic practice, recitation, and so forth, or from a guru, may arrange his own purification; / for in the text called Vājasineya it is said: "One should sprinkle one's own body."

13.s:
ityādyupakramaṃ yāvadante tatpariniṣṭhitam /
abhiṣikto bhavedevaṃ na bāhyakalaśāmbubhiḥ // 144
13.d:
इत्याद्युपक्रमं यावदन्ते तत्परिनिष्ठितम् ।
अभिषिक्तो भवेदेवं न बाह्यकलशाम्बुभिः ॥ 144
13.m: Beginning with such [rites], culminating in what is fully accomplished at the end, / one becomes consecrated in this manner, not by external waters of a pot.

13.s:
śrīsarvavīraśrībrahmayāmalādau ca tattathā /
nirūpitaṃ maheśena kiyadvā likhyatāmidam // 145
13.d:
श्रीसर्ववीरश्रीब्रह्मयामलादौ च तत्तथा ।
निरूपितं महेशेन कियद्वा लिख्यतामिदम् ॥ 145
13.m: And in the venerable Sarvavīra, the venerable Brahmayāmala, and other texts, it is likewise / determined by the Great Lord; how much of this can be written down?

13.s:
itthaṃ prātibhavijñānaṃ kiṃ kiṃ kasya na sādhayet /
yatprātibhādvā sarvaṃ cetyūce śeṣamahāmuniḥ // 146
13.d:
इत्थं प्रातिभविज्ञानं किं किं कस्य न साधयेत् ।
यत्प्रातिभाद्वा सर्वं चेत्यूचे शेषमहामुनिः ॥ 146
13.m: In this way, what could intuitive knowledge not accomplish, and for whom? / As the great sage Śeṣa said: "Or from the intuitive flash, everything."

13.s:
anye tvāhurakāmasya prātibho gururīdṛśaḥ /
sāmagrījanyatā kāmye tenārimansaṃskṛto guruḥ // 147
13.d:
अन्ये त्वाहुरकामस्य प्रातिभो गुरुरीदृशः ।
सामग्रीजन्यता काम्ये तेनारिमन्संस्कृतो गुरुः ॥ 147
13.m: Others, however, say: such an intuitive guru belongs [only] to one free of desires; / for a desire-prompted [goal], there is dependence on the totality of causes, and therefore in this [case] an initiated guru [is needed].

13.s:
niyatermahimā naiva phale sādhye nivartate /
abhiṣiktaścīrṇavidyāvratastena phalapradaḥ // 148
13.d:
नियतेर्महिमा नैव फले साध्ये निवर्तते ।
अभिषिक्तश्चीर्णविद्याव्रतस्तेन फलप्रदः ॥ 148
13.m: The majesty of the cosmic order (niyati) does not cease when a result is to be accomplished; / therefore, one who is consecrated and has observed the vow of knowledge is the bestower of results.

13.s:
asadetaditi prāhurguravastattvadarśinaḥ /
śrīsomānandakalyāṇabhavabhūtipurogamāḥ // 149
13.d:
असदेतदिति प्राहुर्गुरवस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ।
श्रीसोमानन्दकल्याणभवभूतिपुरोगमाः ॥ 149
13.m: The gurus who perceive the truth, led by the venerable Somānanda, / Kalyāṇa, and Bhavabhūti, have declared: "This is untrue."

13.s:
tathāhi trīśikāśāstravivṛtau te'bhyadhurbudhāḥ /
sāṃsiddhikaṃ yadvijñānaṃ taccintāratnamucyate // 150
13.d:
तथाहि त्रीशिकाशास्त्रविवृतौ तेऽभ्यधुर्बुधाः ।
सांसिद्धिकं यद्विज्ञानं तच्चिन्तारत्नमुच्यते ॥ 150
13.m: For thus those wise ones explained in the commentary on the Trīśikā treatise: / "That knowledge which is innate is called the wish-fulfilling jewel;

13.s:
tadabhāve tadarthaṃ tadāhṛtaṃ jñānamādṛtam /
evaṃ yo veda tattvena tasya nirvāṇagāminī // 151
13.d:
तदभावे तदर्थं तदाहृतं ज्ञानमादृतम् ।
एवं यो वेद तत्त्वेन तस्य निर्वाणगामिनी ॥ 151
13.m: in its absence, knowledge acquired for its sake is respected. / Whoever knows thus in truth, for him there is an initiation

13.s:
dīkṣā bhavatyasandigdhā tilājyāhutivarjitā /
adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo'pyevaṃ yaḥ kaścidvetti tattvataḥ // 152
13.d:
दीक्षा भवत्यसन्दिग्धा तिलाज्याहुतिवर्जिता ।
अदृष्टमण्डलोऽप्येवं यः कश्चिद्वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥ 152
13.m: that leads to liberation, undoubted, devoid of oblations of sesame and ghee. / Even one who has not seen the maṇḍala, who knows thus in truth,

13.s:
sa siddhibhāgbhavennityaṃ sa yogī sa ca dīkṣitaḥ /
avidhijño vidhānajño jāyate yajanaṃ prati // 153
13.d:
स सिद्धिभाग्भवेन्नित्यं स योगी स च दीक्षितः ।
अविधिज्ञो विधानज्ञो जायते यजनं प्रति ॥ 153
13.m: always shares in spiritual accomplishment; he is a yogin and he is initiated. / One ignorant of rules becomes a knower of rules with respect to worship."

13.s:
ityādibhistrīśikoktairvākyairmāheśvaraiḥ sphuṭam /
jñānaṃ dīkṣādisaṃskārasatattvamiti varṇitam // 154
13.d:
इत्यादिभिस्त्रीशिकोक्तैर्वाक्यैर्माहेश्वरैः स्फुटम् ।
ज्ञानं दीक्षादिसंस्कारसतत्त्वमिति वर्णितम् ॥ 154
13.m: By such statements spoken in the Trīśikā, uttered by the Great Lord, it is clearly / described that knowledge is the true reality of the purificatory rites such as initiation.

13.s:
jñānopāyastu dīkṣādikriyā jñānaviyoginām /
ityetadadhunaivāstā svaprastāve bhaviṣyati // 155
13.d:
ज्ञानोपायस्तु दीक्षादिक्रिया ज्ञानवियोगिनाम् ।
इत्येतदधुनैवास्ता स्वप्रस्तावे भविष्यति ॥ 155
13.m: Action such as initiation, on the other hand, is a means to knowledge for those devoid of knowledge. / Let this stand for now; it will be treated in its proper occasion.

13.s:
guruśāstrapramāṇāderapyupāyatvamaṃjasā /
pratibhā paramevaiṣā sarvakāmadughā yataḥ // 156
13.d:
गुरुशास्त्रप्रमाणादेरप्युपायत्वमंजसा ।
प्रतिभा परमेवैषा सर्वकामदुघा यतः ॥ 156
13.m: Even the fact that the guru, scriptures, pramāṇa, and the rest are means is straight away [due to this]; / for this intuitive flash is the supreme cow that yields all desires.

13.s:
upāyayogakramato nirupāyamathākramam /
yadrūpaṃ tatparaṃ tattvaṃ tatra tatra suniścitam // 157
13.d:
उपाययोगक्रमतो निरुपायमथाक्रमम् ।
यद्रूपं तत्परं तत्त्वं तत्र तत्र सुनिश्चितम् ॥ 157
13.m: Whether that supreme reality is without means through the succession of yoga using means, / or non-successive, it is well ascertained in each case.

13.s:
yastu prātibhabāhyātmasaṃskāradvayasundaraḥ /
ukto'nanyopakāryatvātsa sākṣādvarado guruḥ // 158
13.d:
यस्तु प्रातिभबाह्यात्मसंस्कारद्वयसुन्दरः ।
उक्तोऽनन्योपकार्यत्वात्स साक्षाद्वरदो गुरुः ॥ 158
13.m: He, however, who is adorned with the two purifications—intuitive and external-internal—/ is declared to be the guru who directly bestows boons, because he cannot be benefited by another.

13.s:
svamuktimātre kasyāpi yāvadviśvavimocane /
pratibhodeti khadyotaratnatārendusūryavat // 159
13.d:
स्वमुक्तिमात्रे कस्यापि यावद्विश्वविमोचने ।
प्रतिभोदेति खद्योतरत्नतारेन्दुसूर्यवत् ॥ 159
13.m: For someone, intuition arises merely for his own liberation; for another, up to the liberation of the universe, / like a firefly, a jewel, a star, the moon, or the sun.

13.s:
tataḥ prātibhasaṃvittyai śāstramasmatkṛtaṃ tvidam /
yo'bhyasyetsa gururnaiva vastvarthā hi viḍambakāḥ // 160
13.d:
ततः प्रातिभसंवित्त्यै शास्त्रमस्मत्कृतं त्विदम् ।
योऽभ्यस्येत्स गुरुर्नैव वस्त्वर्था हि विडम्बकाः ॥ 160
13.m: Therefore, whoever studies this treatise composed by us for the sake of intuitive consciousness / is a guru, not those who are pretenders regarding the true purpose.

13.s:
paropajīvitābuddhyā sarva itthaṃ na bhāsate /
taduktyā na vinā vetti śaktipātasya māndyataḥ // 161
13.d:
परोपजीविताबुद्ध्या सर्व इत्थं न भासते ।
तदुक्त्या न विना वेत्ति शक्तिपातस्य मान्द्यतः ॥ 161
13.m: Because of the mentality of relying on others, not everything shines forth in this way; / without his instruction, one does not know, due to the sluggishness of the descent of power.

13.s:
sphuṭametacca śāstreṣu teṣu teṣu nirūpyate /
kiraṇāyāṃ tathoktaṃ ca gurutaḥ śāstrataḥ svataḥ // 162
13.d:
स्फुटमेतच्च शास्त्रेषु तेषु तेषु निरूप्यते ।
किरणायां तथोक्तं च गुरुतः शास्त्रतः स्वतः ॥ 162
13.m: And this is clearly set forth in various scriptures. / In the Kiraṇa it is likewise stated: "From the guru, from scripture, and from oneself."

13.s:
jñānayogyāstathā keciccaryāyogyāstathāpare /
śrīmannandiśikhātantre vitatyaitannirūpitam // 163
13.d:
ज्ञानयोग्यास्तथा केचिच्चर्यायोग्यास्तथापरे ।
श्रीमन्नन्दिशिखातन्त्रे वितत्यैतन्निरूपितम् ॥ 163
13.m: Likewise, some are fit for knowledge, and others are fit for ritual conduct; / this has been set forth at length in the venerable Nandiśikhātantra.

13.s:
praśnottaramukheneti tadabhagnaṃ nirūpyate /
anirdeśyaḥ śivastatra ko'bhyupāyo nirūpyatām // 164
13.d:
प्रश्नोत्तरमुखेनेति तदभग्नं निरूप्यते ।
अनिर्देश्यः शिवस्तत्र कोऽभ्युपायो निरूप्यताम् ॥ 164
13.m: It is set forth there unbroken by way of question and answer: / "Śiva is indescribable; in that regard, let the means be explained."

13.s:
iti praśne kṛte devyā śrīmāñchaṃbhurnyarūpayam /
upāyo'tra vivekaikaḥ sa hi heyaṃ vihāpayan // 165
13.d:
इति प्रश्ने कृते देव्या श्रीमाञ्छंभुर्न्यरूपयम् ।
उपायोऽत्र विवेकैकः स हि हेयं विहापयन् ॥ 165
13.m: When this question was posed by the Goddess, the venerable Śambhu explained: / "The unique means here is discernment alone, for it, causing what is to be abandoned to be discarded,

13.s:
dadātyasya ca suśroṇi prātibhaṃ jñānamuttamam /
yadā pratibhayā yuktastadā muktaśca mocayet // 166
13.d:
ददात्यस्य च सुश्रोणि प्रातिभं ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।
यदा प्रतिभया युक्तस्तदा मुक्तश्च मोचयेत् ॥ 166
13.m: And it gives to him, O fair-hipped one, supreme intuitive knowledge. / When endowed with the intuitive flash, then, being liberated, he can liberate [others].

13.s:
paraśaktinipātena dhvastamāyāmalaḥ pumān /
nanu prāgdīkṣayā mokṣo'dhunā tu prātibhātkatham // 167
13.d:
परशक्तिनिपातेन ध्वस्तमायामलः पुमान् ।
ननु प्राग्दीक्षया मोक्षोऽधुना तु प्रातिभात्कथम् ॥ 167
13.m: [Such] a person has the impurity of māyā destroyed by the descent of the supreme power. / [The Goddess asks:] 'Surely liberation was previously said to come from initiation; how now does it come from intuitive [knowledge]?'

13.s:
iti devyā kṛte praśne prāvartata vibhorvacaḥ /
dīkṣayā mucyate jantuḥ prātibhena tathā priye // 168
13.d:
इति देव्या कृते प्रश्ने प्रावर्तत विभोर्वचः ।
दीक्षया मुच्यते जन्तुः प्रातिभेन तथा प्रिये ॥ 168
13.m: When this question was posed by the Goddess, the speech of the All-Pervading Lord commenced: / 'A living creature is liberated through initiation, and likewise through intuitive [knowledge], O beloved.

13.s:
gurvāyattā tu sā dīkṣā badhyabandhanamokṣaṇe /
prātibho'sya svabhāvastu kevalībhāvasiddhidaḥ // 169
13.d:
गुर्वायत्ता तु सा दीक्षा बध्यबन्धनमोक्षणे ।
प्रातिभोऽस्य स्वभावस्तु केवलीभावसिद्धिदः ॥ 169
13.m: That initiation, however, depends on a guru for releasing the bound one from bondage, / but intuitive [knowledge] is one's own nature, bestowing the accomplishment of the state of absolute isolation.

13.s:
kevalasya dhruvaṃ muktiḥ paratattvena sā nanu /
nṛśaktiśivamuktaṃ hi tattvatrayamidaṃ tvayā // 170
13.d:
केवलस्य ध्रुवं मुक्तिः परतत्त्वेन सा ननु ।
नृशक्तिशिवमुक्तं हि तत्त्वत्रयमिदं त्वया ॥ 170
13.m: Surely the liberation of the isolated one is firmly [established] through the supreme reality; / for this triad of principles—man, power, and Śiva—has indeed been spoken by you.

13.s:
nā badhyo bandhane śaktiḥ karaṇaṃ kartṛtāṃ spṛśat /
śivaḥ karteti tatproktaṃ sarvaṃ gurvāgamādaṇoḥ // 171
13.d:
ना बध्यो बन्धने शक्तिः करणं कर्तृतां स्पृशत् ।
शिवः कर्तेति तत्प्रोक्तं सर्वं गुर्वागमादणोः ॥ 171
13.m: Man is bound in bondage; power is the instrument touching agency; / Śiva is the agent: all this has been declared from the guru's transmission to the bound soul.

13.s:
punarvivekāduktaṃ taduttarottaramucyatām /
kathaṃ vivekaḥ kiṃ vāsya devadeva vivicyate // 172
13.d:
पुनर्विवेकादुक्तं तदुत्तरोत्तरमुच्यताम् ।
कथं विवेकः किं वास्य देवदेव विविच्यते ॥ 172
13.m: Again, it was stated [to arise] from discernment; let what is further and further beyond be told: / How does discernment arise, or what of him is discerned, O God of gods?'

13.s:
ityukte parameśānyā jagādādiguruḥ śivaḥ /
śivāditattvatritayaṃ tadāgamavaśādguroḥ // 173
13.d:
इत्युक्ते परमेशान्या जगादादिगुरुः शिवः ।
शिवादितत्त्वत्रितयं तदागमवशाद्गुरोः ॥ 173
13.m: When this was spoken by the Supreme Mistress, Śiva, the primordial guru, declared: / 'The triad of principles beginning with Śiva, established through the transmission of that guru,

13.s:
adhrottaragairvākyaiḥ siddhaṃ prātibhatāṃ vrajet /
dīkṣāsicchinnapāśatvādbhāvanābhāvitasya hi // 174
13.d:
अध्रोत्तरगैर्वाक्यैः सिद्धं प्रातिभतां व्रजेत् ।
दीक्षासिच्छिन्नपाशत्वाद्भावनाभावितस्य हि ॥ 174
13.m: through statements relating to lower and higher, attains intuitive nature. / For of one cultivated through contemplation, whose bonds are severed by the sword of initiation,

13.s:
vikāsaṃ tattvamāyāti prātibhaṃ tadudāhṛtam /
bhasmacchannāgnivatsphauṭyaṃ prātibhe gauravāgamāt // 175
13.d:
विकासं तत्त्वमायाति प्रातिभं तदुदाहृतम् ।
भस्मच्छन्नाग्निवत्स्फौट्यं प्रातिभे गौरवागमात् ॥ 175
13.m: the reality comes to expansion; that is declared to be intuitive [knowledge]. / Like fire covered by ashes, clarity in intuitive [knowledge] arises from the guru's transmission.

13.s:
bījaṃ kāloptasaṃsiktaṃ yathā vardheta tattathā /
yogayāgajapairuktairguruṇā prātibhaṃ sphuṭet // 176
13.d:
बीजं कालोप्तसंसिक्तं यथा वर्धेत तत्तथा ।
योगयागजपैरुक्तैर्गुरुणा प्रातिभं स्फुटेत् ॥ 176
13.m: Just as a seed sown and watered in proper season will grow, even so / intuitive [knowledge] bursts forth through yoga, sacrifice, and recitation taught by the guru.

13.s:
viveko'tīndriyastveṣa yadāyāti vivecanam /
paśupāśapatijñānaṃ svayaṃ nirbhāsate tadā // 177
13.d:
विवेकोऽतीन्द्रियस्त्वेष यदायाति विवेचनम् ।
पशुपाशपतिज्ञानं स्वयं निर्भासते तदा ॥ 177
13.m: When this discernment, which is beyond the senses, comes to realization, / then the knowledge of the bound soul, the bond, and the Lord shines forth of itself.

13.s:
prātibhe tu samāyāte jñānamanyattu sendriyam /
vāgakṣiśrutigamyaṃ cāpyanyāpekṣaṃ varānane // 178
13.d:
प्रातिभे तु समायाते ज्ञानमन्यत्तु सेन्द्रियम् ।
वागक्षिश्रुतिगम्यं चाप्यन्यापेक्षं वरानने ॥ 178
13.m: When intuitive [knowledge] has arisen, other knowledge involving the senses, / accessible through speech, eye, and ear, and dependent on other [factors], O fair-faced one,

13.s:
tattyajedbuddhimāsthāya pradīpaṃ tu yathā divā /
prādurbhūtavivekasya syāccidindriyagocare // 179
13.d:
तत्त्यजेद्बुद्धिमास्थाय प्रदीपं तु यथा दिवा ।
प्रादुर्भूतविवेकस्य स्याच्चिदिन्द्रियगोचरे ॥ 179
13.m: one should abandon, having relied on intellect, just like a lamp by day. / For one in whom discernment has manifested, within the domain of consciousness and the senses

13.s:
dūrācchrutyādivedhādivṛddhikrīḍāvicitritā /
sarvabhāvavivekāttu sarvabhāvaparāṅmukhaḥ // 180
13.d:
दूराच्छ्रुत्यादिवेधादिवृद्धिक्रीडाविचित्रिता ।
सर्वभावविवेकात्तु सर्वभावपराङ्मुखः ॥ 180
13.m: [such abilities as] hearing from afar, piercing, and other powers may appear, variegated with playful display; / yet from discernment of all existents, turning away from all existents,

13.s:
krīḍāsu suviraktātmā śivabhāvaikabhāvitaḥ /
māhātmyametatsuśroṇi prātibhasya vidhīyate // 181
13.d:
क्रीडासु सुविरक्तात्मा शिवभावैकभावितः ।
माहात्म्यमेतत्सुश्रोणि प्रातिभस्य विधीयते ॥ 181
13.m: his self entirely detached from playful displays, cultivated solely in the state of Śiva— / this, O fair-hipped one, is proclaimed to be the majesty of intuitive [knowledge].

13.s:
svacchāyādarśavatpaśyedbahirantargataṃ śivam /
heyopādeyatattvajñastadā dhyāyennijāṃ citim // 182
13.d:
स्वच्छायादर्शवत्पश्येद्बहिरन्तर्गतं शिवम् ।
हेयोपादेयतत्त्वज्ञस्तदा ध्यायेन्निजां चितिम् ॥ 182
13.m: Like one's reflection in a mirror, he sees Śiva existing inside and outside; / knowing the reality of what is to be avoided and what is to be adopted, he then contemplates his own consciousness.

13.s:
siddhijālaṃ hi kathitaṃ parapratyayakāraṇam /
ihaiva siddhāḥ kāyānte mucyeranniti bhāvanāt // 183
13.d:
सिद्धिजालं हि कथितं परप्रत्ययकारणम् ।
इहैव सिद्धाः कायान्ते मुच्येरन्निति भावनात् ॥ 183
13.m: For the web of spiritual accomplishments has been declared to be the cause of conviction in others; / through [such] contemplation, 'Those accomplished here in this very life are liberated at the end of the body.'

13.s:
parabhāvanadārḍhyāttu jīvanmukto nigadyate /
etatte prātibhe bhede lakṣaṇaṃ samudāhṛtam // 184
13.d:
परभावनदार्ढ्यात्तु जीवन्मुक्तो निगद्यते ।
एतत्ते प्रातिभे भेदे लक्षणं समुदाहृतम् ॥ 184
13.m: Through firmness in the supreme contemplation, however, he is called liberated while living. / This is declared to you as the defining characteristic of the intuitive variety.

13.s:
śāpānugrahakāryeṣu tathābhyāsena śaktayā /
teṣūdāsīnatāyāṃ tu mucyate mocayetparān // 185
13.d:
शापानुग्रहकार्येषु तथाभ्यासेन शक्तया ।
तेषूदासीनतायां तु मुच्यते मोचयेत्परान् ॥ 185
13.m: With respect to acts of cursing and grace, likewise through practice endowed with power, / but upon indifference toward them, he is liberated and liberates others.

13.s:
bhūtendriyādiyogena baddho'ṇuḥ saṃsareddhruvam /
sa eva pratibhāyuktaḥ śaktitattvaṃ nigadyate // 186
13.d:
भूतेन्द्रियादियोगेन बद्धोऽणुः संसरेद्ध्रुवम् ।
स एव प्रतिभायुक्तः शक्तितत्त्वं निगद्यते ॥ 186
13.m: Bound through connection with the elements, senses, and the rest, the bound soul inevitably transmigrates; / that very [soul], endowed with the intuitive flash, is called the principle of power.

13.s:
tatpātāveśato muktaḥ śiva eva bhavārṇavāt /
nanvācāryātsendriyaṃ tajjñānamuktamatīndriyam // 187
13.d:
तत्पातावेशतो मुक्तः शिव एव भवार्णवात् ।
नन्वाचार्यात्सेन्द्रियं तज्ज्ञानमुक्तमतीन्द्रियम् ॥ 187
13.m: Liberated from the ocean of transmigratory existence through the descent and immersion of that [power], he is Śiva himself.' / [The Goddess asks:] 'Surely that knowledge from the master was said to involve the senses, while that beyond the senses

13.s:
vivekajaṃ ca tadbuddhyā tatkathaṃ syānnirindriyam /
iti pṛṣṭo'bhyadhātsvāntadhiyorjāḍyaikavāsanāt // 188
13.d:
विवेकजं च तद्बुद्ध्या तत्कथं स्यान्निरिन्द्रियम् ।
इति पृष्टोऽभ्यधात्स्वान्तधियोर्जाड्यैकवासनात् ॥ 188
13.m: is born of discernment through the intellect; how then could it be devoid of senses?' / Asked thus, he replied: 'From the latent impression consisting purely of dullness of the inner sense and intellect,

13.s:
akṣatvaṃ pravivekena tacchittau bhāsakaḥ śivaḥ /
saṃskāraḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ paratā parikīrtitā // 189
13.d:
अक्षत्वं प्रविवेकेन तच्छित्तौ भासकः शिवः ।
संस्कारः सर्वभावानां परता परिकीर्तिता ॥ 189
13.m: arises sensory nature; through thorough discernment, upon their cessation, Śiva is the illuminator. / The refinement of all entities is proclaimed to be transcendence.

13.s:
manobuddhī na bhinne tu kasmiṃścitkāraṇāntare /
viveke kāraṇe hyete prabhuśaktyupavṛṃhite // 190
13.d:
मनोबुद्धी न भिन्ने तु कस्मिंश्चित्कारणान्तरे ।
विवेके कारणे ह्येते प्रभुशक्त्युपवृंहिते ॥ 190
13.m: Mind and intellect are not separate in some other cause; / for when discernment is the cause, these two are augmented by the Lord's power.

13.s:
na manobuddhihīnastu jñānasyādhigamaḥ priye /
parabhāvāttu tatsūkṣmaṃ śaktitattvaṃ nigadyate // 191
13.d:
न मनोबुद्धिहीनस्तु ज्ञानस्याधिगमः प्रिये ।
परभावात्तु तत्सूक्ष्मं शक्तितत्त्वं निगद्यते ॥ 191
13.m: The apprehension of knowledge does not occur devoid of mind and intellect, O beloved; / yet through its supreme nature, that subtle [reality] is called the principle of power.

13.s:
vivekaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ śuddhabhāvānmahāśayaḥ /
buddhitattvaṃ tu triguṇamuttamādhamamadhyamam // 192
13.d:
विवेकः सर्वभावानां शुद्धभावान्महाशयः ।
बुद्धितत्त्वं तु त्रिगुणमुत्तमाधममध्यमम् ॥ 192
13.m: Discernment of all entities belongs to the high-minded one through pure being. / The intellect-principle, however, consists of the three qualities—superior, inferior, and intermediate;

13.s:
aṇimādigataṃ cāpi bandhakaṃ jaḍamindriyam /
nanu prātibhato muktau dīkṣayā kiṃ śivādhvare // 193
13.d:
अणिमादिगतं चापि बन्धकं जडमिन्द्रियम् ।
ननु प्रातिभतो मुक्तौ दीक्षया किं शिवाध्वरे ॥ 193
13.m: and the insentient sense-organ pertaining to [powers like] atomicity and the rest is a binder. / [The Goddess asks:] 'Surely, if liberation comes from the intuitive [faculty], what is the use of initiation in the Śaiva sacrifice?'

13.s:
ūce'jñānā hi dīkṣāyāṃ bālavāliśayoṣitaḥ /
pāśacchedādvimucyante prabuddhyante śivādhvare // 194
13.d:
ऊचेऽज्ञाना हि दीक्षायां बालवालिशयोषितः ।
पाशच्छेदाद्विमुच्यन्ते प्रबुद्ध्यन्ते शिवाध्वरे ॥ 194
13.m: He replied: 'Ignorant ones—children, the foolish, and women— / are freed from the cutting of bonds and awakened in the Śaiva sacrifice.

13.s:
tasmāddīkṣā bhavatyeṣu kāraṇatvena sundari /
dīkṣayā pāśamokṣe tu śuddhabhāvādvivekajam // 195
13.d:
तस्माद्दीक्षा भवत्येषु कारणत्वेन सुन्दरि ।
दीक्षया पाशमोक्षे तु शुद्धभावाद्विवेकजम् ॥ 195
13.m: Therefore initiation serves as the cause for them, O beautiful woman; / but upon the release of bonds through initiation, that which is born of discernment [arises] from pure being.'

13.s:
ityeṣa paṭhito granthaḥ svayaṃ ye boddhumakṣamāḥ /
teṣāṃ śivoktisaṃvādādbodho dārḍhyaṃ vrajediti // 196
13.d:
इत्येष पठितो ग्रन्थः स्वयं ये बोद्धुमक्षमाः ।
तेषां शिवोक्तिसंवादाद्बोधो दार्ढ्यं व्रजेदिति ॥ 196
13.m: Thus this text has been cited so that those who are unable to understand on their own / may find that their understanding attains firmness through agreement with the words of Śiva.

13.s:
śrīmanniśāṭane cātmaguruśāstravaśāttridhā /
jñānaṃ mukhyaṃ svopalabdhi vikalpārṇavatāraṇam // 197
13.d:
श्रीमन्निशाटने चात्मगुरुशास्त्रवशात्त्रिधा ।
ज्ञानं मुख्यं स्वोपलब्धि विकल्पार्णवतारणम् ॥ 197
13.m: And in the venerable Niśāṭana [it is said]: 'Knowledge is threefold, depending on self, guru, and scripture; / primary is self-realization, crossing over the ocean of conceptual constructs.

13.s:
mantrātmabhūtadravyāśadivyatattvādigocarā /
śaṃkā vikalpamūlā hi śāmyetsvapratyayāditi // 198
13.d:
मन्त्रात्मभूतद्रव्याशदिव्यतत्त्वादिगोचरा ।
शंका विकल्पमूला हि शाम्येत्स्वप्रत्ययादिति ॥ 198
13.m: Doubt concerning mantras, the self, elemental substances, celestial principles, and the like, / being rooted in conceptual constructs, is stilled by one's own conviction.'

13.s:
enamevārthamantaḥsthaṃ gṛhītvā mālinīmate /
evamasyātmanaḥ kāle kasmiṃścidyogyatāvaśāt // 199
13.d:
एनमेवार्थमन्तःस्थं गृहीत्वा मालिनीमते ।
एवमस्यात्मनः काले कस्मिंश्चिद्योग्यतावशात् ॥ 199
13.m: Grasping this very internal meaning, [it is said] in the Mālinīvijayottara: / 'Thus, at some time, by force of suitability, to this soul

13.s:
śaivī saṃbadhyate śaktiḥ śāntā muktiphalapradā /
tatsaṃbandhāttataḥ kaścittatkṣaṇādapavṛjyate // 200
13.d:
शैवी संबध्यते शक्तिः शान्ता मुक्तिफलप्रदा ।
तत्संबन्धात्ततः कश्चित्तत्क्षणादपवृज्यते ॥ 200
13.m: the power of Śiva connects—tranquil and bestowing the fruit of liberation; / from connection with that, someone is instantly liberated.'

13.s:
ityuktvā tīvratīvrākhyaviṣayaṃ bhāṣate punaḥ /
ajñānena sahaikatvaṃ kasyacidvinivartate // 201
13.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तीव्रतीव्राख्यविषयं भाषते पुनः ।
अज्ञानेन सहैकत्वं कस्यचिद्विनिवर्तते ॥ 201
13.m: Having said this, [the text] again speaks concerning the category called 'extremely intense': / 'The unity [of the soul] with ignorance ceases for a certain person;

13.s:
rudraśaktisamāviṣṭaḥ sa yiyāsuḥ śivecchayā /
bhuktimuktiprasiddhyarthaṃ nīyate sadguruṃ prati // 202
13.d:
रुद्रशक्तिसमाविष्टः स यियासुः शिवेच्छया ।
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रसिद्ध्यर्थं नीयते सद्गुरुं प्रति ॥ 202
13.m: possessed by the power of Rudra, wishing to go by Śiva's will, / he is led to a true guru for the sake of accomplishing enjoyment and liberation.

13.s:
tamārādhya tatastuṣṭāddīkṣāmāsādya śāṅkarīm /
tatkṣaṇādvopabhogādvā dehapātācchivaṃ vrajet // 203
13.d:
तमाराध्य ततस्तुष्टाद्दीक्षामासाद्य शाङ्करीम् ।
तत्क्षणाद्वोपभोगाद्वा देहपाताच्छिवं व्रजेत् ॥ 203
13.m: Having propitiated him and obtained from him, when pleased, the Śaiva initiation, / he reaches Śiva either instantly, or through enjoyment, or at the fall of the body.'

13.s:
asyārthā ātmanaḥ kācitkalanāmarśanātmikā /
svaṃ rūpaṃ prati yā saiva ko'pi kāla ihoditaḥ // 204
13.d:
अस्यार्था आत्मनः काचित्कलनामर्शनात्मिका ।
स्वं रूपं प्रति या सैव कोऽपि काल इहोदितः ॥ 204
13.m: The meaning of this is: a certain impulse consisting of reflective awareness on the part of the soul / toward its own nature is said here to be a certain 'time'.

13.s:
yogyatā śivatādātmyayogārhatvamihocyate /
pūrvaṃ kiṃ na tathā kasmāttadaiveti na saṃgatam // 205
13.d:
योग्यता शिवतादात्म्ययोगार्हत्वमिहोच्यते ।
पूर्वं किं न तथा कस्मात्तदैवेति न संगतम् ॥ 205
13.m: 'Suitability' is stated here to be fitness for union in identity with Śiva. / [Objection:] 'Why was it not so previously? Why only then?' This is not tenable,

13.s:
tathābhāsanamujjhitvā na hi kālo'sti kaścana /
svātantryāttu tathābhāse kālaśaktirvijṛmbhatām // 206
13.d:
तथाभासनमुज्झित्वा न हि कालोऽस्ति कश्चन ।
स्वातन्त्र्यात्तु तथाभासे कालशक्तिर्विजृम्भताम् ॥ 206
13.m: for there is no time whatsoever apart from shining forth in that manner; / but from absolute autonomy, when it shines forth thus, let the power of time unfold.

13.s:
natu paryanuyuktyai sā śive tanmahimoditā /
nanu śaivī mahāśaktiḥ saṃbaddhaivātmabhiḥ sthitā /
satyaṃ sācchādanātmā tu śāntā tveṣā svarūpadṛk // 207
13.d:
नतु पर्यनुयुक्त्यै सा शिवे तन्महिमोदिता ।
ननु शैवी महाशक्तिः संबद्धैवात्मभिः स्थिता ।
सत्यं साच्छादनात्मा तु शान्ता त्वेषा स्वरूपदृक् ॥ 207
13.m: It is not [subject] to cross-examination; in Śiva it is proclaimed as His majesty. / [Objection:] 'Surely the great power of Śiva stays eternally connected with souls?' / True, but it is concealing in nature, whereas this tranquil [power] perceives the essential nature.

13.s: kṣobho hi bheda evaikyaṃ praśamastanmayī tataḥ // 208
13.d: क्षोभो हि भेद एवैक्यं प्रशमस्तन्मयी ततः ॥ 208
13.m: For agitation is indeed differentiation, whereas peace is oneness; therefore [she] consists of that [oneness].

13.s:
tayā śāntyā tu saṃbaddhaḥ sthitaḥ śaktisvarūpabhāk /
tyaktāṇubhāvo bhavati śivastacchaktidārḍhyataḥ // 209
13.d:
तया शान्त्या तु संबद्धः स्थितः शक्तिस्वरूपभाक् ।
त्यक्ताणुभावो भवति शिवस्तच्छक्तिदार्ढ्यतः ॥ 209
13.m: Connected with that tranquil [power], abiding as one sharing the essential nature of power, / his state of being a bound soul abandoned, he becomes Śiva through the firmness of that power.

13.s:
tatrāpi tāratamyādivaśācchīghracirāditaḥ /
dehapāto bhavedasya yadvā kāṣṭhāditulyatā // 210
13.d:
तत्रापि तारतम्यादिवशाच्छीघ्रचिरादितः ।
देहपातो भवेदस्य यद्वा काष्ठादितुल्यता ॥ 210
13.m: Even there, due to gradations and the like, sooner or later, / the fall of his body occurs, or else a state resembling a piece of wood.

13.s:
samastavyavahāreṣu parācīnitacetanaḥ /
tīvratīvramahāśaktisamāviṣṭaḥ sa sidhyati // 211
13.d:
समस्तव्यवहारेषु पराचीनितचेतनः ।
तीव्रतीव्रमहाशक्तिसमाविष्टः स सिध्यति ॥ 211
13.m: With his consciousness turned away from all ordinary activity, / possessed by the exceedingly intense great power, he attains spiritual accomplishment. // 211

13.s:
evaṃ prāgviṣayo grantha iyānanyatra tu sphuṭam /
granthāntaraṃ madhyatīvraśaktipātāṃśasūcakam // 212
13.d:
एवं प्राग्विषयो ग्रन्थ इयानन्यत्र तु स्फुटम् ।
ग्रन्थान्तरं मध्यतीव्रशक्तिपातांशसूचकम् ॥ 212
13.m: So much is the passage concerning the preceding topic; but elsewhere, clearly, / another passage indicates the subdivision of the medium-intense descent of power. // 212

13.s:
ajñānarūpatā puṃsi bodhaḥ saṃkocite hṛdi /
saṃkoce vinivṛtte tu svasvabhāvaḥ prakāśate // 213
13.d:
अज्ञानरूपता पुंसि बोधः संकोचिते हृदि ।
संकोचे विनिवृत्ते तु स्वस्वभावः प्रकाशते ॥ 213
13.m: Consciousness in a person takes the form of ignorance when the heart is contracted; / but when contraction has ceased, his own essential nature shines forth. // 213

13.s:
rudraśaktisamāviṣṭa ityanenāsya varṇyate /
cihnavargo ya ukto'tra rudre bhaktiḥ suniścalā // 214
13.d:
रुद्रशक्तिसमाविष्ट इत्यनेनास्य वर्ण्यते ।
चिह्नवर्गो य उक्तोऽत्र रुद्रे भक्तिः सुनिश्चला ॥ 214
13.m: By the statement 'possessed by the power of Rudra,' there is described / the set of signs stated here: unwavering devotion to Rudra, // 214

13.s:
mantrasiddhiḥ sarvatattvavaśitvaṃ kṛtyasaṃpadaḥ /
kavitvaṃ sarvaśāstrārthaboddhṛtvamiti tatkramāt // 215
13.d:
मन्त्रसिद्धिः सर्वतत्त्ववशित्वं कृत्यसंपदः ।
कवित्वं सर्वशास्त्रार्थबोद्धृत्वमिति तत्क्रमात् ॥ 215
13.m: Attainment of mantras, mastery over all principles of reality, successful completion of undertakings, / poetic capacity, and comprehension of the meaning of all scriptures, in that order. // 215

13.s:
svatāratamyayogātsyādeṣāṃ vyastasamastatā /
tatrāpi bhuktau muktau ca prādhānyaṃ carcayedbudhaḥ // 216
13.d:
स्वतारतम्ययोगात्स्यादेषां व्यस्तसमस्तता ।
तत्रापि भुक्तौ मुक्तौ च प्राधान्यं चर्चयेद्बुधः ॥ 216
13.m: Through their own gradation, these may be separate or combined; / even then, the wise person should examine whether enjoyment or liberation is primary. // 216

13.s:
sa ityanto grantha eṣa dvitīyaviṣayaḥ sphuṭaḥ /
anyastu mandatīvrākhyaśaktipātavidhiṃ prati // 217
13.d:
स इत्यन्तो ग्रन्थ एष द्वितीयविषयः स्फुटः ।
अन्यस्तु मन्दतीव्राख्यशक्तिपातविधिं प्रति ॥ 217
13.m: This passage ending with 'he' clearly concerns the second category; / but another concerns the rule for the descent of power called slow-intense. // 217

13.s:
mandatīvrācchaktibalādyiyāsāsyopajāyate /
śivecchāvaśayogena sadguruṃ prati so'pi ca // 218
13.d:
मन्दतीव्राच्छक्तिबलाद्यियासास्योपजायते ।
शिवेच्छावशयोगेन सद्गुरुं प्रति सोऽपि च ॥ 218
13.m: From the force of the slow-intense power, a desire to go is born in him / toward a true guru, through the power of Śiva's will; and he too // 218

13.s:
atraiva lakṣitaḥ śāstre yaduktaṃ parameṣṭhinā /
yaḥ punaḥ sarvatattvāni vettyetāni yathārthataḥ // 219
13.d:
अत्रैव लक्षितः शास्त्रे यदुक्तं परमेष्ठिना ।
यः पुनः सर्वतत्त्वानि वेत्त्येतानि यथार्थतः ॥ 219
13.m: Is characterized right in this scripture, as stated by the Supreme Lord: / 'Whoever truly knows all these principles of reality, // 219

13.s:
sa gururmatsamaḥ prokto mantravīryaprakāśakaḥ /
dṛṣṭāḥ saṃbhāvitāstena spṛṣṭāśca prītacetasā // 220
13.d:
स गुरुर्मत्समः प्रोक्तो मन्त्रवीर्यप्रकाशकः ।
दृष्टाः संभावितास्तेन स्पृष्टाश्च प्रीतचेतसा ॥ 220
13.m: He is declared to be a guru equal to myself, revealing the potency of mantras. / Seen, honored, and touched by him with a joyful mind, // 220

13.s:
narāḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyante saptajanmakṛtairapi /
ye punardīkṣitāstena prāṇinaḥ śivacoditāḥ // 221
13.d:
नराः पापैः प्रमुच्यन्ते सप्तजन्मकृतैरपि ।
ये पुनर्दीक्षितास्तेन प्राणिनः शिवचोदिताः ॥ 221
13.m: Men are freed even from sins accumulated across seven lifetimes. / Those living beings who are initiated by him, impelled by Śiva, // 221

13.s:
te yatheṣṭaṃ phalaṃ prāpya padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam /
kiṃ tattvaṃ tattvavedī ka ityāmarśanayogataḥ // 222
13.d:
ते यथेष्टं फलं प्राप्य पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम् ।
किं तत्त्वं तत्त्ववेदी क इत्यामर्शनयोगतः ॥ 222
13.m: Attain their desired fruit and go to the sorrowless abode.' / Through contemplation such as 'What is the true reality? Who knows reality?', // 222

13.s:
pratibhānātsuḥṛtsaṅgādgurau jigamiṣurbhavet /
evaṃ jigamiṣāyogādācāryaḥ prāpyate sa ca // 223
13.d:
प्रतिभानात्सुःऋत्सङ्गाद्गुरौ जिगमिषुर्भवेत् ।
एवं जिगमिषायोगादाचार्यः प्राप्यते स च ॥ 223
13.m: From intuitive flash or through companionship with good friends, he becomes one wishing to go to a guru; / thus, through that desire to go, a master is found. And he, // 223

13.s:
tāratamyādiyogena saṃsiddhaḥ saṃskṛto'pi ca /
prāgbhedabhāgī jhaṭiti kramātsāmastyatoṃśataḥ // 224
13.d:
तारतम्यादियोगेन संसिद्धः संस्कृतोऽपि च ।
प्राग्भेदभागी झटिति क्रमात्सामस्त्यतोंशतः ॥ 224
13.m: Through gradations and the like, is spontaneously perfected or consecrated, / possessing the former distinctions, all at once or gradually, wholly or in part. // 224

13.s:
ityādibhedabhinno hi gurorlābha ihoditaḥ /
tasmāddīkṣāṃ sa labhate sadya eva śivapradām // 225
13.d:
इत्यादिभेदभिन्नो हि गुरोर्लाभ इहोदितः ।
तस्माद्दीक्षां स लभते सद्य एव शिवप्रदाम् ॥ 225
13.m: Differentiated by such divisions, the finding of a guru is declared here; / from him he receives initiation that instantly bestows Śivahood, // 225

13.s:
jñānarūpāṃ yathā vetti sarvameva yathārthataḥ /
jīvanmuktaḥ śivībhūtastadaivāsau nigadyate // 226
13.d:
ज्ञानरूपां यथा वेत्ति सर्वमेव यथार्थतः ।
जीवन्मुक्तः शिवीभूतस्तदैवासौ निगद्यते ॥ 226
13.m: Consisting of knowledge, so that he knows everything truly as it is; / he is then indeed proclaimed to be liberated while living, having become Śiva. // 226

13.s:
dehasaṃbandhitāpyasya śivatāyai yataḥ sphuṭā /
asyāṃ bhedo hi kathanātsaṅgamādavalokanāt // 227
13.d:
देहसंबन्धिताप्यस्य शिवतायै यतः स्फुटा ।
अस्यां भेदो हि कथनात्सङ्गमादवलोकनात् ॥ 227
13.m: For even his connection with a body is clearly for the purpose of Śivahood. / In this [initiation], distinction indeed arises from instruction, contact, gazing, // 227

13.s:
śāstrātsaṃkramaṇātsāmyacaryāsaṃdarśanāccaroḥ /
mantramudrādimāhātmyātsamastavyastabhedataḥ // 228
13.d:
शास्त्रात्संक्रमणात्साम्यचर्यासंदर्शनाच्चरोः ।
मन्त्रमुद्रादिमाहात्म्यात्समस्तव्यस्तभेदतः ॥ 228
13.m: From scripture, transmission, observance of equanimity, the sight of the sacred offering, / from the majesty of mantras and mudrās, differentiated collectively or separately, // 228

13.s:
kriyayā vāntarākārarūpaprāṇapraveśataḥ /
tadā ca dehasaṃstho'pi sa mukta iti bhaṇyate // 229
13.d:
क्रियया वान्तराकाररूपप्राणप्रवेशतः ।
तदा च देहसंस्थोऽपि स मुक्त इति भण्यते ॥ 229
13.m: Or by ritual action, or by penetration through the vital breath in an internal form; / and then, even while residing in the body, he is said to be liberated. // 229

13.s:
uktaṃ ca śāstrayoḥ śrīmadratnamālāgamākhyayoḥ /
yasminkāle tu guruṇā nirvikalpaṃ prakāśitam // 230
13.d:
उक्तं च शास्त्रयोः श्रीमद्रत्नमालागमाख्ययोः ।
यस्मिन्काले तु गुरुणा निर्विकल्पं प्रकाशितम् ॥ 230
13.m: And it is said in the two scriptures named the venerable Ratnamālā and Āgama: / 'At the very moment when the non-conceptual is revealed by the guru, // 230

13.s:
tadaiva kila mukto'sau yantraṃ tiṣṭhati kevalam /
prārabdhṛkarmasaṃbandhāddehasya sukhiduḥkhite // 231
13.d:
तदैव किल मुक्तोऽसौ यन्त्रं तिष्ठति केवलम् ।
प्रारब्धृकर्मसंबन्धाद्देहस्य सुखिदुःखिते ॥ 231
13.m: At that very moment, indeed, he is liberated; the body remains merely as an apparatus.' / Because of connection with prārabdha karma, the body's experiences of pleasure and pain // 231

13.s:
na viśaṅketa tacca śrīgamaśāstre nirūpitam /
avidyopāsito deho hyanyajanmasamudbhuvā // 232
13.d:
न विशङ्केत तच्च श्रीगमशास्त्रे निरूपितम् ।
अविद्योपासितो देहो ह्यन्यजन्मसमुद्भुवा ॥ 232
13.m: Should not cause doubt; and that is explained in the venerable Gamāśāstra: / 'The body, sustained by nescience, through karma born of another birth— // 232

13.s:
karmaṇā tena bādhyante jñānino'pi kalevare /
jātyāyurbhogadasyaikapraghaṭṭakatayā sthitiḥ // 233
13.d:
कर्मणा तेन बाध्यन्ते ज्ञानिनोऽपि कलेवरे ।
जात्यायुर्भोगदस्यैकप्रघट्टकतया स्थितिः ॥ 233
13.m: By that karma, even the wise are afflicted in the body. / The status of that which yields birth, lifespan, and enjoyment exists as a single continuum.' // 233

13.s:
uktaikavacanāddhiśca yatastenetisaṃgatiḥ /
abhyāsayuktisaṃkrāntivedhaghaṭṭanarodhataḥ // 234
13.d:
उक्तैकवचनाद्धिश्च यतस्तेनेतिसंगतिः ।
अभ्यासयुक्तिसंक्रान्तिवेधघट्टनरोधतः ॥ 234
13.m: Because of the stated singular number and the particle 'hi' ('for'), the connection is made through 'by that.' / By means of practice, application, transmission, piercing, obstruction, // 234

13.s:
hutervā mantrasāmarthyātpāśacchedaprayogataḥ /
sadyonirvāṇadāṃ kuryātsadyaḥprāṇaviyojikām // 235
13.d:
हुतेर्वा मन्त्रसामर्थ्यात्पाशच्छेदप्रयोगतः ।
सद्योनिर्वाणदां कुर्यात्सद्यःप्राणवियोजिकाम् ॥ 235
13.m: Or oblation, or through the power of mantra, or the application of severing bonds, / he should perform [the initiation] that grants instant liberation, instantly separating the vital breaths. // 235

13.s:
tatra tveṣo'sti niyama āsanne maraṇakṣaṇe /
tāṃ kuryānnānyathārabdhṛ karma yasmānna śuddhyati // 236
13.d:
तत्र त्वेषोऽस्ति नियम आसन्ने मरणक्षणे ।
तां कुर्यान्नान्यथारब्धृ कर्म यस्मान्न शुद्ध्यति ॥ 236
13.m: There, however, this restriction holds: he should perform it when the moment of death is near, / not otherwise, since prārabdha karma is not purged. // 236

13.s:
uktaṃ ca pūrvamevaitanmaṃtrasāmarthyayogataḥ /
prāṇairviyojito'pyeṣa bhuṅkte śeṣaphalaṃ yataḥ // 237
13.d:
उक्तं च पूर्वमेवैतन्मंत्रसामर्थ्ययोगतः ।
प्राणैर्वियोजितोऽप्येष भुङ्क्ते शेषफलं यतः ॥ 237
13.m: And this has already been stated: through the efficacy of mantra, / even though separated from the vital breaths, he experiences the remaining fruit, because // 237

13.s:
tajjanmaśeṣaṃ vividhamativāhya tataḥ sphuṭam /
karmāntaranirodhena śīghramevāpavṛjyate // 238
13.d:
तज्जन्मशेषं विविधमतिवाह्य ततः स्फुटम् ।
कर्मान्तरनिरोधेन शीघ्रमेवापवृज्यते ॥ 238
13.m: Having clearly spent that diverse remainder of life, / through the blocking of further karma, he is very quickly liberated. // 238

13.s:
tasmātprāṇaharīṃ dīkṣāṃ nājñātvā maraṇakṣaṇam /
vidadhyātparameśājñālaṅghanaikaphalā hi sā // 239
13.d:
तस्मात्प्राणहरीं दीक्षां नाज्ञात्वा मरणक्षणम् ।
विदध्यात्परमेशाज्ञालङ्घनैकफला हि सा ॥ 239
13.m: Therefore, without knowing the moment of death, he should not perform / the initiation that takes life; for that has as its sole fruit the transgression of the Supreme Lord's command. // 239

13.s:
ekastriko'yaṃ nirṇītaḥ śaktipāte'pyathāparaḥ /
tīvramadhye tu dīkṣāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ na tathā dṛḍhām // 240
13.d:
एकस्त्रिकोऽयं निर्णीतः शक्तिपातेऽप्यथापरः ।
तीव्रमध्ये तु दीक्षायां कृतायां न तथा दृढाम् ॥ 240
13.m: This first triad of the descent of power has thus been determined. Now the next: / in the intense-medium, when initiation is performed, he does not know so firmly // 240

13.s:
svātmano vetti śivatāṃ dehānte tu śivo bhavet /
uktaṃ ca niśisaṃcārayogasaṃcāraśāstrayoḥ // 241
13.d:
स्वात्मनो वेत्ति शिवतां देहान्ते तु शिवो भवेत् ।
उक्तं च निशिसंचारयोगसंचारशास्त्रयोः ॥ 241
13.m: His own Śivahood, but at the end of the body he becomes Śiva. / And it is said in the Niśisaṃcāra and the Yogasaṃcāra scriptures: // 241

13.s:
vikalpāttu tanau sthitvā dahānte śivatāṃ vrajet /
madhyamadhye śaktipāte śivalābhotsuko'pi san // 242
13.d:
विकल्पात्तु तनौ स्थित्वा दहान्ते शिवतां व्रजेत् ।
मध्यमध्ये शक्तिपाते शिवलाभोत्सुकोऽपि सन् ॥ 242
13.m: 'Remaining in the body due to conceptual thought, at the end of the body he attains Śivahood.' / In the medium-medium descent of power, even though eager for the attainment of Śiva, // 242

13.s:
bubhukṣuryatra yuktastadbhuktvā dehakṣaye śivaḥ /
mandamadhye tu tatraiva tattve kvāpi niyojitaḥ // 243
13.d:
बुभुक्षुर्यत्र युक्तस्तद्भुक्त्वा देहक्षये शिवः ।
मन्दमध्ये तु तत्रैव तत्त्वे क्वापि नियोजितः ॥ 243
13.m: Desiring enjoyment, having enjoyed that to which he was joined, he becomes Śiva at the destruction of the body. / In the slow-medium, however, united with some principle of reality right there, // 243

13.s:
dehānte tattvagaṃ bhogaṃ bhuktvā paścācchivaṃ vrajet /
tatrāpi tāratamyasya saṃbhavācciraśīghratā // 244
13.d:
देहान्ते तत्त्वगं भोगं भुक्त्वा पश्चाच्छिवं व्रजेत् ।
तत्रापि तारतम्यस्य संभवाच्चिरशीघ्रता ॥ 244
13.m: Having enjoyed the experience belonging to that principle at the end of the body, he later attains Śiva. / There too, because variation is possible, there is slowness or quickness, // 244

13.s:
bahvalpabhogayogaśca dehabhūmālpatākramaḥ /
tīvramande madhyamande mandamande bubhukṣutā // 245
13.d:
बह्वल्पभोगयोगश्च देहभूमाल्पताक्रमः ।
तीव्रमन्दे मध्यमन्दे मन्दमन्दे बुभुक्षुता ॥ 245
13.m: The combination of greater or lesser enjoyment, and the sequence of more or fewer bodies. / In the intense-slow, medium-slow, and slow-slow, the desire for enjoyment // 245

13.s:
kramānmukhyātimātreṇa vidhinaityantataḥ śivam /
anye yiyāsurityādigranthaṃ prāggranthasaṃgatam // 246
13.d:
क्रमान्मुख्यातिमात्रेण विधिनैत्यन्ततः शिवम् ।
अन्ये यियासुरित्यादिग्रन्थं प्राग्ग्रन्थसंगतम् ॥ 246
13.m: Gradually leads to Śiva through predominantly transcendent means in the end. / Others connect the passage beginning with 'wishing to go' with the previous text, // 246

13.s:
kurvanti madhyatīvrākhyaśaktisaṃpātagocaram /
yadā pratibhayāviṣṭo'pyeṣa saṃvādayojanām // 247
13.d:
कुर्वन्ति मध्यतीव्राख्यशक्तिसंपातगोचरम् ।
यदा प्रतिभयाविष्टोऽप्येष संवादयोजनाम् ॥ 247
13.m: Making it pertain to the descent of power called medium-intense: / when, even though possessed by intuitive flash, he, desiring to achieve harmony, // 247

13.s:
icchanyiyāsurbhavati tadā nīyeta sadgurum /
na sarvaḥ pratibhāviṣṭaḥ śaktyā nīyeta sadgurum // 248
13.d:
इच्छन्यियासुर्भवति तदा नीयेत सद्गुरुम् ।
न सर्वः प्रतिभाविष्टः शक्त्या नीयेत सद्गुरुम् ॥ 248
13.m: Wishes to go, he is then led to a true guru. / Not everyone possessed by intuitive flash is led to a true guru by power; // 248

13.s:
iti brūte yiyāsutvaṃ vaktavyaṃ nānyathā dhruvam /
rudraśaktisamāviṣṭo nīyate sadguruṃ prati // 249
13.d:
इति ब्रूते यियासुत्वं वक्तव्यं नान्यथा ध्रुवम् ।
रुद्रशक्तिसमाविष्टो नीयते सद्गुरुं प्रति ॥ 249
13.m: So one says: the desire to go must certainly be stated otherwise. / One possessed by the power of Rudra is led to a true guru; // 249

13.s:
tena prāptavivekotthajñānasaṃpūrṇamānasaḥ /
dārḍhyasaṃvādarūḍhyāderyiyāsurbhavati sphuṭam // 250
13.d:
तेन प्राप्तविवेकोत्थज्ञानसंपूर्णमानसः ।
दार्ढ्यसंवादरूढ्यादेर्यियासुर्भवति स्फुटम् ॥ 250
13.m: By that, with a mind filled with knowledge arisen from attained discrimination, / he clearly becomes one wishing to go, for the sake of confirmation, harmony, and firm establishment. // 250

13.s:
uktaṃ nandiśikhātantre prācyaṣaṭke maheśinā /
abhilāṣaḥ śive deve paśūnāṃ bhavate tadā // 251
13.d:
उक्तं नन्दिशिखातन्त्रे प्राच्यषट्के महेशिना ।
अभिलाषः शिवे देवे पशूनां भवते तदा ॥ 251
13.m: It is said by the Great Lord in the early hexad of the Nandiśikhātantra: / 'Desire for Lord Śiva arises in bound souls then, // 251

13.s:
yadā śaivābhimānena yuktā vai paramāṇavaḥ /
tadaiva te vimuktāstu dīkṣitā guruṇā yataḥ // 252
13.d:
यदा शैवाभिमानेन युक्ता वै परमाणवः ।
तदैव ते विमुक्तास्तु दीक्षिता गुरुणा यतः ॥ 252
13.m: When the ultimate souls are indeed endowed with Śaiva self-identification. / At that very moment they are liberated, having been initiated by the guru, because // 252

13.s:
prāptimātrācca te siddhasādhyā iti hi gamyate /
tamārādhyeti tu grantho mandatīvraikagocaraḥ // 253
13.d:
प्राप्तिमात्राच्च ते सिद्धसाध्या इति हि गम्यते ।
तमाराध्येति तु ग्रन्थो मन्दतीव्रैकगोचरः ॥ 253
13.m: It is understood that from the mere encounter their ends are accomplished.' / But the text 'having worshipped him' pertains exclusively to the slow-intense. // 253

13.s:
navadhā śaktipāto'yaṃ śaṃbhunāthena varṇitaḥ /
idaṃ sāramiha jñeyaṃ paripūrṇacidātmanaḥ // 254
13.d:
नवधा शक्तिपातोऽयं शंभुनाथेन वर्णितः ।
इदं सारमिह ज्ञेयं परिपूर्णचिदात्मनः ॥ 254
13.m: This ninefold descent of power was described by Śambhunātha. / This essential truth should be known here: for the self of full consciousness, // 254

13.s:
prakāśaḥ paramaḥ śaktipāto'vacchedavarjitaḥ /
tathāvidho'pi bhogāṃśāvacchedenopalakṣitaḥ // 255
13.d:
प्रकाशः परमः शक्तिपातोऽवच्छेदवर्जितः ।
तथाविधोऽपि भोगांशावच्छेदेनोपलक्षितः ॥ 255
13.m: Luminosity is the supreme descent of power, free from limitation. / Even though of that nature, when characterized by the limitation of a portion of enjoyment, // 255

13.s:
aparaḥ śaktipāto'sau paryante śivatāpradaḥ /
ubhayatrāpi karmādermāyāntarvartino yataḥ // 256
13.d:
अपरः शक्तिपातोऽसौ पर्यन्ते शिवताप्रदः ।
उभयत्रापि कर्मादेर्मायान्तर्वर्तिनो यतः ॥ 256
13.m: This other descent of power bestows Śivahood in the end; / because in both cases, karma and the rest abide within māyā. // 256

13.s:
nāsti vyāpāra ityevaṃ nirapekṣaḥ sa sarvataḥ /
tena māyāntarāle ye rudrā ye ca tadūrdhvataḥ // 257
13.d:
नास्ति व्यापार इत्येवं निरपेक्षः स सर्वतः ।
तेन मायान्तराले ये रुद्रा ये च तदूर्ध्वतः ॥ 257
13.m: 'There is no activity': thus he is entirely independent. / Thereby, the Rudras who are within māyā and those who are above it [are transcended].

13.s:
svādhikārakṣaye taistairbhairavībhūyate haṭhāt /
ye māyayā hyanākrāntāste karmādyanapekṣiṇaḥ // 258
13.d:
स्वाधिकारक्षये तैस्तैर्भैरवीभूयते हठात् ।
ये मायया ह्यनाक्रान्तास्ते कर्माद्यनपेक्षिणः ॥ 258
13.m: Upon the exhaustion of their particular offices, they are forcibly transformed into Bhairava. / For those who are not overcome by Māyā do not depend on karma and the rest.

13.s:
śaktipātavaśādeva tāṃ tāṃ siddhimupāśritāḥ /
nanu pūjājapadhyānaśaṃkarāsevanādibhiḥ // 259
13.d:
शक्तिपातवशादेव तां तां सिद्धिमुपाश्रिताः ।
ननु पूजाजपध्यानशंकरासेवनादिभिः ॥ 259
13.m: Solely by the force of the descent of power have they resorted to this or that spiritual accomplishment. / [Objection:] Surely, through worship, recitation, meditation, service to Śaṅkara, and the like,

13.s:
te mantrāditvamāpannāḥ kathaṃ karmānapekṣiṇaḥ /
maivaṃ tathāvidhottīrṇaśivadhyānajapādiṣu // 260
13.d:
ते मन्त्रादित्वमापन्नाः कथं कर्मानपेक्षिणः ।
मैवं तथाविधोत्तीर्णशिवध्यानजपादिषु ॥ 260
13.m: they attain the state of mantras and so on—how then do they not depend on karma? / [Reply:] Not so! Whence comes in the first place the very engagement of these [beings]

13.s:
pravṛttireva prathamameṣāṃ kasmādvivicyatām /
karmatatsāmyavairāgyamalapākādi dūṣitam // 261
13.d:
प्रवृत्तिरेव प्रथममेषां कस्माद्विविच्यताम् ।
कर्मतत्साम्यवैराग्यमलपाकादि दूषितम् ॥ 261
13.m: in meditation, recitation, and so on directed toward such a transcendent Śiva? Let this be examined! / [The theories of] karma, the balance of karmas, dispassion, the ripening of impurity, and the like have [already] been refuted.

13.s:
īśvarecchā nimittaṃ cecchaktipātaikahetutā /
japādikā kriyāśaktirevetthaṃ natu karma tat // 262
13.d:
ईश्वरेच्छा निमित्तं चेच्छक्तिपातैकहेतुता ।
जपादिका क्रियाशक्तिरेवेत्थं नतु कर्म तत् ॥ 262
13.m: If the will of the Lord is the cause, then the descent of power is the sole cause. / Recitation and the like are in this way nothing other than the power of action, not karma.

13.s:
karma tallokarūḍhaṃ hi yadbhogamavaraṃ dadat /
tirodhatte bhoktṛrūpaṃ saṃjñāyā tu na no bharaḥ // 263
13.d:
कर्म तल्लोकरूढं हि यद्भोगमवरं ददत् ।
तिरोधत्ते भोक्तृरूपं संज्ञाया तु न नो भरः ॥ 263
13.m: For that is conventionally called 'karma' in worldly usage which, bestowing inferior enjoyment, / conceals the nature of the experiencer. But we do not insist on a mere name.

13.s:
teṣāṃ bhogotkatā kasmāditi ceddattamuttaram /
citrākāraprakāśo'yaṃ svatantraḥ parameśvaraḥ // 264
13.d:
तेषां भोगोत्कता कस्मादिति चेद्दत्तमुत्तरम् ।
चित्राकारप्रकाशोऽयं स्वतन्त्रः परमेश्वरः ॥ 264
13.m: If it is asked, 'Why is there among them an intensity of enjoyment?', the answer has [already] been given: / this supreme Lord is independent, manifesting in manifold forms.

13.s:
svātantryāttu tirobhāvabandho bhoge'sya bhoktṛtām /
puṣṇansvaṃ rūpameva syānmalakarmādivarjitam // 265
13.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यात्तु तिरोभावबन्धो भोगेऽस्य भोक्तृताम् ।
पुष्णन्स्वं रूपमेव स्यान्मलकर्मादिवर्जितम् ॥ 265
13.m: Out of absolute autonomy, however, the bond of concealment, nourishing his state of being an experiencer in enjoyment, / becomes his very own nature, devoid of impurity, karma, and the rest.

13.s:
uktaṃ seyaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ śivasya paśuvartinī /
bandhayitrīti tatkarma kathyate rūpalopakṛt // 266
13.d:
उक्तं सेयं क्रियाशक्तिः शिवस्य पशुवर्तिनी ।
बन्धयित्रीति तत्कर्म कथ्यते रूपलोपकृत् ॥ 266
13.m: It has been said: this very power of action of Śiva, abiding in the bound soul, / is the binder; therefore it is called karma, causing the loss of [one's true] form.

13.s:
jñātā sā ca kriyāśaktiḥ sadyaḥ siddhyupapādikā /
avicchinnasvātmasaṃvitprathā siddhirihocyate // 267
13.d:
ज्ञाता सा च क्रियाशक्तिः सद्यः सिद्ध्युपपादिका ।
अविच्छिन्नस्वात्मसंवित्प्रथा सिद्धिरिहोच्यते ॥ 267
13.m: And when that power of action is known, it instantly brings about spiritual accomplishment. / Here, spiritual accomplishment is said to be the uninterrupted expansion of the consciousness of one's own self.

13.s:
sā bhogamokṣasvātantryamahālakṣmīrihākṣayā /
viṣṇvādirūpatā deve yā kācitsā nijātmanā // 268
13.d:
सा भोगमोक्षस्वातन्त्र्यमहालक्ष्मीरिहाक्षया ।
विष्ण्वादिरूपता देवे या काचित्सा निजात्मना ॥ 268
13.m: It is the imperishable Great Fortune of the absolute autonomy of enjoyment and liberation. / Whatever state of being Viṣṇu and others there is in the Lord, by its very nature,

13.s:
bhedayogavaśānmāyāpadamadhyavyavasthitā /
tena tadrūpatāyogācchaktipātaḥ sthito'pi san // 269
13.d:
भेदयोगवशान्मायापदमध्यव्यवस्थिता ।
तेन तद्रूपतायोगाच्छक्तिपातः स्थितोऽपि सन् ॥ 269
13.m: due to the presence of differentiation, is situated in the midst of the plane of Māyā. / Therefore, because of association with that form, even though the descent of power is present,

13.s:
tāvantaṃ bhogamādhatte paryante śivatāṃ natu /
yathā svātantryato rājāpyanugṛhṇāti kaṃcana // 270
13.d:
तावन्तं भोगमाधत्ते पर्यन्ते शिवतां नतु ।
यथा स्वातन्त्र्यतो राजाप्यनुगृह्णाति कंचन ॥ 270
13.m: it confers only that much enjoyment, but not the state of Śiva at the end. / Just as a king, out of absolute autonomy, bestows grace upon someone,

13.s:
īśaśaktisamāveśāttathā viṣṇvādayo'pyalam /
māyāgarbhādhikārīyaśaktipātavaśāttataḥ // 271
13.d:
ईशशक्तिसमावेशात्तथा विष्ण्वादयोऽप्यलम् ।
मायागर्भाधिकारीयशक्तिपातवशात्ततः ॥ 271
13.m: so also Viṣṇu and the others are empowered by the penetration of the Lord's power. / Consequently, by the power of the descent of power pertaining to the office-holders within the womb of Māyā,

13.s:
ko'pi pradhānapuruṣavivekī prakṛtergataḥ /
utkṛṣṭāttata evāśu ko'pi buddhā vivekitām // 272
13.d:
कोऽपि प्रधानपुरुषविवेकी प्रकृतेर्गतः ।
उत्कृष्टात्तत एवाशु कोऽपि बुद्धा विवेकिताम् ॥ 272
13.m: someone who discriminates between Pradhāna and the Puruṣa moves beyond Prakṛti; / from that exalted [state], someone, swiftly having realized discrimination through the intellect,

13.s:
kṣaṇātpuṃsaḥ kalāyāśca puṃmāyāntaravedakaḥ /
kalāśrayasyāpyatyantaṃ karmaṇo vinivartanāt // 273
13.d:
क्षणात्पुंसः कलायाश्च पुंमायान्तरवेदकः ।
कलाश्रयस्याप्यत्यन्तं कर्मणो विनिवर्तनात् ॥ 273
13.m: discerns instantly the distinction between the Puruṣa and Kalā, and between the Puruṣa and Māyā, / because of the complete cessation of karma, even that supported by Kalā.

13.s:
jñānākalaḥ prāktanastu karmī tasyāśrayasthiteḥ /
sa paraṃ prakṛterbudhne sṛṣṭiṃ nāyāti jātucit // 274
13.d:
ज्ञानाकलः प्राक्तनस्तु कर्मी तस्याश्रयस्थितेः ।
स परं प्रकृतेर्बुध्ने सृष्टिं नायाति जातुचित् ॥ 274
13.m: He is a knower free of instruments; but the former [discriminator] is bound by karma, because of abiding in its locus. / He, however, never enters creation at the base of Prakṛti.

13.s:
māyādhare tu sṛjyetānanteśena pracodanāt /
vijñānākalatāṃ prāptaḥ kevalādadhikārataḥ // 275
13.d:
मायाधरे तु सृज्येतानन्तेशेन प्रचोदनात् ।
विज्ञानाकलतां प्राप्तः केवलादधिकारतः ॥ 275
13.m: Under the realm of Māyā, however, he may be emanated by the impulsion of the Lord Ananta. / One who has attained the status of a knower free of instruments, from the office of mere

13.s:
malānmantratadīśādibhāvameti sadā śivāt /
patyuḥ parasmādyastveṣa śaktipātaḥ sa vai malāt // 276
13.d:
मलान्मन्त्रतदीशादिभावमेति सदा शिवात् ।
पत्युः परस्माद्यस्त्वेष शक्तिपातः स वै मलात् ॥ 276
13.m: impurity, attains the state of mantra, lord of mantra, and so forth, from Sadāśiva. / But that descent of power which comes from the supreme Lord, the Master, truly

13.s:
ajñānākhyādviyokteti śivabhāvaprakāśakaḥ /
nānyena śivabhāvo hi kenacitsaṃprakāśate // 277
13.d:
अज्ञानाख्याद्वियोक्तेति शिवभावप्रकाशकः ।
नान्येन शिवभावो हि केनचित्संप्रकाशते ॥ 277
13.m: disjoins from the impurity called ignorance, and manifests the state of Śiva. / For the state of Śiva is not revealed by any other means.

13.s:
svacchandaśāstre tenoktaṃ vādināṃ tu śatatrayam /
triṣaṣṭyabhyadhikaṃ bhrāntaṃ vaiṣṇavādyaṃ niśāntare // 278
13.d:
स्वच्छन्दशास्त्रे तेनोक्तं वादिनां तु शतत्रयम् ।
त्रिषष्ट्यभ्यधिकं भ्रान्तं वैष्णवाद्यं निशान्तरे ॥ 278
13.m: Therefore it is said in the Svacchanda Tantra that the three hundred and sixty-three / disputants—the Vaiṣṇavas and the rest—are deluded in different systems.

13.s:
śivajñānaṃ kevalaṃ ca śivatāpattidāyakam /
śivatāpattiparyantaḥ śaktipātaśca carcyate // 279
13.d:
शिवज्ञानं केवलं च शिवतापत्तिदायकम् ।
शिवतापत्तिपर्यन्तः शक्तिपातश्च चर्च्यते ॥ 279
13.m: And the knowledge of Śiva alone is the giver of the attainment of Śivahood; / and the descent of power culminating in the attainment of Śivahood is [now] being examined.

13.s:
anyathā kiṃ hi tatsyādyacchaivyā śaktyānadhiṣṭhitam /
teneha vaiṣṇavādīnāṃ nādhikāraḥ kathaṃcana // 280
13.d:
अन्यथा किं हि तत्स्याद्यच्छैव्या शक्त्यानधिष्ठितम् ।
तेनेह वैष्णवादीनां नाधिकारः कथंचन ॥ 280
13.m: Otherwise, what indeed could exist that is not presided over by the power of Śiva? / Therefore, Vaiṣṇavas and the rest have no qualification whatsoever here.

13.s:
te hi bhedaikavṛttitvādabhede dūravarjitāḥ /
svātantryāttu maheśasya te'pi cecchivatonmukhāḥ // 281
13.d:
ते हि भेदैकवृत्तित्वादभेदे दूरवर्जिताः ।
स्वातन्त्र्यात्तु महेशस्य तेऽपि चेच्छिवतोन्मुखाः ॥ 281
13.m: For they, functioning solely in difference, are far removed from non-duality. / But out of the absolute autonomy of the Great Lord, if even they become turned toward Śiva,

13.s:
dviguṇā saṃskriyāstyeṣāṃ liṅgoddhṛtyātha dīkṣayā /
duṣṭādhivāsavigame puṣpaiḥ kumbho'dhivāsyate // 282
13.d:
द्विगुणा संस्क्रियास्त्येषां लिङ्गोद्धृत्याथ दीक्षया ।
दुष्टाधिवासविगमे पुष्पैः कुम्भोऽधिवास्यते ॥ 282
13.m: their purificatory rite is twofold: by the extraction of the insignia, and then by initiation. / When a bad odor is removed, a jar is perfumed with flowers:

13.s:
dviguṇo'sya sa saṃskāro netthaṃ śuddhe ghaṭe vidhiḥ /
itthaṃ śrīśaktipāto'yaṃ nirapekṣa ihoditaḥ // 283
13.d:
द्विगुणोऽस्य स संस्कारो नेत्थं शुद्धे घटे विधिः ।
इत्थं श्रीशक्तिपातोऽयं निरपेक्ष इहोदितः ॥ 283
13.m: its purification is twofold; such a rule does not apply to a clean vessel. / Thus this noble descent of power is here declared to be independent.

13.s:
anayaiva diśā neyaṃ mataṅgakiraṇādikam /
granthagauravabhītyā tu tallikhitvā na yojitam // 284
13.d:
अनयैव दिशा नेयं मतङ्गकिरणादिकम् ।
ग्रन्थगौरवभीत्या तु तल्लिखित्वा न योजितम् ॥ 284
13.m: Along this very line should texts such as the Mataṅga and the Kiraṇa be interpreted; / but out of fear of swelling the book, they are not cited and applied here.

13.s:
purāṇe'pi ca tasyaiva prasādādbhaktiriṣyate /
yayā yānti parāṃ siddhiṃ tadbhāvagatamānasāḥ // 285
13.d:
पुराणेऽपि च तस्यैव प्रसादाद्भक्तिरिष्यते ।
यया यान्ति परां सिद्धिं तद्भावगतमानसाः ॥ 285
13.m: And even in the Purāṇa, devotion is accepted [as arising] from His grace alone, / by which those whose minds have entered His nature attain supreme spiritual accomplishment.

13.s:
