evakāreṇa karmādisāpekṣatvaṃ niṣidhyate /
prasādo nirmalībhāvastena saṃpūrṇarūpatā // 286
13.d:
एवकारेण कर्मादिसापेक्षत्वं निषिध्यते ।
प्रसादो निर्मलीभावस्तेन संपूर्णरूपता ॥ 286
13.m: By the word 'alone' (eva), dependence on karma and the rest is negated. / Grace is purification; thereby complete fullness of nature [is attained].

13.s:
ātmanā tena hi śivaḥ svayaṃ pūrṇaḥ prakāśate /
śivībhāvamahāsiddhisparśavandhye tu kutracit // 287
13.d:
आत्मना तेन हि शिवः स्वयं पूर्णः प्रकाशते ।
शिवीभावमहासिद्धिस्पर्शवन्ध्ये तु कुत्रचित् ॥ 287
13.m: For by that self, Śiva Himself shines forth as full. / But where [devotion] is devoid of the touch of the great spiritual accomplishment of becoming Śiva,

13.s:
vaiṣṇavādau hi yā bhaktirnāsau kevalataḥ śivāt /
śivo bhavati tatraiṣa kāraṇaṃ na tu kevalaḥ // 288
13.d:
वैष्णवादौ हि या भक्तिर्नासौ केवलतः शिवात् ।
शिवो भवति तत्रैष कारणं न तु केवलः ॥ 288
13.m: namely, the devotion found among Vaiṣṇavas and others, it does not come from Śiva alone. / Śiva is indeed a cause there, but not the sole cause,

13.s:
nirmalaścāpi tu prāptāvacchitkarmādyapekṣakaḥ /
yayā yānti parāṃ siddhimityasyedaṃ tu jīvitam // 289
13.d:
निर्मलश्चापि तु प्राप्तावच्छित्कर्माद्यपेक्षकः ।
यया यान्ति परां सिद्धिमित्यस्येदं तु जीवितम् ॥ 289
13.m: and not pure, but rather dependent on karma and the rest limited to what has been attained. / This indeed is the core meaning of [the verse ending], 'by which they attain supreme spiritual accomplishment.'

13.s:
śrīmānutpaladevaścāpyasmākaṃ paramo guruḥ /
śaktipātasamaye vicāraṇaṃ prāptamīśa na karoṣi karhicit // 290
13.d:
श्रीमानुत्पलदेवश्चाप्यस्माकं परमो गुरुः ।
शक्तिपातसमये विचारणं प्राप्तमीश न करोषि कर्हिचित् ॥ 290
13.m: And the illustrious Utpaladeva, our supreme guru, [said]: / 'At the time of the descent of power, O Lord, You never make any deliberation that has been occasioned [by conditions].

13.s:
adya māṃ prati kimāgataṃ yataḥ svaprakāśanavidhau vilambase /
karhicitprāptaśabdābhyāmanapekṣitvamūcivān // 291
13.d:
अद्य मां प्रति किमागतं यतः स्वप्रकाशनविधौ विलम्बसे ।
कर्हिचित्प्राप्तशब्दाभ्यामनपेक्षित्वमूचिवान् ॥ 291
13.m: What has happened toward me today, that You delay in the act of revealing Yourself?' / By the two words 'never' (karhicit) and 'occasioned' (prāpta), he stated independence,

13.s:
durlabhatvamarāgitvaṃ śaktipātavidhau vibhoḥ /
aparārdhena tasyaiva śaktipātasya citratām // 292
13.d:
दुर्लभत्वमरागित्वं शक्तिपातविधौ विभोः ।
अपरार्धेन तस्यैव शक्तिपातस्य चित्रताम् ॥ 292
13.m: the rarity, and the impartiality of the All-pervading Lord in the act of the descent of power; / and by the second half [of the verse], the variegated nature of that very descent of power,

13.s:
vyavadhānacirakṣiprabhedādyairupavarṇitaiḥ /
śrīmatāpyaniruddhena śaktimunmīlinīṃ vibhoḥ // 293
13.d:
व्यवधानचिरक्षिप्रभेदाद्यैरुपवर्णितैः ।
श्रीमताप्यनिरुद्धेन शक्तिमुन्मीलिनीं विभोः ॥ 293
13.m: described through differences of intervention, delay, swiftness, and so forth. / Even by the illustrious Aniruddha, explaining the unfolding power of the All-pervading Lord

13.s:
vyācakṣāṇena mātaṅge varṇitā nirapekṣatā /
sthāvarānte'pi devasya svarūponmīlanātmikā // 294
13.d:
व्याचक्षाणेन मातङ्गे वर्णिता निरपेक्षता ।
स्थावरान्तेऽपि देवस्य स्वरूपोन्मीलनात्मिका ॥ 294
13.m: in the Mataṅga, this independence was described: / reaching even to immovable beings, the Lord's power, consisting in the unfolding of His own nature,

13.s:
śaktiḥ patantī sāpekṣā na kvāpīti suvistarāt /
evaṃ vicitre'pyetasmiñchaktipāte sthite sati // 295
13.d:
शक्तिः पतन्ती सापेक्षा न क्वापीति सुविस्तरात् ।
एवं विचित्रेऽप्येतस्मिञ्छक्तिपाते स्थिते सति ॥ 295
13.m: falls without depending on anything anywhere, as [stated] at great length. / Thus, though this descent of power is manifold,

13.s:
tāratamyādibhirbhedaiḥ samayyādivicitratā /
kaścidrudrāśatāmātrāpādanāttatprasādataḥ // 296
13.d:
तारतम्यादिभिर्भेदैः समय्यादिविचित्रता ।
कश्चिद्रुद्राशतामात्रापादनात्तत्प्रसादतः ॥ 296
13.m: there is diversity among initiates into the rule and the rest through gradations and other distinctions. / One, through being brought merely to the state of a Rudra, by his grace

13.s:
śivatvaṃ kramaśo gacchet samayī yo nirūpyate /
kaścicchuddhādhvabandhaḥ san putrakaḥ śīghramakramāt // 297
13.d:
शिवत्वं क्रमशो गच्छेत् समयी यो निरूप्यते ।
कश्चिच्छुद्धाध्वबन्धः सन् पुत्रकः शीघ्रमक्रमात् ॥ 297
13.m: may gradually attain Śivahood; he is defined as an initiate into the rule. / Another, being bound to the pure path, is a spiritual son swiftly without succession.

13.s:
bhogavyavadhinā ko'pi sādhakaściraśīghrataḥ /
kaścitsaṃpūrṇakartavyaḥ kṛtyapañcakabhāgini // 298
13.d:
भोगव्यवधिना कोऽपि साधकश्चिरशीघ्रतः ।
कश्चित्संपूर्णकर्तव्यः कृत्यपञ्चकभागिनि ॥ 298
13.m: Another, an adept, through the intervention of enjoyment, [attains it] either slowly or swiftly. / Another, who has completed all duties, participating in the fivefold activity,

13.s:
rūpe sthito guruḥ so'pi bhogamokṣādibhedabhāk /
samayyādicatuṣkasya samāsavyāsayogataḥ // 299
13.d:
रूपे स्थितो गुरुः सोऽपि भोगमोक्षादिभेदभाक् ।
समय्यादिचतुष्कस्य समासव्यासयोगतः ॥ 299
13.m: abiding in that form, is a guru; he too shares in the distinctions of enjoyment, liberation, and so forth. / Through the combination of brief and detailed forms of this tetrad of initiate into the rule and the rest,

13.s:
kramākramādibhirbhedaiḥ śaktipātasya citratā /
kramikaḥ śaktipātaśca siddhānte vāmake tataḥ // 300
13.d:
क्रमाक्रमादिभिर्भेदैः शक्तिपातस्य चित्रता ।
क्रमिकः शक्तिपातश्च सिद्धान्ते वामके ततः ॥ 300
13.m: and through distinctions of succession, non-succession, and so on, there is diversity in the descent of power. / The descent of power is successive in the Siddhānta, and then in the Vāma,

13.s:
dakṣe mate kule kaule ṣaḍardhe hṛdaye tataḥ /
ullaṅghanavaśādvāpi jhaṭityakramameva vā // 301
13.d:
दक्षे मते कुले कौले षडर्धे हृदये ततः ।
उल्लङ्घनवशाद्वापि झटित्यक्रममेव वा ॥ 301
13.m: then in the Dakṣiṇa, the Mata, the Kula, the Kaula, the Trika, and the Hṛdaya; / or else, by virtue of transcendence, it occurs instantly and without succession.

13.s:
uktaṃ śrībhairavakule pañcadīkṣāsusaṃskṛtaḥ /
gururullaṅghitādhaḥsthasrotā vai trikaśāstragaḥ // 302
13.d:
उक्तं श्रीभैरवकुले पञ्चदीक्षासुसंस्कृतः ।
गुरुरुल्लङ्घिताधःस्थस्रोता वै त्रिकशास्त्रगः ॥ 302
13.m: It is stated in the Śrībhairavakula: 'Purified by the five initiations, / a guru who has transcended the lower streams is truly grounded in the Trika scriptures.'

13.s:
jñānācārādibhedena hyuttarādharatā vibhuḥ /
śāstreṣvadīdṛśacchrīmatsarvācārahṛdādiṣu // 303
13.d:
ज्ञानाचारादिभेदेन ह्युत्तराधरता विभुः ।
शास्त्रेष्वदीदृशच्छ्रीमत्सर्वाचारहृदादिषु ॥ 303
13.m: Through differences of knowledge, conduct, and the like, the All-pervading Lord has shown / a hierarchy of higher and lower in scriptures such as the noble Sarvācārahṛdaya.

13.s:
vāmamārgābhiṣiktastu daiśikaḥ paratattvavit /
tathāpi bhairave tantre punaḥ saṃskāramarhati // 304
13.d:
वाममार्गाभिषिक्तस्तु दैशिकः परतत्त्ववित् ।
तथापि भैरवे तन्त्रे पुनः संस्कारमर्हति ॥ 304
13.m: Even a preceptor consecrated in the path of Vāma, knowing the supreme reality, / nevertheless requires a further consecration in the Bhairava Tantra.

13.s:
śaivavaimalasiddhāntā ārhatāḥ kārukāśca ye /
sarve te paśavo jñeyā bhairave mātṛmaṇḍale // 305
13.d:
शैववैमलसिद्धान्ता आर्हताः कारुकाश्च ये ।
सर्वे ते पशवो ज्ञेया भैरवे मातृमण्डले ॥ 305
13.m: Those of the Śaiva Siddhānta, the Vaimalas, the Jainas, and the Kārukas— / all of them are to be known as bound souls in the Bhairava circle of mothers.

13.s:
kulakālīvidhau coktaṃ vaiṣṇavānā viśeṣataḥ /
bhasmaniṣṭhāprapannānāmityādau naiva yogyatā // 306
13.d:
कुलकालीविधौ चोक्तं वैष्णवाना विशेषतः ।
भस्मनिष्ठाप्रपन्नानामित्यादौ नैव योग्यता ॥ 306
13.m: And in the Kulakālīvidhi it is stated: 'Especially for Vaiṣṇavas, / for those devoted to ashes, and so forth, there is no qualification whatsoever.'

13.s:
svacchandaśāstre saṃkṣepāduktaṃ ca śrīmaheśinā /
anyaśāstrarato yastu nāsau siddhiphalapradaḥ // 307
13.d:
स्वच्छन्दशास्त्रे संक्षेपादुक्तं च श्रीमहेशिना ।
अन्यशास्त्ररतो यस्तु नासौ सिद्धिफलप्रदः ॥ 307
13.m: In the Svacchandaśāstra, too, it has been stated concisely by the venerable supreme Lord: / 'One who is attached to another scripture does not grant the fruit of spiritual accomplishment.'

13.s:
samayyādikramāllabdhābhiṣeko hi gururmataḥ /
sa ca śaktivaśāditthaṃ vaiṣṇavādiṣu ko'nvayaḥ // 308
13.d:
समय्यादिक्रमाल्लब्धाभिषेको हि गुरुर्मतः ।
स च शक्तिवशादित्थं वैष्णवादिषु कोऽन्वयः ॥ 308
13.m: For a guru is regarded as one who has attained consecration through the order of the initiate into the rule and the rest; / and that occurs by virtue of [divine] power. What connection, then, is there in Vaiṣṇavas and the like?

13.s:
chadmāpaśravaṇādyaistu tajjñānaṃ gṛhṇato bhavet /
prāyaścittamatastādṛgadhikāryatra kiṃ bhavet // 309
13.d:
छद्मापश्रवणाद्यैस्तु तज्ज्ञानं गृह्णतो भवेत् ।
प्रायश्चित्तमतस्तादृगधिकार्यत्र किं भवेत् ॥ 309
13.m: For those who receive that knowledge through deceit, eavesdropping, and the like, / expiation is prescribed. How then could such a person become an authority here?

13.s:
phalākāṅkṣāyutaḥ śiṣyastadekāyattasiddhikaḥ /
dhruvaṃ pacyeta narake prāyaścittyupasevanāt // 310
13.d:
फलाकाङ्क्षायुतः शिष्यस्तदेकायत्तसिद्धिकः ।
ध्रुवं पच्येत नरके प्रायश्चित्त्युपसेवनात् ॥ 310
13.m: A disciple seeking results whose spiritual accomplishments depend solely upon him / would surely burn in hell on account of serving one who requires expiation.

13.s:
tirobhāvaprakāro'yaṃ yattādṛśi niyojitaḥ /
gurau śivena tadbhaktiḥ śaktipāto'sya nocyate // 311
13.d:
तिरोभावप्रकारोऽयं यत्तादृशि नियोजितः ।
गुरौ शिवेन तद्भक्तिः शक्तिपातोऽस्य नोच्यते ॥ 311
13.m: This is a mode of concealment: that he is directed by Śiva / to such a guru. Devotion to him is not called the descent of power upon him.

13.s:
yadātu vaicitryavaśājjānīyāttasya tādṛśam /
viparītapravṛttatvaṃ jñānaṃ tasmādupāharet // 312
13.d:
यदातु वैचित्र्यवशाज्जानीयात्तस्य तादृशम् ।
विपरीतप्रवृत्तत्वं ज्ञानं तस्मादुपाहरेत् ॥ 312
13.m: When, however, by virtue of diversity [of karma], he recognizes such a perverse tendency in him, / he should take away the knowledge from him;

13.s:
taṃ ca tyajetpāpavṛttiṃ bhavettu jñānatatparaḥ /
yathā caurādgṛhītvārthaṃ taṃ nigṛhṇāti bhūpatiḥ // 313
13.d:
तं च त्यजेत्पापवृत्तिं भवेत्तु ज्ञानतत्परः ।
यथा चौराद्गृहीत्वार्थं तं निगृह्णाति भूपतिः ॥ 313
13.m: and he should abandon that sinful man and become intent upon knowledge, / just as a king, having confiscated the wealth from a thief, punishes him.

13.s:
vaiṣṇavādestathā śaivaṃ jñānamāhṛtya sanmatiḥ /
sa hi bhedaikavṛttitvaṃ śivajñāne śrute'pyalam // 314
13.d:
वैष्णवादेस्तथा शैवं ज्ञानमाहृत्य सन्मतिः ।
स हि भेदैकवृत्तित्वं शिवज्ञाने श्रुतेऽप्यलम् ॥ 314
13.m: Similarly, having gathered the Śaiva knowledge from a Vaiṣṇava or the like, a man of noble intellect [should abandon him]; / for although he has heard the Śaiva knowledge, he is entirely absorbed in dualistic conduct,

13.s:
nojjhatīti dṛḍhaṃ vāmādhiṣṭhitastatpaśūttamaḥ /
śivenaiva tirobhāvya sthāpito niyaterbalāt // 315
13.d:
नोज्झतीति दृढं वामाधिष्ठितस्तत्पशूत्तमः ।
शिवेनैव तिरोभाव्य स्थापितो नियतेर्बलात् ॥ 315
13.m: and does not firmly abandon it; being possessed by Vāmā, he is the highest of bound souls, / concealed by Śiva himself and established [there] by the force of necessity.

13.s:
kathaṅkāraṃ patipadaṃ prayātu paratantritaḥ /
svacchandaśāstre proktaṃ ca vaiṣṇavādiṣu ye ratāḥ // 316
13.d:
कथङ्कारं पतिपदं प्रयातु परतन्त्रितः ।
स्वच्छन्दशास्त्रे प्रोक्तं च वैष्णवादिषु ये रताः ॥ 316
13.m: How could one who is subservient to others attain the state of the Lord? / And it is stated in the Svacchandaśāstra: 'Those who are devoted to Vaiṣṇava teachings and the like,

13.s:
bhramayatyeva tānmāyā hyamokṣe mokṣalipsayā /
vaiṣṇavādiḥ śaivaśāstraṃ melayannijaśāsane // 317
13.d:
भ्रमयत्येव तान्माया ह्यमोक्षे मोक्षलिप्सया ।
वैष्णवादिः शैवशास्त्रं मेलयन्निजशासने ॥ 317
13.m: Māyā verily deludes, through their desire for liberation in that which is not liberation.' / A Vaiṣṇava or the like who mixes the Śaiva scripture into his own teaching

13.s:
dhruvaṃ saṃśayamāpanna ubhayabhraṣṭatāṃ vrajet /
svadṛṣṭau paradṛṣṭau ca samayollaṅghanādasau // 318
13.d:
ध्रुवं संशयमापन्न उभयभ्रष्टतां व्रजेत् ।
स्वदृष्टौ परदृष्टौ च समयोल्लङ्घनादसौ ॥ 318
13.m: surely falls into doubt and meets with downfall from both, / because he transgresses the pledge both in his own doctrine and in the other doctrine.

13.s:
pratyavāyaṃ yato'bhyeti carettannedṛśaṃ kramam /
uktaṃ śrīmadgahvare ca parameśena tādṛśam // 319
13.d:
प्रत्यवायं यतोऽभ्येति चरेत्तन्नेदृशं क्रमम् ।
उक्तं श्रीमद्गह्वरे च परमेशेन तादृशम् ॥ 319
13.m: Since he incurs adverse consequences, he should not follow such a path. / And similarly it has been stated by the supreme Lord in the venerable Gahvara:

13.s:
nānyaśāstrābhiyuktaṣu śivajñānaṃ prakāśate /
tanna saiddhāntiko vāme nāsau dakṣe sa no mate // 320
13.d:
नान्यशास्त्राभियुक्तषु शिवज्ञानं प्रकाशते ।
तन्न सैद्धान्तिको वामे नासौ दक्षे स नो मते ॥ 320
13.m: 'The knowledge of Śiva does not shine forth in those engaged in other scriptures.' / Therefore, one belonging to the Siddhānta has no authority in Vāma, nor he in Dakṣiṇa, nor he in Mata,

13.s:
kulakaule trike nāsau pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ paratra tu /
avacchinno'navacchedaṃ no vettyānantyasaṃsthitaḥ // 321
13.d:
कुलकौले त्रिके नासौ पूर्वः पूर्वः परत्र तु ।
अवच्छिन्नोऽनवच्छेदं नो वेत्त्यानन्त्यसंस्थितः ॥ 321
13.m: nor he in Kula, Kaula, and Trika. Each preceding one has no authority in what is subsequent; / being limited, he does not know the unlimited, [whereas] one abiding in infinity

13.s:
sarvaṃsahastato'dhaḥstha ūrdhvastho'dhikṛto guruḥ /
svātmīyādharasaṃsparśātprāṇayannadharāḥ kriyāḥ // 322
13.d:
सर्वंसहस्ततोऽधःस्थ ऊर्ध्वस्थोऽधिकृतो गुरुः ।
स्वात्मीयाधरसंस्पर्शात्प्राणयन्नधराः क्रियाः ॥ 322
13.m: bears all. Therefore, a guru situated above is authorized over what is below; / animating lower rites through the touch of what belongs to his own lower [path],

13.s:
saphalīkurute yattadūrdhvastho gururuttamaḥ /
adhaḥsthadṛkstho'pyetādṛggurusevī bhavetsa yaḥ // 323
13.d:
सफलीकुरुते यत्तदूर्ध्वस्थो गुरुरुत्तमः ।
अधःस्थदृक्स्थोऽप्येतादृग्गुरुसेवी भवेत्स यः ॥ 323
13.m: he brings them to fruition; hence a guru situated above is supreme. / Even if one is situated in a lower view, if he becomes a follower of such a guru,

13.s:
tādṛkśaktinipāteddho yo drāgūrdhvamimaṃ nayet /
tattadgirinadīprāyāvacchinne kṣetrapīṭhake // 324
13.d:
तादृक्शक्तिनिपातेद्धो यो द्रागूर्ध्वमिमं नयेत् ।
तत्तद्गिरिनदीप्रायावच्छिन्ने क्षेत्रपीठके ॥ 324
13.m: he is kindled by such a descent of power as quickly leads him higher. / In sacred fields and seats demarcated by respective mountains and rivers,

13.s:
uttarottaravijñāne nādhikāryadharo'dharaḥ /
uttarottaramācāryaṃ vidannapyadharo'dharaḥ // 325
13.d:
उत्तरोत्तरविज्ञाने नाधिकार्यधरोऽधरः ।
उत्तरोत्तरमाचार्यं विदन्नप्यधरोऽधरः ॥ 325
13.m: each lower one has no authority in each subsequent knowledge. / Even if he knows the higher master, each lower one,

13.s:
kurvannadhikriyāṃ śāstralaṅghī nigrahabhājanam /
śaktipātabalādeva jñānayogyavicitratā // 326
13.d:
कुर्वन्नधिक्रियां शास्त्रलङ्घी निग्रहभाजनम् ।
शक्तिपातबलादेव ज्ञानयोग्यविचित्रता ॥ 326
13.m: if he assumes an authority [beyond his level], transgresses the scripture and becomes an object of reprimand. / The diversity of capacity for knowledge arises solely from the strength of the descent of power.

13.s:
śrautaṃ cintāmayaṃ dvyātma bhāvanāmayameva ca /
jñānaṃ taduttaraṃ jyāyo yato mokṣaikakāraṇam // 327
13.d:
श्रौतं चिन्तामयं द्व्यात्म भावनामयमेव च ।
ज्ञानं तदुत्तरं ज्यायो यतो मोक्षैककारणम् ॥ 327
13.m: Knowledge is twofold: based on scriptures, and consisting of contemplation; / and that which consists of creative meditation is the highest, because it is the sole cause of liberation.

13.s:
tattvebhya uddhṛtiṃ kvāpi yojanaṃ sakale'kale /
kathaṃ kuryādvinā jñānaṃ bhāvanāmayamuttamam // 328
13.d:
तत्त्वेभ्य उद्धृतिं क्वापि योजनं सकलेऽकले ।
कथं कुर्याद्विना ज्ञानं भावनामयमुत्तमम् ॥ 328
13.m: How could one perform the extraction from the principles, or somewhere their integration into the composite or simple, / without the supreme knowledge that consists of creative meditation?

13.s:
yogī tu prāptatattattvasiddhirapyuttame pade /
sadāśivādye svabhyastajñānitvādeva yojakaḥ // 329
13.d:
योगी तु प्राप्ततत्तत्त्वसिद्धिरप्युत्तमे पदे ।
सदाशिवाद्ये स्वभ्यस्तज्ञानित्वादेव योजकः ॥ 329
13.m: A yogin, however, even though he has attained the spiritual accomplishments of various principles, is an integrator in the supreme state— / in the Sadāśiva level and above—only by virtue of possessing well-practiced knowledge.

13.s:
adhareṣu ca tattveṣu yā siddhiryogajāsya sā /
vimocanāyāṃ nopāyaḥ sthitāpi dhanadāravat // 330
13.d:
अधरेषु च तत्त्वेषु या सिद्धिर्योगजास्य सा ।
विमोचनायां नोपायः स्थितापि धनदारवत् ॥ 330
13.m: And whatever spiritual accomplishment born of yoga he has in the lower principles, / that, though present, is no means for liberation, like wealth and women.

13.s:
yastūtpannasamastādhvasiddhiḥ sahi sadāśivaḥ /
sākṣādeṣa kathaṃ martyānmocayedgurutāṃ vrajan // 331
13.d:
यस्तूत्पन्नसमस्ताध्वसिद्धिः सहि सदाशिवः ।
साक्षादेष कथं मर्त्यान्मोचयेद्गुरुतां व्रजन् ॥ 331
13.m: He, however, who has attained the spiritual accomplishment of the entire path is himself Sadāśiva / in visible form. How could he, having attained guruhood, fail to liberate mortals?

13.s:
tenoktaṃ mālinītantre vicārya jñānayogite /
yataśca mokṣadaḥ proktaḥ svabhyastajñānavānbudhaiḥ // 332
13.d:
तेनोक्तं मालिनीतन्त्रे विचार्य ज्ञानयोगिते ।
यतश्च मोक्षदः प्रोक्तः स्वभ्यस्तज्ञानवान्बुधैः ॥ 332
13.m: Therefore it was stated in the Mālinītantra after examining the possession of knowledge and yoga; / and because one endowed with well-practiced knowledge is declared by the wise to be the bestower of liberation,

13.s:
tasmātsvabhyastavijñānataivaikaṃ gurulakṣaṇam /
vibhāgastveṣa me proktaḥ śaṃbhunāthena darśyate // 333
13.d:
तस्मात्स्वभ्यस्तविज्ञानतैवैकं गुरुलक्षणम् ।
विभागस्त्वेष मे प्रोक्तः शंभुनाथेन दर्श्यते ॥ 333
13.m: possessing well-practiced knowledge is indeed the sole characteristic of a guru. / This classification, however, stated by me, is being shown by Śambhunātha.

13.s:
mokṣajñānaparaḥ kuryādguruṃ svabhyastavedanam /
anyaṃ tyajetprāptamapi tathācoktaṃ śivena tat // 334
13.d:
मोक्षज्ञानपरः कुर्याद्गुरुं स्वभ्यस्तवेदनम् ।
अन्यं त्यजेत्प्राप्तमपि तथाचोक्तं शिवेन तत् ॥ 334
13.m: One intent upon the knowledge of liberation should adopt a guru whose knowledge is well-practiced; / he should abandon any other, even if already attained. And so it was stated by Śiva:

13.s:
āmodārthī yathā bhṛṅgaḥ puṣpātpuṣpāntaraṃ vrajet /
vijñānārthī tathā śiṣyo gurorgurvantaraṃ vrajet // 335
13.d:
आमोदार्थी यथा भृङ्गः पुष्पात्पुष्पान्तरं व्रजेत् ।
विज्ञानार्थी तथा शिष्यो गुरोर्गुर्वन्तरं व्रजेत् ॥ 335
13.m: 'Just as a bee in search of fragrance moves from flower to flower, / so a disciple in search of knowledge should move from guru to guru.

13.s:
śaktihīnaṃ guruṃ prāpya mokṣajñāne kathaṃ śrayet /
naṣṭamūle drume devi kutaḥ puṣpaphalādikam // 336
13.d:
शक्तिहीनं गुरुं प्राप्य मोक्षज्ञाने कथं श्रयेत् ।
नष्टमूले द्रुमे देवि कुतः पुष्पफलादिकम् ॥ 336
13.m: Having found a guru devoid of power, how could one resort to him for the knowledge of liberation? / When a tree has lost its roots, O goddess, whence can come flowers, fruits, and the like?'

13.s:
uttarottaramutkarṣalakṣmīṃ paśyannapi sthitaḥ /
adhame yaḥ pade tasmātko'nyaḥ syāddaivadagdhakaḥ // 337
13.d:
उत्तरोत्तरमुत्कर्षलक्ष्मीं पश्यन्नपि स्थितः ।
अधमे यः पदे तस्मात्कोऽन्यः स्याद्दैवदग्धकः ॥ 337
13.m: Even when perceiving the splendor of successively higher excellence, whoever remains / in a lower state—who else could be more cursed by fate than he?

13.s:
yastu bhogaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca vāñchedvijñānameva ca /
svabhyastajñāninaṃ yogasiddhaṃ sa gurumāśrayet // 338
13.d:
यस्तु भोगं च मोक्षं च वाञ्छेद्विज्ञानमेव च ।
स्वभ्यस्तज्ञानिनं योगसिद्धं स गुरुमाश्रयेत् ॥ 338
13.m: He, however, who desires both enjoyment and liberation, and knowledge as well, / should take refuge in a guru who possesses well-practiced knowledge and is perfected in yoga.

13.s:
tadabhāve tu vijñānamokṣayorjñāninaṃ śrayet /
bhuktyaṃśe yoginaṃ yastatphalaṃ dātuṃ bhavetkṣamaḥ // 339
13.d:
तदभावे तु विज्ञानमोक्षयोर्ज्ञानिनं श्रयेत् ।
भुक्त्यंशे योगिनं यस्तत्फलं दातुं भवेत्क्षमः ॥ 339
13.m: In the absence of such a one, he should resort to a knower for knowledge and liberation, / and, for the part of enjoyment, to a yogin who is capable of granting that fruit.

13.s:
phaladānākṣame yoginyapāyaikopadeśini /
varaṃ jñānī yo'bhyupāyaṃ diśedapica mocayet // 340
13.d:
फलदानाक्षमे योगिन्यपायैकोपदेशिनि ।
वरं ज्ञानी योऽभ्युपायं दिशेदपिच मोचयेत् ॥ 340
13.m: When a yogin is incapable of giving the fruit and teaches only destructive practices, / better is a knower who points out the proper means and also liberates.

13.s:
jñānī na pūrṇa evaiko yadi hyaṃśāṃśikākramāt /
jñānānyādāya vijñānaṃ kurvītākhaṇḍamaṇḍalam // 341
13.d:
ज्ञानी न पूर्ण एवैको यदि ह्यंशांशिकाक्रमात् ।
ज्ञानान्यादाय विज्ञानं कुर्वीताखण्डमण्डलम् ॥ 341
13.m: If a single knower is not complete, then by receiving knowledges / through a gradual succession of portions, one should make one's knowledge an unbroken circle.

13.s:
tenāsaṃkhyāngurūnkuryātpūraṇāya svasaṃvidaḥ /
dhanyastu pūrṇavijñānaṃ jñānārthī labhate gurum // 342
13.d:
तेनासंख्यान्गुरून्कुर्यात्पूरणाय स्वसंविदः ।
धन्यस्तु पूर्णविज्ञानं ज्ञानार्थी लभते गुरुम् ॥ 342
13.m: For this reason, one should resort to countless gurus for the completion of one's consciousness; / but fortunate is the seeker of knowledge who finds a guru of complete knowledge.

13.s:
nānāgurvāgamasrotaḥpratibhāmātramiśritam /
kṛtvā jñānārṇavaṃ svābhirvipruṅgiḥ plāvayenna kim // 343
13.d:
नानागुर्वागमस्रोतःप्रतिभामात्रमिश्रितम् ।
कृत्वा ज्ञानार्णवं स्वाभिर्विप्रुङ्गिः प्लावयेन्न किम् ॥ 343
13.m: Having made an ocean of knowledge mingled only with the intuitive flash flowing from the traditions of diverse gurus, / why would one not inundate [the world] with one's own droplets?

13.s:
ā tapanānmoṭakāntaṃ yasya me'sti gurukramaḥ /
tasya me sarvaśiṣyasya nopadeśadaridratā // 344
13.d:
आ तपनान्मोटकान्तं यस्य मेऽस्ति गुरुक्रमः ।
तस्य मे सर्वशिष्यस्य नोपदेशदरिद्रता ॥ 344
13.m: 'For me, whose lineage of gurus extends from Tapana up to Moṭaka, / for me, who am a disciple of all, there is no poverty of instruction.'

13.s:
śrīmatā kallaṭenetthaṃ guruṇā tu nyarūpyata /
ahamapyata evādhaḥśāstradṛṣṭikutūhalāt // 345
13.d:
श्रीमता कल्लटेनेत्थं गुरुणा तु न्यरूप्यत ।
अहमप्यत एवाधःशास्त्रदृष्टिकुतूहलात् ॥ 345
13.m: Thus indeed it was explained by the venerable guru Kallaṭa. / For this very reason, out of curiosity about the views of lower scriptures,

13.s:
tārkikaśrautabauddhārhadvaiṣṇavādīnnaseviṣi /
lokādhyātmātimārgādikarmayogavidhānataḥ // 346
13.d:
तार्किकश्रौतबौद्धार्हद्वैष्णवादीन्नसेविषि ।
लोकाध्यात्मातिमार्गादिकर्मयोगविधानतः ॥ 346
13.m: I too served logicians, Vedāntins, Buddhists, Jainas, Vaiṣṇavas, and others, / following the injunctions of common, spiritual, and trans-path disciplines and rituals.

13.s:
saṃbodhotkarṣabāhulyātkramotkṛṣṭānvibhāvayet /
śrīpūrvaśāstre praṣṭāro munayo nāradādayaḥ // 347
13.d:
संबोधोत्कर्षबाहुल्यात्क्रमोत्कृष्टान्विभावयेत् ।
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे प्रष्टारो मुनयो नारदादयः ॥ 347
13.m: One should contemplate those who are progressively higher by the abundance of the excellence of their awakening. / In the venerable Pūrvaśāstra, the questioning sages, Nārada and the rest,

13.s:
prāgvaiṣṇavāḥ saugatāśca siddhāntādividastataḥ /
kramāttrikārthavijñānacandrotsukitadṛṣṭayaḥ // 348
13.d:
प्राग्वैष्णवाः सौगताश्च सिद्धान्तादिविदस्ततः ।
क्रमात्त्रिकार्थविज्ञानचन्द्रोत्सुकितदृष्टयः ॥ 348
13.m: were initially Vaiṣṇavas, then Buddhists, then knowers of the Siddhānta and the like, / whose vision was progressively eager for the moon of knowledge of the meaning of Trika.

13.s:
tasmānna gurubhūyastve viśaṅketa kadācana /
gurvantararate mūḍhe āgamāntarasevake // 349
13.d:
तस्मान्न गुरुभूयस्त्वे विशङ्केत कदाचन ।
गुर्वन्तररते मूढे आगमान्तरसेवके ॥ 349
13.m: Therefore, one should never doubt the multiplicity of gurus. / For a fool who takes pleasure in an inferior guru and serves another scripture,

13.s:
pratyavāyo ya āmnātaḥ sa itthamiti gṛhyatām /
yo yatra śāstre'dhikṛtaḥ sa tatra gururucyate // 350
13.d:
प्रत्यवायो य आम्नातः स इत्थमिति गृह्यताम् ।
यो यत्र शास्त्रेऽधिकृतः स तत्र गुरुरुच्यते ॥ 350
13.m: the spiritual obstacle taught [in the scriptures] should be understood in this way: / he who is authorized in a given scripture is called the guru in that system;

13.s:
tatrānadhikṛto yastu tadgurvantaramucyate /
yathā tanmaṇḍalāsīno maṇḍalāntarabhūpatim // 351
13.d:
तत्रानधिकृतो यस्तु तद्गुर्वन्तरमुच्यते ।
यथा तन्मण्डलासीनो मण्डलान्तरभूपतिम् ॥ 351
13.m: he, however, who is not authorized therein is called 'another guru.' / Just as someone dwelling in a kingdom, wishing to conquer his own realm,

13.s:
svamaṇḍalajigīṣuḥ sansevamāno vinaśyati /
tathottarottarajñānasiddhiprepsuḥ samāśrayan // 352
13.d:
स्वमण्डलजिगीषुः सन्सेवमानो विनश्यति ।
तथोत्तरोत्तरज्ञानसिद्धिप्रेप्सुः समाश्रयन् ॥ 352
13.m: perishes if he serves the king of another realm, / so one who desires spiritual accomplishment through ever-higher knowledge, if he resorts

13.s:
adharādharamācāryaṃ vināśamadhigacchati /
evamevordhvavartiṣṇorāgamātsiddhivāñchakaḥ // 353
13.d:
अधराधरमाचार्यं विनाशमधिगच्छति ।
एवमेवोर्ध्ववर्तिष्णोरागमात्सिद्धिवाञ्छकः ॥ 353
13.m: to a lower and lower master, meets destruction. / In just this way, one who desires spiritual accomplishment from a higher-ranking scripture,

13.s:
māyīyaśāstranirato vināśaṃ pratipadyate /
uktaṃ ca śrīmadānande karma saṃśritya bhāvataḥ // 354
13.d:
मायीयशास्त्रनिरतो विनाशं प्रतिपद्यते ।
उक्तं च श्रीमदानन्दे कर्म संश्रित्य भावतः ॥ 354
13.m: if devoted to a scripture belonging to Māyā, meets with destruction. / And it is stated in the venerable Ānanda[gahvara]: 'Resorting earnestly to a ritual action,

13.s:
jugupsate tattasmiṃśca viphale'nyatsamāśrayet /
dināddinaṃ hrasaṃstvevaṃ pacyate rauravādiṣu // 355
13.d:
जुगुप्सते तत्तस्मिंश्च विफलेऽन्यत्समाश्रयेत् ।
दिनाद्दिनं ह्रसंस्त्वेवं पच्यते रौरवादिषु ॥ 355
13.m: one despises that [system], and when that fails, one resorts to another. / Declining thus day by day, one is cooked in the Raurava and other hells.'

13.s:
yastūrdhvordhvapathaprepsuradharaṃ gurumāgamam /
jihāsecchaktipātena sa dhanyaḥ pronmukhīkṛtaḥ // 356
13.d:
यस्तूर्ध्वोर्ध्वपथप्रेप्सुरधरं गुरुमागमम् ।
जिहासेच्छक्तिपातेन स धन्यः प्रोन्मुखीकृतः ॥ 356
13.m: He, on the other hand, who, desiring an ever-higher path, wishes to abandon / a lower guru and scripture by virtue of a descent of power, is blessed and oriented upward.

13.s:
ata eveha śāstreṣu śaiveṣveva nirūpyate /
śāstrāntarārthānāśvastānprati saṃskārako vidhiḥ // 357
13.d:
अत एवेह शास्त्रेषु शैवेष्वेव निरूप्यते ।
शास्त्रान्तरार्थानाश्वस्तान्प्रति संस्कारको विधिः ॥ 357
13.m: For this very reason, in the Śaiva scriptures alone is set forth / a transformative ritual procedure for those who have gained trust in the doctrines of other scriptures.

13.s:
ataścāpyuttamaṃ śaivaṃ yo'nyatra patitaḥ sahi /
ihānugrāhya ūrdhvordhvaṃ netastu patitaḥ kvacit // 358
13.d:
अतश्चाप्युत्तमं शैवं योऽन्यत्र पतितः सहि ।
इहानुग्राह्य ऊर्ध्वोर्ध्वं नेतस्तु पतितः क्वचित् ॥ 358
13.m: And for this reason, Śaivism is supreme: one who has fallen elsewhere / is to be graced here, but one brought higher and higher here is never fallen anywhere.

13.s:
ata eva hi sarvajñairbrahmaviṣṇvādibhirnije /
na śāsane samāmnātaṃ liṅgoddhārādi kiṃcana // 359
13.d:
अत एव हि सर्वज्ञैर्ब्रह्मविष्ण्वादिभिर्निजे ।
न शासने समाम्नातं लिङ्गोद्धारादि किंचन ॥ 359
13.m: Indeed, for this very reason, nothing such as the extraction of the insignia / is taught by the omniscient Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and others in their own doctrine.

13.s:
itthaṃ viṣṇvādayaḥ śaivaparamārthaikavedinaḥ /
kāṃścitprati tathādikṣuste mohādvimatiṃ śritāḥ // 360
13.d:
इत्थं विष्ण्वादयः शैवपरमार्थैकवेदिनः ।
कांश्चित्प्रति तथादिक्षुस्ते मोहाद्विमतिं श्रिताः ॥ 360
13.m: Thus Viṣṇu and others, who know solely the ultimate reality of Śiva, / initiated certain individuals in that manner, having resorted to divergence out of delusion.

13.s:
tathāvidhāmeva matiṃ satyasaṃsparśanākṣamām /
dṛṣṭvaiṣāṃ brahmaviṣṇvādyairbuddhairapi tathoditam // 361
ityeṣa yuktyāgamataḥ śaktipāto vivecitaḥ /
13.d:
तथाविधामेव मतिं सत्यसंस्पर्शनाक्षमाम् ।
दृष्ट्वैषां ब्रह्मविष्ण्वाद्यैर्बुद्धैरपि तथोदितम् ॥ 361
इत्येष युक्त्यागमतः शक्तिपातो विवेचितः ।
13.m:
Seeing that their intellect was precisely of that kind, incapable of contacting the truth, / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and even the Buddhas spoke in that way.
In this way, the descent of power has been analyzed through reasoning and scripture.

14.s:
tirobhāvasvarūpaṃ tu kathyamānaṃ vivicyatām /
svabhāvāt parameśāno niyatyaniyatikramam // 1
14.d:
तिरोभावस्वरूपं तु कथ्यमानं विविच्यताम् ।
स्वभावात् परमेशानो नियत्यनियतिक्रमम् ॥ 1
14.m: Now let the essential nature of concealment, as it is being explained, be discerned: / By his nature, the Supreme Lord, [freely] touching

14.s:
spṛśanprakāśate yena tataḥ svacchanda ucyate /
niyatiṃ karmaphalayorāśrityaiṣa maheśvaraḥ // 2
14.d:
स्पृशन्प्रकाशते येन ततः स्वच्छन्द उच्यते ।
नियतिं कर्मफलयोराश्रित्यैष महेश्वरः ॥ 2
14.m: the succession of necessity and non-necessity, shines forth; therefore he is called Autonomous. / Having resorted to necessity with regard to action and its fruit, this Great Lord

14.s:
sṛṣṭisaṃsthitisaṃhārānvidhatte'vāntarasthitīn /
mahāsarge punaḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārānantyaśālini // 3
14.d:
सृष्टिसंस्थितिसंहारान्विधत्तेऽवान्तरस्थितीन् ।
महासर्गे पुनः सृष्टिसंहारानन्त्यशालिनि ॥ 3
14.m: brings about emanation, stasis, and dissolution, which are intermediate states. / In the great creation, moreover, which is endowed with an endlessness of emanation and dissolution,

14.s:
ekaḥ sa devo viśvātmā niyatityāgataḥ prabhuḥ /
avāntare yā ca sṛṣṭiḥ sthitiścātrāpyayantritam // 4
14.d:
एकः स देवो विश्वात्मा नियतित्यागतः प्रभुः ।
अवान्तरे या च सृष्टिः स्थितिश्चात्राप्ययन्त्रितम् ॥ 4
14.m: that sole god, whose self is all, is the sovereign Lord through the renunciation of necessity. / And during intermediate emanation and stasis, he remains unconstrained here,

14.s:
nojjhatyeṣa vapustyaktaniyatiśca sthito'tra tat /
niyatyaiva yadā caiṣa svarūpācchādanakramāt // 5
14.d:
नोज्झत्येष वपुस्त्यक्तनियतिश्च स्थितोऽत्र तत् ।
नियत्यैव यदा चैष स्वरूपाच्छादनक्रमात् ॥ 5
14.m: not abandoning this form, having abandoned necessity. / And when, precisely through necessity, by the process of veiling his own nature,

14.s:
bhuṅkte duḥkhavimohādi tadā karmaphalakramaḥ /
tyaktvā tu niyamaṃ kārmaṃ duḥkhamohaparītatām // 6
14.d:
भुङ्क्ते दुःखविमोहादि तदा कर्मफलक्रमः ।
त्यक्त्वा तु नियमं कार्मं दुःखमोहपरीतताम् ॥ 6
14.m: he experiences suffering, delusion, and so forth, that is the sequence of the fruit of action. / But having abandoned the rule born of action, desiring to manifest the state of being beset by suffering and delusion,

14.s:
bibhāsayiṣurāste'yaṃ tirodhāne'napekṣakaḥ /
yathā prakāśasvātantryāt pratibuddho'pyabuddhavat // 7
14.d:
बिभासयिषुरास्तेऽयं तिरोधानेऽनपेक्षकः ।
यथा प्रकाशस्वातन्त्र्यात् प्रतिबुद्धोऽप्यबुद्धवत् ॥ 7
14.m: he abides independent in concealment. / Just as, through the absolute autonomy of luminosity, an awakened person remains like an unawakened one,

14.s:
āste tadvadanuttīrṇo'pyuttīrṇa iva ceṣṭate /
yathā ca buddhastāṃ mūḍhaceṣṭāṃ kurvannapi dviṣan // 8
14.d:
आस्ते तद्वदनुत्तीर्णोऽप्युत्तीर्ण इव चेष्टते ।
यथा च बुद्धस्तां मूढचेष्टां कुर्वन्नपि द्विषन् ॥ 8
14.m: so one who has not crossed over acts as if he has crossed over. / And just as an awakened one, even while performing the behavior of a fool, hating it,

14.s:
hṛdyāste mūḍha evaṃ hi prabuddhānāṃ viceṣṭitam /
śrīvidyādhipatiścāha mānastotre tadīdṛśam // 9
14.d:
हृद्यास्ते मूढ एवं हि प्रबुद्धानां विचेष्टितम् ।
श्रीविद्याधिपतिश्चाह मानस्तोत्रे तदीदृशम् ॥ 9
14.m: remains in the heart a fool, such indeed is the behavior of the awakened. / And the venerable Vidyādhipati said thus in the Mānastotra:

14.s:
ye yauṣmāke śāsanamārge kṛtadīkṣāḥ saṃgacchanto mohavaśādvipratipattim /
nūnaṃ teṣā nāsti bhavadbhānuniyogaḥ saṅkocaḥ kiṃ sūryakaraistāmarasānām // 10
14.d:
ये यौष्माके शासनमार्गे कृतदीक्षाः संगच्छन्तो मोहवशाद्विप्रतिपत्तिम् ।
नूनं तेषा नास्ति भवद्भानुनियोगः सङ्कोचः किं सूर्यकरैस्तामरसानाम् ॥ 10
14.m: 'Those who, having received initiation in your doctrinal path, fall into error under the sway of delusion— / surely upon them there is no dispensation from your sun: does the lotus contract because of the sun's rays?

14.s:
jñātajñeyā dhātṛpadasthā api santo ye tvanmārgātkāpathagāste'pi na samyaka /
prāyasteṣāṃ laiṅgikabuddhyādisamuttho mithyābodhaḥ sarpavasādīpajakalpaḥ // 11
14.d:
ज्ञातज्ञेया धातृपदस्था अपि सन्तो ये त्वन्मार्गात्कापथगास्तेऽपि न सम्यक ।
प्रायस्तेषां लैङ्गिकबुद्ध्यादिसमुत्थो मिथ्याबोधः सर्पवसादीपजकल्पः ॥ 11
14.m: Even those who, having known what is to be known, abide in the state of the Creator, yet deviate from your path to wrong paths, do not [see] rightly; / mostly, their false awareness arising from inferential intellect and the like is like a lamp made of snake-fat.

14.s:
yasmādviddhaṃ sūtakamukhyena nu tāmraṃ tadyadbhūyaḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ no samupeyāt /
no taiḥ pītaṃ bhūtalasaṃsthairamṛtaṃ tadyeṣāṃ tṛṭkṣudduḥkhavibādhāḥ punarasmin // 12
14.d:
यस्माद्विद्धं सूतकमुख्येन नु ताम्रं तद्यद्भूयः स्वां प्रकृतिं नो समुपेयात् ।
नो तैः पीतं भूतलसंस्थैरमृतं तद्येषां तृट्क्षुद्दुःखविबाधाः पुनरस्मिन् ॥ 12
14.m: For just as copper transmuted by supreme quicksilver does not return to its original nature, / so nectar was not drunk by those dwelling on earth in whom thirst, hunger, pain, and affliction arise once more.'

14.s:
tataḥ prabuddhaceṣṭāsau mantracaryārcanādikā /
dveṣeddhāntardahatyenaṃ dāhaḥ śaṅkaiva sā yataḥ // 13
14.d:
ततः प्रबुद्धचेष्टासौ मन्त्रचर्यार्चनादिका ।
द्वेषेद्धान्तर्दहत्येनं दाहः शङ्कैव सा यतः ॥ 13
14.m: Therefore, this behavior of an awakened person—practice of mantras, worship, and the like— / burns him inwardly, inflamed by hatred, since that burning is nothing but doubt.

14.s:
na cāsya karmamahimā tādṛgyenetthamāsta saḥ /
kiṃ hi tatkarma kasmādvā pūrveṇātra samo vidhiḥ // 14
14.d:
न चास्य कर्ममहिमा तादृग्येनेत्थमास्त सः ।
किं हि तत्कर्म कस्माद्वा पूर्वेणात्र समो विधिः ॥ 14
14.m: Nor is there such majesty of his past action by which he would remain thus; / for what is that action, or whence does it arise? The rule here is the same as before.

14.s:
tasmātsā parameśecchā yayāyaṃ mohitastathā /
anantakālasaṃvedyaduḥkhapātratvamīhate // 15
14.d:
तस्मात्सा परमेशेच्छा ययायं मोहितस्तथा ।
अनन्तकालसंवेद्यदुःखपात्रत्वमीहते ॥ 15
14.m: Therefore, it is the will of the Supreme Lord by which he has been so deluded / that he desires the status of a vessel of suffering to be experienced for endless time.

14.s:
tatrāpi cecchāvaicitryādihāmutrobhayātmakaḥ /
duḥkhasyāpi vibhedo'sti ciraśaighryakṛtastathā // 16
14.d:
तत्रापि चेच्छावैचित्र्यादिहामुत्रोभयात्मकः ।
दुःखस्यापि विभेदोऽस्ति चिरशैघ्र्यकृतस्तथा ॥ 16
14.m: Even there, due to the diversity of will, there is a distinction of suffering / pertaining to this world, the next, or both, as well as caused by slowness or quickness.

14.s:
kālakāmāndhakādīnāṃ paulastyapuravāsinām /
tathānyeṣāṃ tirobhāvastāvadduḥkho hyamutra ca // 17
14.d:
कालकामान्धकादीनां पौलस्त्यपुरवासिनाम् ।
तथान्येषां तिरोभावस्तावद्दुःखो ह्यमुत्र च ॥ 17
14.m: Concealment for Kāla, Kāma, Andhaka, and others, as well as for the inhabitants of Rāvaṇa's city / and others, is suffering both here and in the hereafter.

14.s:
anyo'pi ca tirobhāvaḥ samayollaṅghanātmakaḥ /
yaduktaṃ parameśena śrīmadānandagahvare // 18
14.d:
अन्योऽपि च तिरोभावः समयोल्लङ्घनात्मकः ।
यदुक्तं परमेशेन श्रीमदानन्दगह्वरे ॥ 18
14.m: There is also another concealment consisting of the transgression of the rule, / as stated by the Supreme Lord in the venerable Ānandagahvara:

14.s:
samayollaṅghanāddevi kravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ /
tatrāpi mandatīvrādibhedādbahuvidhaḥ kramaḥ // 19
14.d:
समयोल्लङ्घनाद्देवि क्रव्यादत्वं शतं समाः ।
तत्रापि मन्दतीव्रादिभेदाद्बहुविधः क्रमः ॥ 19
14.m: 'O Goddess, from the transgression of the rule one becomes a flesh-eating demon for a hundred years.' / There too, the sequence is of many kinds according to the divisions of slow, intense, and so forth.

14.s:
svātantryācca maheśasya tirobhūto'pyasau svayam /
paradvāreṇa vābhyeti bhūyo'nugrahamapyalam // 20
14.d:
स्वातन्त्र्याच्च महेशस्य तिरोभूतोऽप्यसौ स्वयम् ।
परद्वारेण वाभ्येति भूयोऽनुग्रहमप्यलम् ॥ 20
14.m: And by the absolute autonomy of the Great Lord, even having been concealed, he himself / or through an intermediary fully attains grace once again.

14.s:
bhūyo'nugrahataḥ prāyaścittādyācaraṇe sati /
anusāreṇa dīkṣādau kṛte syācchivatāmayaḥ // 21
14.d:
भूयोऽनुग्रहतः प्रायश्चित्ताद्याचरणे सति ।
अनुसारेण दीक्षादौ कृते स्याच्छिवतामयः ॥ 21
14.m: From grace once again, when expiation and the like are performed, / and when initiation and so forth are performed accordingly, he will be composed of the state of Śiva.

14.s:
tirobhūtaḥ paretāsurapi bandhusuhṛdgurūn /
ālambya śaktipātena dīkṣādyairanugṛhyate // 22
14.d:
तिरोभूतः परेतासुरपि बन्धुसुहृद्गुरून् ।
आलम्ब्य शक्तिपातेन दीक्षाद्यैरनुगृह्यते ॥ 22
14.m: One who has been concealed, even when his breath has departed, is graced / through a descent of power by means of initiation and the like, resorting to relatives, friends, or gurus.

14.s:
tatrāpi kālaśīghratvaciratvādivibhedatām /
tathaiti śaktipāto'sau yenāyāti śivātmatām // 23
14.d:
तत्रापि कालशीघ्रत्वचिरत्वादिविभेदताम् ।
तथैति शक्तिपातोऽसौ येनायाति शिवात्मताम् ॥ 23
14.m: There too, that descent of power attains distinctions such as quickness or delay of time, / by means of which he attains the state of Śiva.

14.s:
itthaṃ sṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsatirobhāvamanugrahaḥ /
iti pañcasu kartṛtvaṃ śivatvaṃ saṃvidātmanaḥ // 24
14.d:
इत्थं सृष्टिस्थितिध्वंसतिरोभावमनुग्रहः ।
इति पञ्चसु कर्तृत्वं शिवत्वं संविदात्मनः ॥ 24
14.m: Thus, agency in the five [cosmic acts]—emanation, stasis, dissolution, concealment, / and grace—is the state of Śiva belonging to the self of consciousness.

14.s:
pañcakṛtyasvatantratvasaṃpūrṇasvātmamāninaḥ /
yogino'rcājapadhyānayogāḥ saṃsyuḥ sadoditāḥ // 25
14.d:
पञ्चकृत्यस्वतन्त्रत्वसंपूर्णस्वात्ममानिनः ।
योगिनोऽर्चाजपध्यानयोगाः संस्युः सदोदिताः ॥ 25
14.m: For a yogin who regards his own self as complete in autonomy regarding the five acts, / worship, recitation, meditation, and yoga are ever-risen.

14.s:
aindrajālikavṛttānte na rajyeta kadācana /
sādāśivo'pi yo bhogo bandhaḥ so'pyucitātmanām // 26
14.d:
ऐन्द्रजालिकवृत्तान्ते न रज्येत कदाचन ।
सादाशिवोऽपि यो भोगो बन्धः सोऽप्युचितात्मनाम् ॥ 26
14.m: He would never take pleasure in the condition of a magician; / even that enjoyment which belongs to Sadāśiva is bondage for those of worthy nature.

14.s:
jñātṛtvameva śivatā svātantryaṃ tadihocyate /
kulālavattu kartṛtvaṃ na mukhyaṃ tadadhiṣṭhiteḥ // 27
14.d:
ज्ञातृत्वमेव शिवता स्वातन्त्र्यं तदिहोच्यते ।
कुलालवत्तु कर्तृत्वं न मुख्यं तदधिष्ठितेः ॥ 27
14.m: The state of being the knower is alone the state of Śiva; that is here called absolute autonomy. / Agency like that of a potter is not primary, because it is presided over by that [knower].

14.s:
iti jñātvā grahītavyā naiva jātvapi khaṇḍanā /
śivo'haṃ cenmadicchānuvarti kiṃ na jagattviti // 28
14.d:
इति ज्ञात्वा ग्रहीतव्या नैव जात्वपि खण्डना ।
शिवोऽहं चेन्मदिच्छानुवर्ति किं न जगत्त्विति ॥ 28
14.m: Knowing thus, one must never accept the objection: / 'If I am Śiva, why does the universe not conform to my will?'

14.s:
mamecchāmanuvartantāmityatrāhaṃvidi sphuret /
śivo vā parameśāno dehādiratha nirmitaḥ // 29
14.d:
ममेच्छामनुवर्तन्तामित्यत्राहंविदि स्फुरेत् ।
शिवो वा परमेशानो देहादिरथ निर्मितः ॥ 29
14.m: When one thinks 'let [all] conform to my will,' in that consciousness of 'I' / what shines forth—Śiva, the Supreme Lord, or the body and so forth fashioned [by him]?

14.s:
śivasya tāvadastyetaddehastveṣa tathā tvayā /
kṛtaḥ kānyā dehatāsya tatkiṃ syādvācyatāpadam // 30
14.d:
शिवस्य तावदस्त्येतद्देहस्त्वेष तथा त्वया ।
कृतः कान्या देहतास्य तत्किं स्याद्वाच्यतापदम् ॥ 30
14.m: This [conformity] indeed belongs to Śiva; but this body was made in that way by you. / What other bodily nature does it have, that it should be an object of speech [as independent]?

14.s:
uktaṃ ca siddhasantānaśrīmadūrmimahākule /
pavanabhramaṇaprāṇavikṣepādikṛtaśramāḥ // 31
14.d:
उक्तं च सिद्धसन्तानश्रीमदूर्मिमहाकुले ।
पवनभ्रमणप्राणविक्षेपादिकृतश्रमाः ॥ 31
14.m: And it is said in the venerable Ūrmimahākula of the lineage of the Siddhas: / 'Those who have exerted themselves in circulating the breath, scattering the vital air, and the like,'

14.s:
kuhakādiṣu ye bhrāntāste bhrāntāḥ parame pade /
sarvatra bahumānena yāpyutkrāntirvimuktaye // 32
14.d:
कुहकादिषु ये भ्रान्तास्ते भ्रान्ताः परमे पदे ।
सर्वत्र बहुमानेन याप्युत्क्रान्तिर्विमुक्तये ॥ 32
14.m: Those who are bewildered by jugglery and the like are deluded with regard to the supreme state. / The yogic transit which, being respected everywhere, is taught for liberation

14.s:
proktā sā sāraśāstreṣu bhogopāyatayoditā /
yadi sarvagatā devo vadotkramya kva yāsyati // 33
14.d:
प्रोक्ता सा सारशास्त्रेषु भोगोपायतयोदिता ।
यदि सर्वगता देवो वदोत्क्रम्य क्व यास्यति ॥ 33
14.m: is explained in the essential scriptures as a means to enjoyment. / If the deity is omnipresent, tell [me]: having departed, where will he go?

14.s:
athāsarvagatastarhi ghaṭatulyastadā bhavet /
utkrāntividhiyogo'yamekadeśena kathyate // 34
14.d:
अथासर्वगतस्तर्हि घटतुल्यस्तदा भवेत् ।
उत्क्रान्तिविधियोगोऽयमेकदेशेन कथ्यते ॥ 34
14.m: If, on the other hand, he is not omnipresent, then he would be like a pot. / This application of the rule of yogic transit is spoken of in relation to a limited realm;

14.s:
niraṃśe śivatattve tu kathamutkrāntisaṃgatiḥ /
yathā dharādau vāyvante bhṛgvambvagnyupavāsakaiḥ // 35
14.d:
निरंशे शिवतत्त्वे तु कथमुत्क्रान्तिसंगतिः ।
यथा धरादौ वाय्वन्ते भृग्वम्ब्वग्न्युपवासकैः ॥ 35
14.m: how, however, could yogic transit apply to the partless level of Śiva? / Just as in [the elements] beginning with earth and ending with wind, through [falling from] a cliff, water, fire, or fasting,

14.s:
ātmano yojanaṃ vyomni tadvadutkrāntivartanā /
tasmānnotkramayejjīvaṃ paratattvasamīhayā // 36
14.d:
आत्मनो योजनं व्योम्नि तद्वदुत्क्रान्तिवर्तना ।
तस्मान्नोत्क्रमयेज्जीवं परतत्त्वसमीहया ॥ 36
14.m: there is the conjoining of the self to space, so operates yogic transit; / therefore, one should not cause the individual soul to depart out of a longing for the supreme reality.

14.s:
śrīpūrvaśāstre tūktaṃ yadutkrānterlakṣaṇaṃ na tat /
muktyupāyatayā kiṃtu bhogahānyai tathaiṣaṇāt // 37
14.d:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तूक्तं यदुत्क्रान्तेर्लक्षणं न तत् ।
मुक्त्युपायतया किंतु भोगहान्यै तथैषणात् ॥ 37
14.m: What is stated in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra as the definition of yogic transit, however, is not that / as a means to liberation, but rather for the abandonment of enjoyment, because such is [the practitioner's] desire:

14.s:
japadhyānādisaṃsiddhaḥ svātantryācchaktipātataḥ /
bhogaṃ prati viraktaśceditthaṃ dehaṃ tyajediti // 38
14.d:
जपध्यानादिसंसिद्धः स्वातन्त्र्याच्छक्तिपाततः ।
भोगं प्रति विरक्तश्चेदित्थं देहं त्यजेदिति ॥ 38
14.m: one who is accomplished through recitation, meditation, and so forth, out of absolute autonomy due to the descent of power, / if he has become detached from enjoyment, may thus abandon the body.

14.s:
svacchandamṛtyorapi yad bhīṣmādeḥ śrūyate kila /
bhogavairasyasaṃprāptau jīvitāntopasarpaṇam // 39
14.d:
स्वच्छन्दमृत्योरपि यद् भीष्मादेः श्रूयते किल ।
भोगवैरस्यसंप्राप्तौ जीवितान्तोपसर्पणम् ॥ 39
14.m: Indeed, even regarding those of voluntary death such as Bhīṣma, it is heard / that recourse to the end of life occurs when a distaste for enjoyment is attained.

14.s:
yogamantrāmṛtadravyavarādyaiḥ siddhibhāktanuḥ /
hātuṃ nahyanyathā śakyā vinoktakramayogataḥ // 40
14.d:
योगमन्त्रामृतद्रव्यवराद्यैः सिद्धिभाक्तनुः ।
हातुं नह्यन्यथा शक्या विनोक्तक्रमयोगतः ॥ 40
14.m: A body endowed with spiritual accomplishment through yoga, mantras, nectar, excellent substances, and so forth, / can certainly not be abandoned otherwise than by the application of the stated method.

14.s:
uktaṃ ca mālinītantre parameśena tādṛśam /
sarvamapyathavā bhogaṃ manyamāno virūpakam // 41
14.d:
उक्तं च मालिनीतन्त्रे परमेशेन तादृशम् ।
सर्वमप्यथवा भोगं मन्यमानो विरूपकम् ॥ 41
14.m: And in the Mālinītantra such was spoken by the Supreme Lord: / "Or else, considering all enjoyment to be deformed,"

14.s:
ityādi vadatā sarvairalakṣyāntaḥsatattvakam /
evaṃ sṛṣṭyādikartavyasvasvātantryopadeśanam // 42
14.d:
इत्यादि वदता सर्वैरलक्ष्यान्तःसतत्त्वकम् ।
एवं सृष्ट्यादिकर्तव्यस्वस्वातन्त्र्योपदेशनम् ॥ 42
14.m: and so forth. Saying this, whose inner reality is imperceptible to all, / [the guru gives] the instruction in one's own absolute autonomy regarding what is to be done, such as emission and the rest;

14.s:
yatsaiva mukhyadīkṣā syācchiṣyasya śivadāyinī /
uktaṃ śrīniśicāre ca bhairavīyeṇa tejasā // 43
14.d:
यत्सैव मुख्यदीक्षा स्याच्छिष्यस्य शिवदायिनी ।
उक्तं श्रीनिशिचारे च भैरवीयेण तेजसा ॥ 43
14.m: which very [instruction] is the principal initiation that bestows Śiva upon the disciple. / And it is said in the venerable Niśicāra: "By Bhairava's radiance

14.s:
vyāptaṃ viśvaṃ prapaśyanti vikalpojjhitacetasaḥ /
vikalpayuktacittastu piṇḍapātācchivaṃ vrajet // 44
14.d:
व्याप्तं विश्वं प्रपश्यन्ति विकल्पोज्झितचेतसः ।
विकल्पयुक्तचित्तस्तु पिण्डपाताच्छिवं व्रजेत् ॥ 44
14.m: those whose minds are free of conceptual constructs behold the universe as pervaded. / But one whose mind is endowed with conceptual constructs attains Śiva upon the falling of the body.

14.s:
bāhyadīkṣādiyogena caryāsamayakalpanaiḥ /
avikalpastathādyaiva jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ // 45
14.d:
बाह्यदीक्षादियोगेन चर्यासमयकल्पनैः ।
अविकल्पस्तथाद्यैव जीवन्मुक्तो न संशयः ॥ 45
14.m: Through the conjunction of external initiation and the like, by the arrangements of conduct and the rule, / one becomes non-conceptual, and thus is liberated while living this very day, without doubt."

14.s:
saṃsārajīrṇatarumūlakalāpakalpasaṃkalpasāntaratayā paramārthavahneḥ /
syurvisphuliṅgakaṇikā api cettadante dedīpyate vimalabodhahutāśarāśiḥ // 46
itthaṃ dīkṣopakramo'yaṃ darśitaḥ śāstrasaṃmataḥ /
14.d:
संसारजीर्णतरुमूलकलापकल्पसंकल्पसान्तरतया परमार्थवह्नेः ।
स्युर्विस्फुलिङ्गकणिका अपि चेत्तदन्ते देदीप्यते विमलबोधहुताशराशिः ॥ 46
इत्थं दीक्षोपक्रमोऽयं दर्शितः शास्त्रसंमतः ।
14.m:
Even if, because thoughts like the cluster of roots of the withered tree of worldly existence intervene, / there are merely sparks from the fire of ultimate reality, at the end of that shines forth a blazing heap of the fire of spotless consciousness.
Thus this introduction to initiation, conforming to the scriptures, has been shown.
